Rockstar's GTA 6 features a massive open world to explore, and people continue to make fresh discoveries, including a terrifying killer clown Easter egg. It's been discovered that the Haymarket building in Vice Beach County features an elevator filled with balloons. That's creepy, but not the worst. However, after entering the elevators, the doors close and the balloons fall to the ground. As this is happening, carnival music begins to play. The balloons then mysteriously float back up to the ceiling of the elevator, as the lights flicker and the music takes on an eerie tone. Then the lights go out and a killer clown with blood on his face and a knife in his hands charges at you as the lights go out. According to Amazon, apps launch over 35% faster than on the previous model, while the ability to draw power directly from your TV's USB port makes setup a little easier. The redesigned remote also has buttons that are easier to identify by touch, and you get support for HDR10, HDR10+, and HLG content at up to 4K and 60fps. Check out PCMag's review for a closer look at its performance and features.

It has been revealed that the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus with AI-powered Fire TV search is $29.99, down from $69.99, and is built on the second-generation Fire TV Stick 4K hardware that PCMag reviewed in 2023, now paired with AI-powered search that finds titles by actor, plot, or a remembered quote. It supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, which the 4K Select lacks, and it runs Fire OS rather than Vega OS, so sideloading still works.

According to recent reports, fire TV Cube is $89.99, down from $199.99, the largest discount in this roundup and $30 below its 2022 launch price. It's Amazon's fastest streaming device, with an octa-core processor, Wi-Fi 6E, a built-in Ethernet port, and far-field microphones for hands-free Alexa. Its HDMI input and IR blaster also let it connect to and control a cable box. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

The difference between The Witcher 3 and Witcher 4 will be 'comparable' to that of GTA 5 and GTA 6, CD Projekt boss says: 'I mean, it's been 11 years'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.
  • Industry observers note that perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • According to recent reports, "Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski mentioned when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.

Industry observers note that perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. While CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski didn't go too deep on the topic, he did say that the upcoming Witcher 4 will be comparable to GTA 6 in at least one way.

According to recent reports, "Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski mentioned when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6. "Having said that, of course, I'm not going to make a deep dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course, we did look at the game. We did see the differences.

"Do we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

It has been revealed that well, sure. As Nowakowski said, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was released 11 years ago, and it'll be two more years before The Witcher 4 comes out—assuming it's not delayed, which would make it a rarity among CD Projekt games. It will also be the same number of years between Witcher 3 and 4 as spanned GTA 5 and 6. In the world of technology, 13 years is a long time.

Hell, just the upgrade from the original Witcher 3 to the remastered version that dropped earlier this year is notable:.

At the same time, Nowakowski said that while the GTA 6 launch was tremendously successful, CD Projekt Red doesn't intend to merely mimic Rockstar's approach when The Witcher 4 is ready to go: "Our games are different and the require a certain different approach, and we just do certain things differently than they do.".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

He also said that while the release of GTA 6 has had an impact on Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 sales on consoles, he doesn't expect it to have a "material impact" on the tech giant's Q4 finances for one obvious reason.

It has been revealed that "You do have to remember that a lot of our players are also PC-based," Nowakowski remarked. "GTA has not released on PC. We have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales on engagement." And, he added, "on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero.".

Nowakowsi also said that GTA 6 hasn't changed CD Projekt's ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2: If anything, it's "an inspiration in many ways for our developers." And he's not concerned about its success pushing up development budgets, because CD Projekt's games "are not budget-driven developments.".

"I'm not saying that we don't care about the budgets. We do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well," Nowakowski said. "But you cannot make games like that having in mind, 'This is the fixed number of money I want to spend, and that's it. Otherwise, we're gone.'.

Recent findings suggest that "They are ambition-driven developments and money is important. The budgets are not indefinite. That's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is kind of like I said. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release. It has just always been like that.".

Nowakowski's positive take on GTA 6 isn't too far off that of Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who noted yesterday that he's suffering from "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression," although he quickly clarified that CD Projekt is "doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor." (And that he wasn't being serious about cancelling Cyberpunk 2.).

Recent findings suggest that seriously though i think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.

The Witcher 4 is currently slated for launch sometime in 2028, while Cyberpunk 2 isn't expected out before 2030.

  • Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida.
  • You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all. How to find the GTA 6 Super Mario Bros. Easter egg in GTA 6 You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere: Hit the bong, dude Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head. Smash the block Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi. Collect the caps Each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you. As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

Latest Update: The Naruto Movie Sounds Like It Could Be Better Than We Ever Imagined

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that fresh off making the best "Spider-Man" movie in about a decade with "Brand New Day," director Destin Daniel Cretton is plunging into the Land of Fire and ninjas, adapting Masashi Kishimoto's manga/worldwide phenomenon "Naruto" into a live-action film, two years after it was first revealed.
  • Industry observers note that deadline has reported that actor Hiroyuki Sanada ("Shogun," "John Wick: Chapter 4") is in negotiations to star in "Naruto" as Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage and leader of Naruto's ninja village, Konohagakure.
  • According to recent reports, this alone suggests "Naruto" is serious about getting impressive talent: one of the coolest actors alive in Sanada, and a major young actor in Melton, who's won acclaim for his performances in "May December" and "Beef" Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that fresh off making the best "Spider-Man" movie in about a decade with "Brand New Day," director Destin Daniel Cretton is plunging into the Land of Fire and ninjas, adapting Masashi Kishimoto's manga/worldwide phenomenon "Naruto" into a live-action film, two years after it was first revealed. Translating a battle shonen manga/anime into live-action carries negative associations of past, failed attempts. Why bother moving a story designed to stretch reality's limits to a medium that's inherently more confining than a hand-drawn one? Will "Naruto" break this curse? It has a huge stage to do so, and the early steps look promising.

Industry observers note that deadline has reported that actor Hiroyuki Sanada ("Shogun," "John Wick: Chapter 4") is in negotiations to star in "Naruto" as Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage and leader of Naruto's ninja village, Konohagakure. Sanada is the second major actor rumored to be joining "Naruto," after reports in August that Charles Melton had been approached to play Kakashi Hatake, Naruto's masked sensei.

According to recent reports, this alone suggests "Naruto" is serious about getting impressive talent: one of the coolest actors alive in Sanada, and a major young actor in Melton, who's won acclaim for his performances in "May December" and "Beef" Season 2. Not for nothing, Sanada and Melton are Japanese and Korean American, respectively — no whitewashing here, so far, contrary to "Naruto" fans' long-standing jokes about Tom Holland or Timothée Chalamet starring as Naruto.

"Naruto" has launched a "global" search/audition process for the movie's three young leads: Naruto and his teammates Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno. That suggests the film's creators are looking for young actors — possibly, even plausibly, unknowns — who can embody those characters first without prioritizing pre-existing star power.

According to recent reports, casting Hiroyuki Sanada as the Third Hokage suggests the "Naruto" team is already looking to the horizon and seeing sequels. Hiruzen is only a background part of the first "Naruto" arc, "The Land of Waves" (which is the ideal starting place for a movie series). But he takes center stage in the second and third arcs, where one of his former students, the snake-like Orochimaru, serves as the main villain. Hiruzen gets a major action sequence confronting Orochimaru, and casting Sanada — a martial artist who holds a black belt in karate, just as Charles Melton has one in taekwondo — seems like casting with that scene in mind.

If the goal is adapting the "Naruto" manga as a whole, then forward thinking will be key. The manga runs 700 chapters, divided into several story arcs; you'd likely need somewhere between seven and 10 movies to complete it. The live-action "Naruto" is being produced by studio Lionsgate in partnership with Sony. Lionsgate recently proved once more that "The Hunger Games" is a reliable hit for them with the success of "Sunrise on the Reaping." But it's never smart to put all your eggs in one basket. "Naruto" hits overlapping demographic appeal and even some similar story beats as "The Hunger Games" (like children becoming killers and the tragic horrors of war).

Sources indicate that moreover, comic books have become the prime IP of Hollywood these past two decades, and yet manga outsells American comics many times over. Manga/anime is in the cultural mainstream for anyone younger than a young millennial, and the first studio to crack that could be sitting on a cultural gold mine. So, yeah, Lionsgate has a strong incentive to get "Naruto" right, and the talent it's recruiting suggests they understand that.

Even if Destin Daniel Cretton doesn't stick around for any of those potential "Naruto" sequels (I have to imagine Sony and Marvel Studios want him back for more "Spider-Man" movies), getting him as director for the first is another sign that Lionsgate is taking this seriously. Look at what he's directed, and consider how he's intent on casting actors with genuine martial arts bona fides for "Naruto," and it's clear why he's the man for the job.

Sources indicate that an essential part of "Naruto" is its fight choreography, which is more choreographed around hand-to-hand martial arts than most other battle shonen. Yes, the ninjas in "Naruto" use "jutsus," or magical/superpowered attacks powered by spiritual energy, or chakra. But the core of the series' fight scenes is mano-a-mano fights that lay on the brutality and raw emotion; that's especially true in Naruto and Sasuke's various duels.

It has been revealed that the combat in "Naruto" likewise employs parkour acrobatics in the vein of wuxia. (In-universe, ninja learn to channel their chakra to balance on, climb, and run through trees.) Cretton directing "Shang-Chi," a wuxia-flavored Marvel movie, and Spider-Man, who webslings through Newly introduced York City like how Naruto and his ilk dash through forests, gives him the perfect experience to deliver the heightened-but-not-completely intensity of the action from the early "Naruto" arcs.

Sources indicate that cretton also has the perfect sensei to consult with in Masashi Kishimoto, who has endorsed Cretton as the perfect director for the project, the same way that "One Piece" creator Eiichiro Oda personally approved elements of Netflix's "One Piece" series. "One Piece" proved live-action shonen manga/anime can work in the TV format, and "Naruto" might be the project that proves it can be a blockbuster movie.

"Naruto" is right now in development.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that capcom’s live-service dino shooter Exoprimal officially has an end date.
  • “We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027,” the Resident Evil publisher declared this week.
  • The end of service won’t come as a shock to anyone who’s been following the game’s trajectory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that capcom’s live-service dino shooter Exoprimal officially has an end date. Servers will go offline for good in September 2027, just a little over four years after it originally introduced day-and-date with Game Pass. You can still buy it for $60, for some reason.

“We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027,” the Resident Evil publisher declared this week. “We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.”.

The end of service won’t come as a shock to anyone who’s been following the game’s trajectory. Launched in July 2023, it was an early-comer to the wave of post-covid online multiplayer games that have all rapidly been abandoned in the years since. Capcom pulled the plug on additional content updates just 12 months into the game’s life.

According to recent reports, premium passes and microtransactions were still being sold, however. That all ended this week on November 24 alongside the end of service announcement. The game itself and all its DLC will be delisted from consoles and PC on March 30, 2027. Those who already purchased the game will still be able to re-download it and play until the servers go offline.

That is unlikely to be many people. The shooter peaked at eight concurrent players on Steam today. While the shooter had a unique sensibility and some cool horde mechanics, it wasn’t the spiritual Dino Crisis revival most fans had hoped for. Instead, it ended up another example of the industry’s wasted efforts to cash in on the latest gaming fad, and further proof of all the things the Stop Killing Games crowd has been warning people about.

#97280. GTA 6: All The Secret Controls And Gameplay Features You Might Have Missed

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2883 w)

GTA 6: All The Secret Controls And Gameplay Features You Might Have Missed

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • In a recent development, instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists. You've got everything you'd expect for exploring its open-world environment, from options to sprint to aiming your gun, but there's a whole lot more to the game when you start experimenting with the inputs. Whether you're driving or jogging, Jason and Lucia are capable of a whole lot more, and these hidden features aren't thrown at you when you start the game. Instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience. If you don't want to accidentally stumble on them, here's a closer look at every hidden gameplay feature we've discovered so far. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub. Go into first-person mode Want to examine the world in more detail around you? Press L2 (LT on Xbox) to highlight something, then press R3 to go into first-person mode. Ordinarily, you can't move around in this mode, but there is a glitch to force the game to lock you into first-person. Change shoulder cameras Not too substantial a fan of the default over-the-shoulder aiming in GTA 6? You can switch which shoulder you aim from during combat by holding the left button on your D-pad while aiming with L2. Quick-swap between weapons At the same time, you can also quick-swap between weapons by tapping Triangle/Y while aiming, allowing you to keep blastin' like you're some sort of Frank Reynolds character. Do a combat roll! Need to close the gap promptly and avoid taking a few lead injections? Tap X/A while aiming, and you'll do a combat roll. Do a backflip! To show off some athleticism, run towards water, and as you get to the edge, hold X/A on the controller to do a backflip. Pistol-whip when you're out of bullets Got a gun in your hand, but you're out of bullets? It turns out that firearms are still good for inflicting blunt-force trauma, as you can use the melee attack (Square on PS5, X on Xbox) to knock enemies out. Choke enemies out For a stealthy beatdown, start a fight in GTA 6, grapple your opponent with R2, and then hold Square/X to set them up for a chokehold. Press the indicated D-pad button on your controller, and you'll trigger the chokehold. Chain-jump across gaps If you're running across an area that has multiple small gaps, you can tap X to jump across and tap it again to keep your momentum going. Your car door is also a weapon Instead of damaging the hood of your car in GTA 6, put a dent in your door by smashing it into a pedestrian. Like melee attacks, you can hit Square/X on your controller while driving to nail an unlucky person with the door. Your feet are technically free when you're on a bike And if you're not in a car? You can relive your Road Rash days by hitting the melee button to kick someone instead while you scoot around on a bike. Change how you wear your cap Whether you like to wear your cap in a traditional sun-blocking style or backwards, you can swap the position of your headwear easily. Just open the items and weapon wheel by holding L1, select items, and navigate to your cap. Press X/A and you can switch styles. Distract enemies with some whistling, which I can't do in real life GTA 6 makes for a surprisingly good stealth game, and for those scenarios where you need to draw enemy attention, you can whistle at them. Crouch, take cover, hold L2 to aim at a target, and press Triangle/Y to whistle. Loiter like a champ with leaning actions One of the cooler features in GTA 6 for photography fans is the option to lean against walls and railings. When you're near a wall, you can hold Circle/B to lean against it, and when next to a railing, press L3 to rest on that structure--pretty cool for when you want to take a photograph of Jason or Lucia while they chill out. If you're on solid ground, you can also hold down Circle/B to sit down. Choose your favorite hand If you want Jason or Lucia to emulate your dominant hand while they're holding something, press left or right on the D-pad. You can also make them hold two items at the same time, in case you want to show off that you're one of the lucky even-handed few. Auto-drive to destinations  One of our favorite modes in the game--especially when we want to soak in the scenery of Vice City--auto-drive is pretty easy to miss. While you're driving, hold the down button on the D-pad, press Start to enable Cinematic Mode, and then hold Circle/B to switch to auto-drive mode. You can also set the speed between slow/normal/fast for your commute. Quick-scan vehicles Instead of navigating to your WAiNK app, just hold Up on your D-Pad to bring it up instantly. Duck while driving so you can avoid being shot You're going to be in plenty of high-speed shootouts in GTA 6, and if you want to keep your head on your shoulders, hold the Circle/B button while driving to duck down. You have turn signals; use them Unless you're driving the equivalent of a BMW in GTA 6, you should use turn signals. While you're in your car, tap left or right on your D-pad to use these lights. They'll also cancel automatically after you've made a turn. Switch car headlights on and off Want to drive in stealth mode at night? Tap the circle button to turn off your headlights. Just don't be too surprised if other motorists flash you with their lights to remind you that you're driving dark. Leave the engine running Want to prepare your vehicle to be in getaway mode for a heist that you're about to pull off? You can leave the engine running by double-tapping Triangle/Y as you exit your car. Just be aware that this could invite car thieves to swipe your vehicle, since you're leaving it out there and purring. If you do this while piloting a boat, it'll also sail on while you explore the deck. Push vehicles In case you're stuck in a ditch or out of fuel, you can push your vehicle to safety. Position yourself behind, next to, or in front of your car (or boat), and keep pushing your character into it with the left stick until they switch to a pushing animation. Hold Square/X to move the vehicle, or flip it in case it has been overturned or beached. Leave your car door open You can also shave valuable seconds off your getaway by keeping your car door open. As you exit your car, press triangle once. Slide across your car hood For some Dukes of Hazzard action, sprint towards your car, aim for the hood, and tap X to slide across it. Yeehaw. Drop anchor If you don't want your boat to sail away without you while you search the ocean depths for treasure, make certain that you drop anchor. Press and hold left on the D-pad while piloting a boat, navigate to the vehicle menu with the right analog stick, and choose Anchor to lower it. Additional vehicle controls On that note, you can also find extra vehicle controls by bringing up the radio menu (press and hold left on the D-pad), and using the right analogue stick to navigate up. Turn radios on and off instantly If you're anything like me and your ears start to bleed when you boost a car that has the country music station turned on, double-tap left on the D-pad to instantly switch it off. You can smoke while driving Not that you should because it's bad for your health and both hands should be on the steering wheel, but you can hold L1 to bring up your items wheel, select cigarettes or a cigar, and then select R1 or R2 to start puffing away. Flick a cigarette You can also flick your cigarette when you're done smoking by holding the R2 button. Aim, and do that after you've poured out a trail of fuel on the ground, for extra cinema-style points. Flip the bird while driving The universal hand sign for telling someone that their driving is not up to par can easily be done by aiming at a motorist with L2 and then pressing R1 on your controller. Trash talk drivers Or if you need to give some verbal abuse, pull up next to another driver, press L2 to aim at them, and press R3 to give them some grief. Just don't be too surprised if they respond violently to your provocations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing some worthwhile discounts to wireless headphones, with savings of up to $160 across models from Sony, Bose, Apple, Nothing, and other brands. Several of the headphones on sale are relatively newly introduced, including Nothing's Headphone (1) Pro and Bose's second-generation QuietComfort Headphones, both of which launched this fall. Better yet, most of the deals below have dropped to their lowest prices yet on Amazon.

There's a good mix to choose from, too, whether you're looking for premium noise-canceling headphones for flights and commutes, a pair with enough battery life to get you through a week of listening, or something inexpensive for everyday use, with prices starting under $50. You can also check out the rest of our Black Friday coverage for more editor-vetted tech deals as the sale continues.

Sources indicate that the Nothing Headphone (a) is down to a record-low $109 from $199, making it a solid option for everyday listening, especially for Android users who can take advantage of LDAC for higher-quality wireless audio. For more on it, check out this PCMag review.

Spending another $60 gets you the Nothing Headphone (1), now $169 from $299, which is also a record low. It offers a more premium listening experience with active noise cancellation, automatic playback pausing when you take the headphones off, and the option to listen through either USB-C or a 3.5mm cable, making it a well-rounded choice for everyday use. For more on it, check out this PCMag review.

Nothing's newest and most expensive over-ears, the Headphone (1) Pro, are already $80 off at $319, only a couple of months after launching at $399. This is the pair to get for sound quality, since Nothing moved to a three-driver setup in each earcup, and the result is a fuller, more detailed sound than either the Headphone (1) or Headphone (a). For more on it, check out this PCMag review.

Sony's flagship WH-1000XM6 headphones are down to $378 from $459.99, their lowest price yet. Noise cancellation is still the main reason to buy them, and they remain among the best options for blocking out engine rumble on a flight, traffic during a commute, or chatter in a busy office. For more on these over-ears, you can check out our in-depth review.

Sony's WH-CH730N brings noise cancellation down to a much more approachable price, and at $98, down from $179.99, it's the lowest it's been on Amazon. This 2026 update to Sony's budget noise-canceling line now folds up for travel, which the previous model couldn't do, and battery life has jumped to up to 50 hours with noise cancellation on.

Sources indicate that sony's WH-CH530 is the most affordable pair in this roundup at $38, down from $69.99—that's also the lowest it's been since its release this fall. These are simple on-ear headphones without noise cancellation, but they sound better than you'd expect at this price, and the battery lasts up to 55 hours, so a full week of commuting or classes shouldn't be a problem.

Recent findings suggest that the second-generation Bose QuietComfort Headphones are down to $199 from $359, their lowest price yet. That's a substantial discount for a pair that delivers on two of Bose's biggest strengths: comfort and noise cancellation. You can read PCMag's review for a closer look at how they perform.

Bose's flagship QuietComfort Ultra headphones (2nd gen) are down to $339 from $449, saving you $110. Their noise cancellation is among the best you'll find in consumer headphones, making them particularly appealing for frequent flyers or anyone who spends a lot of time in noisy environments. For more on their features and performance, you can check out PCMag's review.

Recent findings suggest that the 2026 JBL Tune 680NC are down to $49.95 from $109.95, their lowest price to date. That's a pretty good deal for anyone looking for affordable noise-canceling headphones, especially since you get adaptive noise cancellation that adjusts to your surroundings and up to 50 hours of battery life with it enabled.

For the same price, JBL's Tune 730BT trades noise cancellation for a larger over-ear fit and even longer battery life, rated at up to 76 hours. At $49.95, down from $89.95, it's at its lowest price on Amazon, and a sensible choice for anyone who mostly listens at home, at a desk, or on quieter commutes where noise cancellation isn't essential.

The JBL Live 780NC are down to $129.95 from $249.95, making them considerably more appealing than at their original price. Battery life is a major advantage here, with JBL estimating up to 50 hours with noise cancellation enabled and 80 hours without, so frequent charging shouldn't be a concern. They also support LDAC for higher-quality Bluetooth audio with compatible devices. For more on their features and performance, you can check out PCMag's review.

In a recent development, apple’s AirPods Max 2 are down to $449 from $549, saving you $100 on the second-generation over-ears that Apple released earlier this year. While the design hasn’t changed much from the original, the upgrade to Apple’s H2 chip brings improved noise cancellation, while its sound remains among the best you'll find in wireless headphones. You can read PCMag's review for a closer look at how they perform.

Soundcore's Q20i headphones are down to $42.69 from $69.99, making them one of the more affordable options for anyone looking for noise-canceling over-ears from a recognizable brand. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What's the most famous film in history?
  • Recent findings suggest that margaret Hamilton as The Wicked Witch of the West is the definitive cultural image of a wicked witch.
  • Recent findings suggest that "Oz" wasn't the first ever color film, despite misconceptions otherwise, but it still represents a turning point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What's the most famous film in history? "Star Wars"? "Citizen Kane"? "Casablanca"? Victor Fleming's "The Wizard of Oz" has to be in contention. "Oz" remains as beloved almost a century after its premiere as it was in its day, and everything of note about the movie is embedded into pop culture, from the Yellow Brick Road to the characters who walk it to the Flying Monkeys. Ever since the 1950s, the film has become a staple of television programming, ensuring generations that came long after the movie itself still learn from an early age to cherish it.

Recent findings suggest that margaret Hamilton as The Wicked Witch of the West is the definitive cultural image of a wicked witch. Her green skin, black outfit with a pointed hat, and, of course, her broom are the blueprint for countless other witches (not to mention, Halloween costumes).

Recent findings suggest that "Oz" wasn't the first ever color film, despite misconceptions otherwise, but it still represents a turning point. One reason the error sticks is how well it maps onto the movie's narrative. Dorothy Gale's (Judy Garland) story begins in plain old Kansas, shot in black and white. Then, when she lands in Oz, the movie turns into technicolor. Even today, the film's rainbow-colored fantasy remains a beautiful spectacle.

Many, many unofficial "Wizard of Oz" sequels and prequels have been made, including various animated movies and TV series. Later "Oz" movies range from the (surprisingly frightening) 1985 sequel "Return to Oz" to Sam Raimi's 2013 prequel about the wizard, "Oz the Great and Powerful." Then of course, there's the stage musical (and now two-part movie) "Wicked," the only "Oz"-inspired work that even comes close to the original movie's cultural status.

Recent findings suggest that as you almost certainly know, during "The Wizard of Oz," Dorothy and her little dog Toto get swept away by  a twister to the Land of Oz. After a grand adventure, she realizes the power to go home was with her all along in the ruby slippers gifted to her by Glinda the Good Witch (Billie Burke). So, calling on the slippers' power, Dorothy closes her eyes and wakes up in her bed back in Kansas after affirming "There's no place like home!" (suggesting, unlike in its source material, Dorothy's adventure was all a dream). She then declares to her Aunt Em (Clara Blandick) and everyone else present that there is, indeed, no place like home.

According to recent reports, at the beginning of "The Wizard of Oz," Dorothy wants to see more of the world beyond Kansas, as she sings in "Somewhere Over The Rainbow." She finally runs away to save her dog Toto from the cruel Mrs. Gulch (Margaret Hamilton), but then rushes back when traveling performer Professor Marvel (Frank Morgan) warns her that her aunt, uncle, and friends back at the farm worry for her.

According to recent reports, there was no doubt that Dolly Parton tribute night at The Voice would be special. NBC’s long-running singing competition, which is presently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, brought the Top 10 together to perform duets to the greatest hits from the late country icon. It was an hour of performances that were entertaining and emotional as each pairing came from different teams, allowing the coaches to work together in rehearsals for the first time.

All of the performances had an added weight to them because the coaches and singers clearly wanted to do the legendary Dolly Parton justice. After a group performance of “9 to 5” that included an entire troupe of backing dancers, BigCountry (Team Queen) and Dakota Cohen (Team Adam) kicked things off with a rockin’ version of “Jolene” that was big on personality and a fun blend of country and rock. It was smart to start the night with such a jolt of energy, allowing the competitors to keep riding that wave all night.

Recent findings suggest that when it finally came time for the most anticipated song of the night in any Dolly Parton tribute, it was up to Connor Closs (Team Adam) and Brianna Cameron (Team Kelly) to tackle “I Will Always Love You.” A song so major it’s terrifying for any singer to take on, let alone a male vocalist and a 14-year-old, these two beautifully blended their vocals in ways that allowed them to uplift each other and soar even higher. Hands down, it was a showstopper, and it stepped Brianna up as a real contender to win it all.

While it was clear the duet of “I Will Always Love You” stole the show, it definitely wasn’t the only memorable performance of the episode. Ferryn & Brinkley (Team Riley) and Kyle Davis (Team Kelly) were paired up on “Islands in the Stream.” It was already charming that the 61-year-old dad was dueting with sisters who are the age of his own daughters and they had a very father-daughter vibe going on. But the reveal that Ferryn & Brinkley both work full-time at Dollywood, the amusement park owned by Dolly Parton herself, and that they even had footage of Ferryn on stage with the icon was really special to see.

Sources indicate that since first appearing at the Blind Auditions, Ferryn & Brinkley have been hugely marketable. From their talent to their personalities, they look and feel like they could easily join the ranks of country stars who've also broken substantial in movies and TV, whether they ultimately win The Voice or not. As we move ever closer to the unveiling of the winning coach and star, it’s getting harder and harder to watch the singers get sent home, but I get the feeling that many of them are going to have a life in entertainment beyond this season.

Recent findings suggest that the only real complaint I’ve had about the Live Reveals has been the lack of coach banter and shenanigans, which was absolutely delightful earlier in the season. Seeing Dolly Parton in past The Voice appearances being her sassy self really helped make up for some of that and was a fitting way to remember her.

The Voice Season 30 will continue to air on NBC on Mondays until the two-hour finale on December 14th when the winner is finally crowned. You can also watch the next day with a Peacock subscription.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles.
  • Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles.
  • In a recent development, that's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles. But it isn't without complications, especially if you're trying to experience the sights and sounds of Vice City with all the moody contrast and bright highlights that HDR offers. That's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it. Like many other games, GTA VI doesn't use the system-level HDR settings on either the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Instead it features its own calibration tool, which lets you adjust the maximum brightness, black levels, and paper white values that work best on your display. While the tool makes calibration seem straightforward, there's an glitch with it that makes it very unreliable. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d3UaVoP6dPg Specifically, the maximum brightness and paper white point values seem to be linked in a way that is both unclear and incorrect. Normally you would set these values individually, with maximum brightness set according to the value your display supports and the paper white value that looks best to you. GTA VI instead changes the maximum peak brightness value it is storing as you change the paper white point. For example, if you set a maximum peak brightness at 1000 nits (a typical value) but then reduce the paper white point (given how how its default is), the peak brightness value reduces as well, with no indication to you that it's happening. HDR enthusiasts and handy calibration assistors HDTVTest and GamingTech have both confirmed the issue, and provided some rough workarounds until Rockstar (hopefully) releases a fix. The idea is setting the maximum brightness value higher than your display supports, but in line with what the game is expecting based on the paper white point value to choose. It's confusing, but GamingTech has drawn up a table that might help depending on your display's specifications. HDTVTest's approach is similar but with different recommended values for both the ideal paper white point and black level values, so you'll need to do some experimenting on your end to find what suits your setup best. Rockstar has released the first patch for GTA VI, but it mostly addresses some widespread bugs that players have been encountering since launch. HDR issues were also common at launch with Red Dead Redemption 2 but eventually were fixed sometime after, but if you're like 45 million other people and planning to explore Leonida today, then hopefully these tweaks let you get it looking its finest.

According to recent reports, sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players, which isn't bad for a game that's presently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

In a recent development, alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active consumers drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the firm's estimates.

Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims, with an estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend, and EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M.".

But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott indicates: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.

Sources indicate that as Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Sources indicate that even to this day, there's a debate over whether or not "Star Trek: The Animated Series" counts as a canonical installment in the "Star Trek" franchise. The show ran for 22 episodes over the course of two seasons from 1973 to 1974, and, in certain respects, it's actually better than "The Original Series." Being an animated 30-minute show, it's a lot more efficient in its storytelling and is able to visually realize far more expansive and outlandish ideas. For instance, it features aliens that evolved from plants and an episode that takes place largely underwater.

In a recent development, that said, there are aspects of "The Animated Series" that directly contradict other entries in the franchise. Take "The Counter-Clock Incident," an episode that introduces Commodore Robert April (James Doohan) as an elderly white man. However, when the character reappeared on "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," he was played by Adrian Holmes, a Black actor. Then there's the episode "The Magicks of Megas-Tu," which is about the USS Enterprise traveling to the center of the galaxy and encountering a being believed to be the Devil. The thing is, this clashes with the film "Star Trek V: The Final Frontier," in which the Enterprise's crew meets an entity thought to be God at the center of the galaxy.

Sources indicate that according to the oral history book "The Fifty-Year Mission," edited by Mark Altman and Edward Gross, "Star Trek" creator Gene Roddenberry himself even said that "The Animated Series" isn't strictly canon. Yet, a lot of the show has become canon over time, as some of the people who worked on it discussed in the short documentary "Drawn to the Final Frontier" (itself included on the series' DVD release).

Sources indicate that it should immediately be pointed out that "Star Trek: The Animated Series" was penned by many of the same writers who worked on "Star Trek: The Original Series," was created by Gene Roddenberry, and features most of the actors from "The Original Series" to boot (save for Walter Koenig as Chekov). What's more, in "Drawn to the Final Frontier," longtime "Trek" writer D.C. Fontana noted that "The Animated Series" had a research manufacturer to ensure it aligned with the events of "The Original Series." As she put it, "It has to follow. It has to make sense. They have to agree.".

Expanding on this, "The Magicks of Megas-Tu" writer Larry Brody addressed the canon question directly in "Drawn to the Final Frontier," stating, "My take as to whether this fits into the 'Star Trek' legacy is that it fits into my version of the 'Star Trek' legacy. I think it should!" Meanwhile, "The Original Series" and "The Animated Series" writer David Gerrold said he felt that debates about canon are silly:.

Sources indicate that "All this argument about canon is stupid. It has Gene Roddenberry's name on it. It has William Shatner as Kirk, it has Leonard Nimoy as Spock, it has [DeForest] Kelley as McCoy, it has Jimmy Doohan as Scotty, it has Majel Barrett as Nurse Chapel, it has Nichelle Nichols as Uhura, it has George Takei as Sulu.".

In a recent development, likewise, when "The Animated Series" initially aired, it didn't really undermine what had been laid down by "The Original Series." Rather, it was the "Star Trek" shows and movies that came after it that led to problems. That sounds like canon to me.

Indeed, many details from "Star Trek: The Animated Series" have since found their way into the live-action canon, like how James Kirk's middle name is Tiberius (as he clarifies in the "Animated Series" episode "Bem"). And though presented as a novel invention on "Star Trek: The Next Generation," the holodeck first appeared in the "Animated Series" episode "The Practical Joker.".

According to recent reports, in keeping with this, the show "Star Trek: Enterprise" incorporates several elements of "The Animated Series" into the mix. Specifically, a Sehlat — a Vulcan creature that serves as Spock's childhood pet in the "Animated Series" episode "Yesteryear" — appears in the "Enterprise" episode "The Forge." The "Enterprise" episode "The Catwalk" similarly confirms that Vulcans go on a desert-bound maturation ritual when they are children known as the kahs-wan, a term that was first spoken in, you guessed it, "Yesteryear.".

And that's to mention nothing of the animated show "Star Trek: Lower Decks," which integrates myriad details and Easter eggs alluding to "The Animated Series." The latter show may be somewhat forgotten these days, but it's certainly worth revisiting (or watching for the very first time) and remains central to so much of the rest of the "Star Trek" mythology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

“You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

“So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” says Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

Recent findings suggest that now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

Sources indicate that kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

Though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

It has been revealed that frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

Industry observers note that alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

Alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

According to recent reports, frost: I was at a place where I stated, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

Industry observers note that alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

Kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

It has been revealed that alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

Recent findings suggest that frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

Kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

Alderton: I have a similar thing in that for the majority of the book, one of the lead characters is completely unknowable. Not just to Elizabeth, but to the audience as well. So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. There is no other option I think than staying with Lizzie.

Frost: It’s very different because the book is entirely from Newland’s point of view. The thing that I wanted to do, and that Netflix were really excited for me to do, was to open it up to find out who the women were.

Industry observers note that I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

Recent findings suggest that the impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

Sources indicate that alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that new perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

According to recent reports, frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

Sources indicate that frost: She had this significant affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

It has been revealed that alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Industry observers note that kazan to Alderton: You’re also a novelist. How are you thinking about bisecting yourself—using both parts of your brain, the novelist part and the dramatist part?

Sources indicate that alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

What amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. It’s like her agent had remarked to her, “I know you’re going to write this novel about this family of five women, but remember, we could get a great movie deal off the back of it. So try and make it as adaptable as possible.” It has literally been written for TV in this totally perfect six-part structure. I just wish she was around to have written screenplays.

Kazan: This is how I feel about Tolstoy too. When I read War and Peace, I’m like, “Oh, he’s seeing it as if it’s a movie.” It’s very strange to read that so far ahead of the technology to make that possible.

Where was each of your point of entry? What was the first scene that you wrote?

Recent findings suggest that frost: I always break the whole thing in quite a lot of detail to feel like I understand where the story's going. I think when I actually started writing, I probably wrote from the beginning.

Kazan: So you outlined her therapy?

Industry observers note that alderton: I do the same. It’s the only thing that gives me freedom and confidence to write.

Kazan: And did you know how many episodes you wanted from the start, or did that change?

It has been revealed that frost: At one point it was longer, and at one point it was shorter. It’s eight in the end. What about you?

Sources indicate that kazan: I wanted eight originally, and then for budget and logistical reasons, I had to boil it down to seven quite late in the process. I had been four years into adapting it.

Kazan: Yeah. And we were a month away from production, and I had to restructure everything quite late in the game.

Kazan: Yeah, but you know what? It was actually this enormous gift. I had this writing teacher in college, a poetry teacher who talked a lot about constraints. And I don’t know if you've ever seen the... What’s his name? He’s a nightmare, but forgive me—the guy who directed Melancholia.

Kazan: There’s this beautiful Lars Von Trier film called The Five Obstructions, a documentary. He challenges his filmmaking teacher to remake this perfect short film that he made in the 1960s with five sets of obstructions to help him break open his creative process again. And that, combined with what my poetry teacher was always saying—which is the form gives you freedom.

Kazan: I feel like having to... Every time I’ve received, “Okay, we don’t have the money for X, or we don’t have the location for Y, or you have to boil eight episodes down to seven,” that it made me think again about, okay, what’s crucial here? Seeing the instruction as a gift rather than as an obstacle really just helped me over and over again. I actually gave myself one night to be really mad about it, and then the next day I was—.

Kazan: A lot of showrunning, for me at least, has been about learning how to manage my emotions on my own time so that I can go to work and help manage everything. The next day, as soon as I started reworking it, I discovered all of the gifts that it would give me.

Sources indicate that alderton: That lesson is one that you only learn with the privilege of experience. This is only my second TV show. My first, Everything I Know About Love, was an adaptation of my memoir. But I remember now the moments where I mentioned, “If we have to lose this scene, there’s no point shooting the whole show.” Things like that.

Kazan: And then you’re in the edit and you’re like, “Actually, that’s better.”.

Alderton: Totally. Or I think back on these things that we couldn’t afford or practically couldn’t work that I really thought would rip out the heart and soul of the show. And now I never dream of an alternate version of that show where those things were put in.

I don’t think I would’ve been as zen as you. I think I would’ve been a petty, grouchy bitch for three days, rather than one.

Kazan: At that point, I was still trying to get my greenlight. I want to hear Dolly’s answer to the first scene question.

According to recent reports, alderton: Oh, sure. So the opening of Pride and Prejudice in the book is obviously setting up the central drama, which is “we need a man. There's a newly introduced man in town.” We decided to put Darcy at the very, very top of the show. There is so much in Pride and Prejudice to delight in. What is easy to forget is that it is the best love story of all time. And I’m just like, “We should land that. The first thing we should land is this intrigue between these two characters.”.

It has been revealed that so Elizabeth is walking around Netherfield Park being kind of nosy and breaking the rules, and she’s intrigued by this man. So much of their attraction to each other, which everyone finds so delicious to read, is that they’re just fascinated with each other, and it takes them a while to work out why. So we wanted to establish that.

Kazan: I love that. I loved her spying and the sort of misunderstanding of who he is.

Dolly, were you wrestling at all about what to do with “it’s truth universally acknowledged,” the most famous line in literature?

According to recent reports, alderton: Andrew Davies gives that line to Elizabeth Bennet, but for me, it felt like it’s the Mrs. Bennet line. The reinterpretation, I suppose, that I’ve done on my Pride and Prejudice is a bit of a justice for Mrs. Bennet. I’m working so hard in this adaptation to really understand why she is the way she is, why she’s so hysterical, why she's seemingly such a social climber. So to give her that line, it felt like we were just off to the races. This is a woman whose preoccupation in life is making sure her daughters are safe. So yeah, it felt like it was an easy line for Olivia [Colman].

When it comes to casting, can you articulate what makes somebody feel appropriate for a period show, versus somebody who seems too contemporary?

Kazan: Or maybe that’s not a concern.

Industry observers note that frost: I think for me, casting is really instinctive. Ben Radcliffe, right from his first tape, I was just, “He is Newland Archer. That is the end of the conversation. We are having him.”.

Kazan: Did you audition all of them?

Sources indicate that frost: All of them did tapes or auditions. It’s so hard to explain, isn’t it? You see somebody and you just go, “That’s what I have in my head. That’s what we need.”.

Alderton: We kind of knew who we wanted Lizzie and Darcy to be, and we had to do chemistry. We did a chemistry [read] with Emma and Jack, and Emma’s an EP on the show. So the minute Jack left, Emma and I looked at each other, and we were like, “That’s totally Darcy.”.

Sources indicate that but it’s interesting that you were saying that thing about chemistry. I don’t know about you guys, but every time I do casting, I’m amazed how much it feels like falling in love. You go away and you find yourself Googling them and thinking about them and dreaming about them. It’s so wonderful if then they want to do it, and it’s so heartbreaking if they don’t.

Kazan: You fall in love, and then sometimes your love affair doesn’t work out.

Alderton: What was your process like?

Frost: Florence [Pugh] was involved really early, right?

Kazan: She was. I had always had this feeling about East of Eden, and I had sort of tried to ignore that feeling because of my grandfather’s relationship to the material and my relationship to coming from this family. And about a year and a half before this call came, I had written my agent saying, “This is so embarrassing, but if the rights to East of Eden ever come up, can you please let me know so that I can pitch on it?” So they did me a solid. I got an appointment to meet, but I didn’t have a lot of time to prepare.

They asked, “Do you have any actors in mind?” I think I had walked into the room not thinking that I had any actors in mind, and then Florence came out of my mouth. I had seen Midsommar, and I felt like I was witnessing the birth of a genius. And Cathy Ames is such a challenging part that I needed an actor of that caliber. But then we didn’t do any more casting for four years after that.

Frost: But she stayed faithful.

In a recent development, kazan: She did. The whole reason this show came together when it did was that there was a window that she had in her schedule. We didn’t have directors yet, and we didn’t have any other cast yet. Her window was starting in October, and between April and June, we put everything together.

According to recent reports, so much of it is alchemical. But once you have that central pole that all the spokes are going to come off of, then you start going, “Okay, well if it’s this Lizzie Bennet, it has to be that Mr. Darcy. If it’s this Newland Archer, it has to be this Ellen.”.

In a recent development, on the page, East of Eden is the only one of these three novels that has a protagonist who isn’t white. But that isn’t true of your series. I’m curious, Emma and Dolly, if you can speak to that—casting actors who aren’t white in these stories that are largely about white characters.

Frost: Yeah. Edith Wharton came from such a privileged, elite white bubble. That is completely what her life was. But the story is about a man who is chafing against that, and these rules are killing him. So having the contrast of the world inside and outside of that elite white bubble felt crucial to telling this story. And Ellen is part of this really exciting wave of immigration that’s coming into New York at the time, and it’s blowing this old world to pieces. And it’s so much more exciting than this kind of decaying, crusty world that he’s been trapped by.

So for me, it felt like a very organic thing to have non-white characters as well that provide that contrast. They are the newly introduced ideas, they are the exciting conversations, they are the music that’s coming in. So he was one foot in each, and it was a very organic thing to do.

Alderton: I think there are so many different ways that you can look at diversity with period work. Bridgerton’s a great example of a specific thing. Colorblind casting is a specific example. We decided that we wanted our Pride and Prejudice to be very rooted in historical reality, but we also didn’t want to make an all-white Pride and Prejudice. We wanted to be inclusive and representative. So we just did our homework, and we found cases of families much like the Bingleys who had roots in trade where there were mixed-race families.

In a recent development, was it the most common thing in Regency England? No. But it’s not the most common thing that a man like Mr. Darcy would’ve married Elizabeth Bennet. It’s so simple in my mind. It’s all made up anyway, and those actors were the best actors for those roles.

Sources indicate that kazan: Can I also say—we have white-presenting actors in East of Eden who have Caribbean roots, and Chinese American people that present as white in our series. I think the idea of whiteness, it can be a weapon. I think it can be weaponized: who we say is white and who we say isn’t white. I just think it’s a funny thing of who we agree is allowed to be in these things and who isn’t.

I do always think it’s a hard thing, because racial identity is such an crucial part of how people go through the world. And what both of you are saying about finding the logic within your stories for the casting that you want to make, I think, is really important. But I also think it's important to think about how there are identities that are not visible.

Was there one moment from each of your novels that you were the most nervous about getting right?

Sources indicate that frost: I don’t know if it’s one piece of the novel per se, but what gave me pause was trying to find a way into Ellen, Countess Olenska. I wanted to find a way to stay completely true to the spirit and intention of her as a character, but make her emotionally legible to a 21st-century audience. As framed in the novel, there is an element of her being beaten by her husband, and now she needs another man to rescue her. That isn’t this sort of independent, forward-looking woman that I felt I needed at the center of the show.

In a recent development, but Edith Wharton, as ever, is so brilliant that she sort of provided this solution partly through me drawing on her own life, which I used to infuse Ellen. Also, without giving spoilers, there are things that are said about Ellen in the novel that Ellen never confirms. We are in a world of rumor and reputation, and it suddenly became clear to me that what is said about her isn't necessarily true. Once I felt I understood who she was, the whole thing just sort of opened up for me. What about you guys?

Alderton: My take is not so much because of the text—it was because of a previous adaptation.

Kazan: I was going to ask you guys about this.

Alderton: About these adaptations that live in your head.

Kazan: All three of these books have multiple—if not multiple, at least a beloved adaptation.

Alderton: Totally. And on the whole, I feel very comfortable being in this great tradition of every 20 or 30 years, there's a Pride and Prejudice. I like that. I don't want to pretend like there are no other adaptations.

Recent findings suggest that but the one thing that was in my head from the very beginning was the wet-shirt moment. Because it’s such a pivotal moment in the story when we see Darcy for who he is the first time. We understand why he’s been so guarded. We understand why he grips to these social structures so strongly. We understand that he’s a deeply honorable, protective, very recently wounded man.

Industry observers note that alderton: And hot as hell. That’s why the wet shirt was so brilliant, because there’s something about literally seeing the skin of him—literally seeing underneath his carapace for the first time. So I was like, “How are we going to do that?” And I think where I got to in the end is that each generation gets the Darcy that they need, whether it’s Laurence Olivier or Colin Firth or Matthew Macfadyen. The ’90s was a very sexually charged, erotic time in culture, so that’s why we got that Darcy. Matthew, there was something that was kind of cooler about his Darcy.

It has been revealed that alderton: And more indie, which represents his time. And where we are now is a time where masculinity is in crisis. And where Jack instinctively went with his Darcy, it’s quite an honorable place and quite a tender place. So that moment in Pemberley, we actually chose to do it over a series of micro moments that show the softness of Darcy. Which I find very deeply erotic in its own way.

What are your own favorite adaptations, not counting the works we’re speaking about?

Alderton: Mine’s the 1995 Sense and Sensibility. The Emma Thompson Sense and Sensibility.

Kazan: That’s a perfect movie. I love another Ang Lee adaptation, The Ice Storm.

Kazan: Thinking of plays, too—Cabaret is unbelievable, [Liza Minnelli’s] performance and what [Bob Fosse’s] doing with film that he couldn’t do in any other medium.

Alderton: But it still retains the theatricality somewhat.

Industry observers note that kazan: Yeah, completely. I have to shout out to my parents—my parents adapted a lot of films. [Editor’s note: Among other films, her mother, Robin Swicord, wrote Practical Magic and the 1994 Little Women; her father, Nicholas Kazan, wrote Reversal of Fortune.] I just demonstrated my kid their Matilda. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two are riding high right now from the success of Grand Theft Auto 6 with a reported 45 million copies sold and $4 billion in revenue already, but this could just the beginning of how much money GTA 6 could bring in. According to Bank of America stock analyst Omar Dessouky, the initial success of GTA 6 reinforces the company's belief that the game has a massive reach, and with that comes the possibility of monetizing the players even more when the next evolution of GTA Online is released. In fact, SeekingAlpha reported that Dessouky said he is so bullish that he believes GTA Online alone "can become a multibillion-dollar franchise, potentially larger than Fortnite." He said Fortnite generates as much as $5 billion in annual revenue, and GTA Online could be bigger in the fullness of time. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 The stock analyst went on to raise his price target on Take-Two's stock to $350. That would represent a significant upside, considering Take-Two currently trades at around $210/share. Take-Two's stock got hammered in 2026 and never fully recovered. The company's shares are down 16% so far in 2026 and down 12% over the past year. Investing is a long-term game, though. Zooming out, Take-Two has crushed it since GTA 5 released. If you bought $10,000 worth of Take-Two stock on the day GTA 5 came out in 2013, and never sold, you'd have more than $120,000 today. As for the next iteration of GTA Online, Rockstar has not said a word about what to expect or if such a mode is even coming. GTA 6, after all, is marketed as a strictly single-player game. That being said, it seems plainly obvious that a latest version of GTA Online is coming. According to multiple reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could launch in 2027, along with a PC edition of the game. GTA Online for GTA 5 has been, and continues to this day, to be a major moneymaker for Rockstar and Take-Two, and it's expected that the developer will find even more ways to make money from players with GTA 6 Online. Some have theorized that GTA 6 Online could have some form of user-generated content, for example, potentially leading to a marketplace of some kind. GTA 6 rolled out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it reached 32.5 million copies sold via pre-purchases alone. On day one, GTA 6 generated $3.79 billion in revenue. Over the first four days, GTA 6 has climbed to 44.9 million copies sold and more than $4 billion in revenue, according to a report. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review. If you’re just getting started with the game, be sure to read GameSpot’s top five best things to do first.

Industry News: There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages
