📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another firm is having an outage.
  • That pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public.
  • According to recent reports, but to skeptics of the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another firm is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication concerns." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

That pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen.".

According to recent reports, but to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering latest security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

In a recent development, mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find fresh security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be mentioned for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

You might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October update. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's important to understand that just about every tech giant that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

According to recent reports, barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as quickly as possible.

The implications aren't specific to any one organization, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Recent findings suggest that of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

A powerful sequence in Grand Theft Auto 6 is rapidly becoming a favorite among the game's many players, but a technical mishap made my experience of this scene very different--hilariously different. Chapter 2 of GTA 6 begins with Jason and Lucia in a rough spot, with the former still recovering from major injuries sustained at the end of Chapter 1, and the latter having to care for him. It isn't until the mission "Breakfast Run" that Jason is back on his feet, and the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like duo mark his recovery with a crime spree. Set to "Money or Nothing" by Dire Straits, Lucia and Jason rob a diner, not dissimilar to a scene from Pulp Fiction, and a playable montage highlights the pair robbing convenience shops, a clothing store, and other establishments. The image of Jason and Lucia busting open double doors, guns in hand, is probably the most iconic image of GTA 6, a statement of intent that defines the game's story going forward. https://bsky.app/profile/compenderizer.bsky.social/post/3n2yzmpjn6c2j But somehow, I had gotten a slightly different version of this montage. When I returned to the motel as Lucia, I sprinted toward the door, only for the game to place me back outside the room. The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut. I suspected that there was a cutscene that I missed showing Jason fully recovered, so I decided to carry out the mission. The problem was that Jason wouldn't put any clothes on. I drove to the diner as the game instructed me to, and the entire mission, Dire Straits and all, resumed with a mostly naked Jason. It was impossible not to cackle at the sheer absurdity of the situation, watching Jason terrorize locals and presumably solidifying a upcoming legacy as the Leonida underwear robber. At one point, the camera cut to Jason's bare foot slamming a gas pedal, and I was left breathless from laughter. Eventually, the game decided to put clothes back on Jason, but I had to visit a salon to grow his hair back. Iconic. Though GTA 6 features nudity in various degrees, you cannot dress Jason and Lucia in their underwear outside of their home. That sprint through the motel room door must have bypassed some sort of clothing check and allowed Jason to freely show skin outside of the motel. I've seen players online talk about an "underwear glitch," and I found one Reddit comment saying that they also had a nearly naked Jason run about in "Breakfast Run," so I appear to be an edge case in experiencing this specific glitch. I can't say that this bug "ruined" one of GTA 6's best missions for me, as I still found myself thoroughly entertained--just not in the way Rockstar Games wanted. Having Jason in his undies while still concealing his identity with a hat and bandana felt like something out of a Saints Row game rather than the fairly serious story GTA 6 was building up to that point. Despite the intense work and detail put into GTA 6, it certainly isn't free of silly glitches and bugs such as this. Luckily, many of them are more amusing than hampering, and Rockstar Games is already putting out post-launch patches for the title. If anything, I'm just bummed that I can't spend the rest of the game as Underwear Jason.

The surrealistic docudrama has already outperformed al reasonable expectations by this point (especially if/when it sets its sights on Academy gold), but this will have every chance to experience a very long tail as more and more viewers discover this movie without ever needing to leave their living rooms.

The baby, Xara Thompson, was found “safe and unharmed,” according to a Tuesday, November 24, Latest York State Police news release.

Industry observers note that dezerea Dashnaw and Raya A. Allen, the women accused of kidnapping the infant, were arrested Tuesday, according to police.

Dashnaw, 21, and Allen, 23, allegedly abducted the baby after Dashnaw arranged for Allen to drive with her to visit an acquaintance and her children in Sterling, a town located on Lake Ontario, police remarked.

“While inside the residence, Dashnaw allegedly took 4-month-old Xara Thompson without the mother’s knowledge or consent,” state police noted in the release.

The women then allegedly left the mother’s home with the baby, prompting authorities to issue an AMBER Alert as investigators searched for the child.

The alert stated, “The child was taken under circumstances that lead the police to believe that they are in imminent danger of serious bodily harm and/or death,” according to WWNY.

Authorities shared an image showing Dashnaw holding the infant.

Investigators ultimately found Dashnaw and Allen at a hotel in Plattsburgh, located more than 200 miles northeast from where the baby was taken from her mother, according to police.

Industry observers note that the baby was transported to Champlain Valley Physicians Hospital to be medically examined as a precaution, authorities noted. The AMBER Alert was ultimately canceled.

Industry observers note that dashnaw and Allen were arraigned on second degree kidnapping charges on Tuesday, according to police. They were ordered to be held in the Cayuga County Jail without bail.

It wasn’t immediately clear whether the women had entered pleas or retained legal counsel.

Sia’s post came approximately one hour after TMZ reported that her attorney, Laura Wasser — famous for representing high-profile clients including Kim Kardashian and Angelina Jolie in their divorces — had filed paperwork asking to bifurcate her marital status, meaning Sia would become legally single despite still battling Bernad over finances in court.

A broader custody agreement was reached last month, with Sia remaining Summi’s primary custodial parent, according to TMZ. They reportedly worked out a schedule for holidays and vacations and agreed to work with a parenting blueprint coordinator.

In April, Sia agreed to pay Bernad $42,500 per month in child support, as well as the cost of private school tuition, agreed extracurricular activities, health insurance and uninsured healthcare costs and a $5 million life insurance policy or trust in their son’s favor.

“I’m a sober working mom trying to buy peace,” Sia wrote via X at the time. “I have primary custody of our son and since i am the only parent earning income i still have to pay California’s incredibly high child support.”.

She continued, “This has been a horrific year, but it taught me how to navigate incredibly difficult situations, prioritize my family and not absorb other people’s negativity. ‘To err is human, to forgive is divine.’”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for years, most multiplayer games on Xbox consoles required a subscription to go online. From Xbox Live to Xbox Game Pass, Microsoft paywalled multiplayer on its platforms, but the tech giant reportedly aimed to break down that barrier for its next-gen console, Project Helix. According to Windows Central, Project Helix was conceived under the previous Xbox leadership team as the device that would bridge the divide between PC and console gaming. Like the Asus Xbox ROG Ally PC handhelds, the console is said to have an Xbox-inspired interface and full PC game support through storefronts like Steam. Because of that design decision, it's claimed it didn't make sense to continue with paid multiplayer, since that service is free for games purchased on PC platforms like Steam and the Epic Games Store. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7H6YGeREMgY&t=159s As the Windows Central report noted, that was reportedly the plan before Xbox leadership was shaken up and gaming hardware prices rose during the AI boom. With Asha Sharma now in charge of Xbox, the gaming division is more focused on profitability, and Microsoft's gaming arm has seen sweeping changes. Mass layoffs and studio divestitures occurred throughout 2026, and Project Helix could be a very expensive family of devices. If Microsoft ditches paid multiplayer, it loses a revenue stream for its next-gen push at a time when component prices have risen steeply. As part of its 25th anniversary celebrations, Microsoft also teased a few more details about Project Helix, calling it specifically "a console" that plays games from your PC, not "a PC that can also play console games." "When we think about Project Helix, it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said.

#97254. Rings Of Power Season 3 Demonstrates Why Canon Is Not Important In Lord Of The Rings

Rings Of Power Season 3 Demonstrates Why Canon Is Not Important In Lord Of The Rings

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that keep it secret, keep it safe ...
  • As an adaptation, "The Rings of Power" is possibly the most polarizing thing to come out of J.R.R.
  • In a recent development, now, canon is one of the biggest battlefronts of the internet fandom wars, which (as ridiculous as they are) themselves have only grown as significant franchises continue to dominate the entertainment landscape.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that keep it secret, keep it safe ... from spoilers. This article discusses major plot details from "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" up through to Season 3, Episode 6.

As an adaptation, "The Rings of Power" is possibly the most polarizing thing to come out of J.R.R. Tolkien's Legendarium in decades. From characters created specifically for the series to its portrayal of fan-favorites like Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), and its tweaks to Tolkien's Middle-earth lore, the show is full of creative elements that have proven controversial. That hasn't changed over time, either, as "The Rings of Power" Season 3 is now adding a love triangle, a new origin story for the Nazgûl, and a meeting between Sauron (Charlie Vickers) and a Balrog (Simon Pegg) to the pile (via IGN). Suffice it to say, these alternations have angered some fans who feel the series is deviating from the canon and, as such, Tolkien's intent.

In a recent development, now, canon is one of the biggest battlefronts of the internet fandom wars, which (as ridiculous as they are) themselves have only grown as significant franchises continue to dominate the entertainment landscape. As a result, lots of online conversations now center on how, say, a "Star Wars" TV series deviates from books written in the 1990s or how a movie like this year's "Resident Evil" fits into the larger property's timeline. But whenit comes to "The Rings of Power," it's even sillier since the show has to please fans of both Tolkien's books and Peter Jackson's "Lord of the Rings" movies alike (even though Jackson's films themselves make substantial modifications to their source material).

Here's the thing, though: Ultimately, canon is not important, especially when it comes to "Lord of the Rings.".

Recent findings suggest that middle-earth has a vast and detailed history spanning thousands of years. And yet, J.R.R. Tolkien technically only published two stories in his lifetime: "The Hobbit" and "The Lord of the Rings." So, when it comes to the proper "canon" of Middle-earth, that's really all there is to it. Sure, Tolkien's appendices introduce concepts such as the tale of Númenor, for example. But all the First Age stuff like the War of Wrath and the Silmarils, Morgoth and Sauron's history, and the larger saga of Arda all came from, essentially, scribbles and notes by Tolkien that were only published posthumously.

Moreover, another thing that makes Middle-earth's mythology so unique is that Tolkien's notes are full of inconsistencies and retcons. Indeed, there are many complications that Tolkien was able to fully make up his mind about, like the origin of the orcs and whether they are inherently and absolutely evil or not. Likewise, Tolkien struggled with whether to keep his original idea of Middle-earth having been a flat world that eventually turned into a spherical planet (after the fall of Númenor), and he never settled on an answer.

It wasn't just that, either. Much like George Lucas has changed the original "Star Wars" trilogy with every new re-release, Tolkien went back and forth on his writing about Middle-earth throughout his lifetime. In the end, he made tons of revisions big and small to the reprints of his "Lord of the Rings" books.

Sources indicate that if J.R.R. Tolkien himself never got around to delivering a complete and finished version of his "canon," then why should fans fight about it? If we should take one thing away from the professor's work, it's that he thought his own fictional universe was malleable, and nothing was set in stone until the last minute. He and George Lucas are far from the only creatives to take this approach, either. For that matter, something as worlds apart as "The Simpsons" is constantly tweaking its own "canon" (with one exception).

This is not to say that we should simply discard everything that has come before and hit the reset button with every fresh entry in a franchise. Consistency is important, but it's equally vital not to let new ideas be limited by what came before. "The Rings of Power" may be adding things that Tolkien never wrote, but it's giving us Sauron clashing with a Balrog, and isn't that idea just too cool to pass up? More than any other property, "Lord of the Rings" doesn't have an expanded universe that's set in stone, anyway. Rather, it's always morphed to incorporate fresh ideas to some degree, so why stop now?

In a recent development, "The Rings of Power" has many problems, especially when it comes to its pacing. That said, it's always done a good job of reinterpreting its source material in a way that captures the essence of Tolkien's ideals while integrating exciting concepts we haven't seen in this franchise before. Stream in on Prime Video, and see for yourself.

Grand Theft Auto 6 gets downright weird when you go off the beaten track, and one secret mission will see you travel to the bowels of hell to fight Beezleboss himself, Satan. This detour is worth it because you'll get cool cosmetics and a powerful shotgun, plus a nice little bump to your health. Here's how you can start this Doom-inspired mission in GTA 6. How to go to Hell in GTA 6 You can find this mission in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County, and it's generally recommended that you tackle it once you've gotten your bearings in Chapter 2 of GTA 6. You can access it with either Jason or Lucia, and you'll need to follow these steps to find it: Start the mission at night, preferably around midnight. Go to the northern section of Port Gellhorn (as indicated on the maps) and look for the Circles of Hell, a house with an open garage. Inside the garage, you'll find two NPCs rocking out. Press L2 to highlight them and start talking. Select the dialogue options "Having fun?" and "It's good" when prompted. Follow the NPCs into a van that appears shortly afterward, and get inside. After being transported to the camping grounds, press L2 to stare into the campfire. Once you've done all that, you'll be taken to Hell, and you'll have to face off against an army of demons. Don't worry! You'll be equipped with a powerful shotgun, so you can mow down the demons and fight your way to Satan. The Prince of Darkness will occasionally summon reinforcements to defend him, but the denizens of hell are no match for a few well-placed shotgun rounds. Finish off the devils, and you'll wake up at the campsite. For your efforts, you'll be rewarded with the following items and upgrades: Circles of Hell top New tattoo design Hellspawn Comshot 12 shotgun (collect it next to the throne) Permanent health boost For a closer look at GTA 6's supernatural side, check out how to encounter an unkillable NPC, solve the Bigfoot mystery, and help out some friendly aliens. How To Play GTA 6 On Your PC Or Phone Via Remote Play On Xbox

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox. This means you can play GTA 6 on your PC, smartphone, or a device like Xbox Rog Ally. Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working. From your console, select Settings then Devices & connections then Remote features. From there, check the box for Enable remote features. Xbox Remote Play also has a "test" feature so you can preview the experience in your home environment before going further. From there, you can play GTA 6 from a mobile device by accessing the Xbox Remote Play website, selecting the console you want to connect to, and then the device. To play GTA 6 on your PC or Xbox Rog Ally, consumers can open the Xbox app for PC, click on their profile, then select Accessories & Remote Play and then select Remote Play to choose the device to play on. Additionally, people have spotted that GTA 6's store page on the PlayStation Store now mentions that Remote Play is supported and that PlayStation 5 and PlayStation Portal owners can use cloud streaming if they have a Premium membership. Right now, you need a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S to stream GTA 6, but some are dreaming of the day when you can simply stream the game to your PC or phone without any expensive hardware. That day may eventually come for GTA 6, as Take-Two's own CEO has mentioned the rising cost of gaming hardware is not a good thing and that streaming games could be a big business very soon. “If you believe in streaming, and to be clear, we really do, and I’m happy to put a timeline on it. I think we’ll be in commercial streaming mode within three years, and by commercial, I mean low latency," Strauss Zelnick said. "That can 10x the effective installed base. Now, it doesn’t mean we’re going to 10x our revenue–and we wouldn’t project that we would–but because obviously your avid consumers already had access to video game machines. But I do think it creates great opportunity for titles that are broadly desirable, even outside of core markets.” GTA 6 is doing just fine without the potential expanded reach of streaming. After all, the game sold 32.5 million copies before launch and generated close to $4 billion in revenue by day one. Even if GTA 6 doesn't add support for full streaming without a console, the game is expected to expand its reach in a major way in 2027 with an expected PC release. Beyond that, GTA 6 is reportedly going to add an online mode in 2027 as well, and it could be bigger than Fortnite.

While we regularly see Lego Marvel sets roll out, this is the first-ever Marvel Rivals kit, and it'll go on sale starting January 1, 2027, priced at $50. GameSpot can also exclusively reveal the first images of Jeff below, showing the completed build alongside his box art. See at The Lego Store The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including his big eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar. This won't be a static figure either: once fully assembled, Jeff has a movable head, legs, tail, and fins that let builders recreate his joyful trot, swimming, and battle poses. For added touches, his collar includes his signature name tag, his tongue can be removed to close his mouth, and his fin can be detached so builders can replicate Jeff's Hide-and-Seek movement ability from the game. "Jeff brings together everything players love about a breakout gaming character: an unforgettable silhouette, a personality you understand instantly, and the ability to turn any match into a story," Lego Marvel design lead Jesper C. Nielsen mentioned in a press release. "We wanted this Lego model to capture both sides of him, from the lovable companion fans want beside their screen to the unpredictable strategist they meet in battle." Meanwhile, Jeff and the rest of the Marvel Rivals roster are preparing to cap off an entire year of Avengers-centric events that have been building up to the game's big Avengers: Doomsday tie-in. Season 11.5 kicks off on December 11. Nightcrawler was recently added to the game, bringing mutant energy, swords, and teleportation strategies, and he'll soon be followed by Marvel's unique take on Dracula, who has spent the last few months hibernating and healing for the battles ahead.

It has been revealed that now that we know that a Red Rising movie is in the works, it's completely understandable that we'd be on the edges of our seats waiting for any word on who might be cast in the book-to-screen adaptation. Eagle-eyed Red Rising fans -- yes, that's an intentional nod to the Bellona sigil right there -- have picked up on the fact that author Pierce Brown has followed Joseph Zada on Instagram, which has led to a lot of enthusiastic speculation that the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping star might be in talks to play a role in Red Rising movie. I've seen one specific character name coming up a lot as the perfect role for Zada to take on, but wait a second, because there are options here.

Industry observers note that to be clear up front, there is no official word that Zada is in talks to star in the Red Rising movie. However, it's not a stretch that his name would be circulating. As mentioned, fans noticed Pierce Brown followed Zada on Instagram. Then there's the fact that Zada is at the moment starring in Francis Lawrence's most recent movie adaptation. Given the news that Lawrence will be directing the Red Rising movie, it stands to reason that he might be considering people he's worked with already for the cast.

Sources indicate that on the other hand, the fact that Pierce Brown and Francis Lawrence have known each other for years (per Lawrence) also needs to be acknowledged, as Brown could've met Zada through the director and followed him just to follow him... as people do. In short, the follow could mean nothing or it could mean something.

However, since we're speculating, I want to talk about the role(s) he'd be right to take, starting with the one that seems to be a crowd favorite.

Recent findings suggest that the handsome Bellona's name came up quite a bit in the comments discussing who Zada should play, and I get it. Even as Golds go, Cassius is known to be extremely handsome, and well, Zada fits that description. Zada's also got the blond curls, which is one of the most distinctive things about Cassius' looks. Also, as a Gold, Cassius is tall, and so is Zada.

When it comes to casting the Gold characters (and Obsidians) in the movie, it seems unlikely that they're going to find the perfect actors to play the roles, who also just so happen to be around or above seven feet tall. How they make the size differences among the colors stand out on screen is going to be a challenge by itself, whether they use forced perspective, special effects or other techniques. Still, if they want to cast actors on the taller side for the Golds, IMDB has Zada listed as 6'2".

Relative to men of average height, Zada's reported height (or anywhere in the ballpark of six feet, really) seems like a good fit for a Gold on screen. That brings me to the alternate speculation, because I don't think Cassius is the only option, or possibly even the best one.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that darrow's the other name I've seen circulating, and honestly, he's the first person I thought of when I saw the topic of Joseph Zada possibly starring in the Red Rising movie. Maybe it's seeing him play a District 12 kid in Sunrise on the Reaping that makes it easier for me to envision him as a lowRed with a score to settle. There are a lot of sides to Darrow, especially when we factor in the teen that he is at the start of Red Rising, and the transition (and drama) he goes through in the first book. I can see Zada tackling that arc really well.

According to recent reports, nah. I can't even picture it... but it'd be fun to see his take on the role.

I'm going to cross Pax off the list right away. Even if Zada bulked up a lot for the part, I picture a guy with the size and personality of a jovial (or ferocious, when necessary) bear for the youngest Telemanus son. However, Roque would be an interesting option. I don't think Zada fits how I imagine Roque to look, but I do think he'd have an interesting take on the thoughtful character.

The last person I considered was The Jackal. While his role in the first book is fairly limited -- he's present more by reputation than he actually is on page -- he does get one of the most memorable scenes, and after playing the hero in the Hunger Games movie, I really wouldn't mind seeing what Zada does with a dark and twisty character like The Jackal.

Whether or not Zada gets cast in the Red Rising movie remains to be seen, but he does seem like a great candidate for a role, and from what he told Xtra, it sounds like he's interested in being involved.

Breaking: Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Recent findings suggest that luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Recent findings suggest that luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

It has been revealed that dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He states to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

In Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a major blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy demonstrated me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” claims Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she indicates. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

In a recent development, of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” indicates Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” notes Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

Sources indicate that when Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she claims. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”.

Taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” claims Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” states Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

It has been revealed that for Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she indicates. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most vital for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

Remember, folks: People will come and go, life will always find a way to kick you while you're down, but the whale? The whale is forever. Ever since the project was first revealed, "Whalefall" remained a fixture in our most anticipated film of 2026 ... and the movie adaptation most definitely lived up to the hype, at least according to, uh, myself. Who wouldn't be interested in the story of a scuba diver with some serious daddy issues getting caught up in a life-or-death struggle between a sperm whale and a squid, ending up swallowed whole by the aforementioned whale, and needing to find a way to escape before his oxygen supply runs out? Though the original Daniel Kraus novel was previously considered an unadaptable work, writer/director Brian Duffield found a way, and the results speak for themselves.

Of course, that was the experience of watching "Whalefall" on the significant screen. What about at home? Fans who found themselves gasping for breath, shielding their eyes, and otherwise staving off panic attacks in theaters (or was that just me?) can now see if the experience translates to the comforting confines of your own living room. 20th Century Studios has announced that "Whalefall" will swim towards a digital PVOD release on December 1, 2026. Those who rent or purchase a digital copy from the online retailer of their choice will also get an exclusive bonus feature (a terrible home media trend we've spoken out on before) in the form of a "Creature Design Audio Commentary" featuring production designer Ramsey Avery and VFX supervisor Guillaume Rocheron.

Fortunately, viewers can look forward to the film's upcoming release on physical media early in the latest year as well.

If you ended up asking yourself "How the heck did they even do that?" every five minutes while watching "Whalefall," we have some excellent news. The ambitious film that once again puts poor Austin Abrams through the wringer after this year's "Resident Evil" won't just be available to watch at home in less time than it takes to be digested by a whale (don't quote me on that fact), it will also come loaded with extras, bonus features, and other goodies for the eager film enthusiast. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • If your feed is full of clips and streams from people who’ve already gone deep into Grand Theft Auto 6, here’s some reassurance: most players aren’t as far along as you probably think.
  • It has been revealed that according to PSNProfiles, only 66.22% of Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PlayStation 5 have earned the trophy for completing Chapter 1, which takes place in the Leonida Keys.
  • Meanwhile, only 40.55% of players have cleared Chapter 2 on PS5, and 31% on Xbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If your feed is full of clips and streams from people who’ve already gone deep into Grand Theft Auto 6, here’s some reassurance: most players aren’t as far along as you probably think.

It has been revealed that according to PSNProfiles, only 66.22% of Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PlayStation 5 have earned the trophy for completing Chapter 1, which takes place in the Leonida Keys. The numbers on Xbox are similar, with 56% of players having beaten that part of the game, according to TrueAchievements. This completion percentage feels particularly significant because the first chapter of the game is a significant departure from classic GTA, with Jason living out a relatively low-key existence interrupted by the occasional shootout with backwoods drug dealers. Still, it seems a solid chunk of players are more than happy fishing with Cal for now.

Meanwhile, only 40.55% of players have cleared Chapter 2 on PS5, and 31% on Xbox. Again, considering that Chapter 3 is arguably where the game becomes more of a traditional Grand Theft Auto entry, as you officially enter Vice City, it’s a bit of a surprise that the numbers are so low, even if it takes close to 20 hours to get there.

As for the rest of the game, few have gotten past Chapter 3: 6.45% have cleared that chapter on PS5, compared to 4% on Xbox; 1.26% have cleared Chapter 4 on PS5 against 1% on Xbox; and a tiny 0.88% have cleared the final mission on PlayStation against fewer than 1% on Xbox.

It has been revealed that although it’s tempting to assume these low completion numbers are simply because the game came out so recently, Sony released player engagement numbers that made it clear most have already put a ton of time into GTA 6. Mat Piscatella, senior director at market research firm Circana, revealed that players spent an average of more than 8 hours playing the game on launch day. As of Nov. 23, PS5 players had already spent an average of 17.4 hours playing. While users are playing a lot and sticking with the game, most are taking their time. Rockstar previously said the main story takes around 50 hours to finish.

Shortly after GTA 6 was released, publisher Take-Two Interactive announced that the game had set a “new record for entertainment across any medium,” making it the biggest launch in entertainment history. It sold 32.5 million copies during its pre-release period, generating $3.79 billion in revenue. In the previously mentioned post that announced PlayStation engagement numbers, Sony also noted GTA 6 was the biggest launch in PlayStation history and that 39 million people had played it on the PS5 as of Monday.

Sources indicate that as for its critical reception, the game has a staggering Metacritic score of 99, tying it with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — the Nintendo 64 version — for the highest-rated game of all time. By every metric, GTA 6 has been a cultural event.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While playing as one character in GTA 6, you have the option to invite your partner to hang out with you.
  • In a recent development, but keeping Jason and Lucia together has some less obvious benefits, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, even after clearing Grand Theft Auto 6’s long story, I keep finding myself drawn back to Leonida. That’s thanks in large part to Jason and Lucia, a pair of charismatic protagonists that I genuinely enjoy spending time with. While you can treat them as independent characters and take them out on solo adventures, GTA 6 shines brightest when you travel around Leonida as a pair. In fact, you’re bound to miss a whole lot if you aren’t letting Jason and Lucia enjoy a date from time to time.

While playing as one character in GTA 6, you have the option to invite your partner to hang out with you. (This feature unlocks partway through Chapter 2 of the story.) If you’re playing as Jason, for instance, you could text Lucia and ask if she wants to hang out, prompting her to drive to your location. You can coordinate crimes this way too; if you find a bank you want to rob, you can ping Jason and tell him to meet Lucia at the spot to pull off the job together. There are a lot of benefits to working together, as heists will become easier and you’ll be able to ask your partner to run off and fence any goods you grab.

In a recent development, but keeping Jason and Lucia together has some less obvious benefits, too. When the two explore together, they’ll occasionally break out into natural conversations. One time while driving through Lummox County listening to a country radio station, Lucia talked about how she thought the genre was a joke growing up. A little odd couple exchange ensued, where Jason talked about how much he loves country music. Later, upon finding a stray bicycle, Lucia told Jason about the time she tried to ride a bike as a kid and crashed into an ice cream truck.

There are even entire running gags that you’ll only hear while playing together. One recurring bit involves Lucia constantly answering spam robocalls and gradually losing her cool over them. That culminates in her giving the AI voice a firm thrashing, while Jason chuckles from the sidelines. Those bits of contextual chatter help make Jason and Lucia feel like an authentic couple rather than voiceless pawns to be moved around.

It has been revealed that more importantly, crucial story details can come out of those moments. One time while exploring a swamp in search of Skunk Ape effigies (weird game!), Jason and Lucia broke out into a conversation about their family dynamics. It started when Jason mentioned Lucia’s mother doesn’t like him very much. After a bit of unconvincing denial, Lucia admitted that there’s truth to Jason’s anxiety: Lucia lied to her mother, saying that Jason essentially walked out on her and their child. That revelation triggered a conversation where Lucia recalled a moment where Jason once told her he didn’t want children, which is why she initially didn’t tell Jason about their son. It’s an crucial moment that gives depth to Jason and Lucia’s history and fills in some questions about why Tommy was kept secret for so long.

It has been revealed that so, if you’ve been exploring Leonida solo for most of your GTA 6 playthrough, make sure to invite your partner to hang out regularly. You’ll miss some of the best human moments in the game if you do, and you’ll understand each character so much more by listening to their chatter. And, of course, you’ll also be able to send Jason off with a bag full of cocaine if you don’t want to trek back to Vice City to sell it.

Industry observers note that in 2014, Skyler Gisondo joined the Night at the Museum franchise to play Ben Stiller’s son, Nick Daley. While he’d worked a lot as a kid before that, this role marked a turning point in his career. Now, he’s reteaming with Stiller for Focker In-Law on the 2026 movie schedule, and he’s playing his son…again. So, considering that, I asked the Superman actor how his first time playing Stiller’s kid impacted his work in the Meet the Parents franchise, and he told me why it was a very full-circle experience.

As a Meet the Parents and Night at the Museum fan, I couldn’t get enough of this reunion. It was also fun to see Stiller and Gisondo reunite now, because I’ve become such a massive fan of the work the Booksmart actor did between Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb and Focker In-Law. So, I asked Gisondo how his history with Stiller played into this experience on Focker In-Law; he remarked:.

It was great. I mean, Night at the Museum was such a formative experience for me. I was 17. It was my first time being a bigger part of a bigger movie like that. And Ben really took me under his wing then, and was so good to me. And I think I had almost forgotten how much I took from that time.

Again, while Skyler Gisondo was a successful child actor, Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb (which you can watch with a Disney+ subscription) was a turning point for him. It makes sense that he learned a lot from Stiller on it that has impacted his career since.

According to recent reports, speaking of his career, after Night at the Museum, Gisondo booked roles in projects like Vacation, Santa Clarita Diet, Booksmart and more. Also, his last couple of years leading up to his reunion with Stiller have been fantastic. He played the beloved Jimmy Olsen in James Gunn’s Superman, he finished the final season of The Righteous Gemstones, and he was a standout alongside Robert Pattinson in Primetime. Truly, he has become quite the actor, and he’s one of my favorite rising stars.

So, to hear that Stiller impacted him is really sweet. What makes it even sweeter is that while working on Focker In-Law, Gisondo realized all this as he started to notice that some of the things he does as an actor are things Stiller does too:.

And then getting reunited on this, like 12 years later, there was all these things I would notice Ben doing before takes or something, and realize that I've done that my whole adult life. And I kind of had forgotten where I’d gotten it from or something. And I think it was really helpful for this movie to have that kind of built-in familial sort of relationship.

Knowing about Stiller and Gisondo’s history certainly played into my enjoyment of the movie, especially since the last time I saw them together, Gisondo was a kid. Now, he’s all grown up, and that fact certainly plays into Focker In-Law.

To that point, in Focker In-Law, we follow Greg Focker (Stiller) as he reunites with his family, including his son Henry (Gisondo). Things get chaotic because Henry brings home his girlfriend, Olivia (Ariana Grande), and he plans to propose to her. After that, we dive into a lot of chaos as Greg butts heads with Henry’s partner, and obviously it leads to some very funny familial hijinks. It’s silly, and it was such a fun way to see the Night at the Museum actors work together again all these years later.

Tech Report: The Witcher 4 Will Be a GTA 6-Sized Leap Forward, CD Projekt Red Indicates

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (542 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We're living in a post-Grand Theft Auto 6 world now, meaning that almost every other game in development will inevitably be compared to Rockstar Games' new open-world crime drama.
  • It has been revealed that during an earnings call on Tuesday, CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski addressed the Leonida-sized elephant in the room: how GTA 6 will influence his tech giant's upcoming games, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.
  • "Of course, we did look at the game," Nowakowski said of GTA 6, adding, "We did see the differences" between it and 2013's Grand Theft Auto 5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're living in a post-Grand Theft Auto 6 world now, meaning that almost every other game in development will inevitably be compared to Rockstar Games' new open-world crime drama. The developer behind two other big open-world brands, The Witcher and Cyberpunk, is now fielding questions about how its future games will stack up against GTA 6.

It has been revealed that during an earnings call on Tuesday, CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski addressed the Leonida-sized elephant in the room: how GTA 6 will influence his tech giant's upcoming games, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2. Nowakowski said that he believes The Witcher 4 will deliver a GTA 6-like leap forward for players.

"Of course, we did look at the game," Nowakowski said of GTA 6, adding, "We did see the differences" between it and 2013's Grand Theft Auto 5. "We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4. It's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So, yes, you should expect us to make a much, much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

Sources indicate that "We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4] and Cyberpunk 2," he stated. "They have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.".

Nowakowski also addressed The Witcher 4's through the lens of GTA 6's budget. Rockstar's latest release is rumored to have a development budget of more than $1 billion, and Nowakowski categorized CD Projekt Red's upcoming games as not having "budget-driven developments.".

It has been revealed that "I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets. We do," he mentioned. "I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind This is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise we’re gone. They're ambition-driven developments and money's notable. The budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that.".

It has been revealed that as for other lessons learned from GTA 6's massive launch, Nowakowski noted that "If you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of the core main gaming bubble, [which is] something we did achieve in the past as well. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach. But in terms of the ultimate effect in terms of breaking out to the mass market, awareness, this is something we consider critical.".

In other words, while CD Projekt Red may take some cues from Rockstar Games, it's not trying to copy the Grand Theft Auto developer's homework.

In a recent development, the Witcher 4 is slated for release in 2028. Cyberpunk 2 does not have an announced release window.

Hexed Review: A Safe And Solidly Witchy Disney Original

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that some of us grew up dreaming of becoming princesses and knights in fairy tales, others of becoming astronauts (or in my case, uh, the guy who gets to drive the garbage truck).
  • The wish-fulfillment of it all probably explains why this makes for such a neat premise in a movie like "Hexed" ...
  • Industry observers note that because being a witch isn't all fun and games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that some of us grew up dreaming of becoming princesses and knights in fairy tales, others of becoming astronauts (or in my case, uh, the guy who gets to drive the garbage truck). Only the coolest — and weirdest — kids among us imagined themselves slapping on some eyeshadow, living it up from atop flying brooms, and casting gnarly spells. Who else but witches can transform the rigidly bland world around us into one positively teeming with magic and color and life?

The wish-fulfillment of it all probably explains why this makes for such a neat premise in a movie like "Hexed" ... even if that potential isn't fully realized. Disney's latest animated original, from directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand and co-director Josie Trinidad, is mostly content to play things safe and deliver a fairly predictable coming-of-age story. While this family-friendly, PG-rated romp doesn't linger too much on the darkness inherent in witches, there's an undeniable undercurrent of something much more provocative at work.

Industry observers note that because being a witch isn't all fun and games. Along with strong personalities and powers beyond compare, they also come with the baggage of being profoundly misunderstood. Their curse is to be loners, outcasts, and pariahs, forever looking for a coven to call their own. Whenever the script by co-writers Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller fully leans into this, embodied by misfit high schooler Billie Doe (voiced by the always-capable Hailee Steinfeld) in search of a deeper sense of belonging, "Hexed" takes on a life of its own. When relying on frenetic pacing and joke-a-minute thrills to sweep us along and glide past any discomfort, it struggles to come together.

According to recent reports, there's a greater movie somewhere inside "Hexed," just waiting to break free. Instead, we're left with a safe and solid enough adventure that could've been something more.

Sources indicate that right from the opening exposition dump of "Hexed," we're taken through a prototypical backstory of how witches were chased out of "normal" society and forced to create a mystical refuge of their own called Hexe. Unfortunately, the founding witch died before she could complete this upcoming utopia, dooming her followers to wait for the prophesied "Chosen One" to cast a spell known only to themselves and restore everyone's powers to their fullest. ("The foretelling was foretold," as numerous characters amusingly reference this event.).

In a recent development, this intersects neatly with Billie's arc, our rule-breaking teenager with latent witchy powers whose mother Alice (the rather obvious voice-casting of Rashida Jones) has hidden away from the world and from her supposed destiny. When Billie's abilities manifest as an infant and nearly spirit her away to Hexe, Alice takes great pains to hide her daughter's true origins from herself — even to the point of moving out of Salem altogether and into the blandest, most unassuming place on Earth to pass as an unremarkable normie (Ohio). All in all, it's a pretty standard setup for a parable about identity, puberty, and being yourself (alongside a hint of queer subtext), which "Hexed" pulls off with the appropriate amount of emotional, tear-jerker aplomb.

Industry observers note that but otherwise, this is largely an excuse to show off the film's stunning world-building prowess. Yes, Hexe oftentimes tends to resemble Universal's Wizarding World of Harry Potter. But once Billie finally makes it to this living and breathing realm — marked by an expanding aspect ratio to soak in the full scope of Hexe — and assembles unlikely allies like an enchanted pot, Walton Goggins' cat-like and delightfully-named familiar Beef Roger Crummchuk, and neurotic owl Nigel (Henry Winkler), you'll never want to leave this kaleidoscopic wonderland.

Recent findings suggest that where "Hexed" struggles most, ironically, is in its attempt to carve out a niche for itself amid the vast canon of Disney's animated movies. On one hand, it's strangely fitting for a story about individualism to be so preoccupied by what's come before. On the other, it has the side effect of triggering a tangible identity crisis. At this point, Disney's house-style CG animation has been set in stone and nothing here diverges all that much from the likes of "Frozen" — down to the look of the film's main villain Queen Celeste, brought to life by a scenery-chewing Jodie Foster. Elsewhere, some of the imagery of Hexe itself feel cribbed from classics like "Cinderella" or "Fantasia," coming across less like a loving homage and more like a copy of a copy. Even Kris Bowers' distinctive score is overshadowed by a parade of on-the-nose needle drops, from Queen to Dua Lipa.

This has the cumulative effect of making "Hexed" an oddly meta experience, in a way that both livens things up and makes for a somewhat awkward addition to the Disney pantheon. Much of the humor comes from the script's winking self-awareness and its many "Can you believe this?" visual gags, which could've fell flat on their face but instead (mostly) work. But even its most inspired moments of creativity and imagination feel undercut by a script that's either unwilling or unable to push such boundaries beyond its most surface-level joys.

Still, parents could do far worse than "Hexed" when it comes to movies their children will inevitably re-watch a million times over once it comes to Disney+. While that might seem like damning with faint praise, it does speak to the basics of storytelling that directors Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand, and Josie Trinidad manage to get right — especially within a noticeably tight, 103-minute runtime. For all intents and purposes, this breezy storyline might as well be designed to function like a runaway train, constantly keeping the action at a sprinter's pace and hardly giving young viewers a chance to catch their breath. Even the "camera" stays in motion at almost all times and makes the few, much-needed moments of respite and quiet conversation stand out all the more.

This "Get in, get out" approach at least provides a jolt of energy right from the get-go and carries the emotions along with it, even if it can occasionally get exhausting. At its heart, "Hexed" lives or dies by the mother/daughter bond forged between impulsive Billie and overbearing Alice, and its best moments soar as direct result of never losing sight of these two characters.

There are plenty of narrative holes left oddly unexplained and an unfortunate bit of sequel-bait sweatiness to contend with, likely included in the off-chance this kills it at the box office. (This raises another question, of course: Was holding this Halloween-friendly movie about spooky witches closer to the extended Thanksgiving holiday weekend really worth it?) But thanks to dazzling visuals, a strong emotional undercurrent, and killer world-building, "Hexed" is a solid — if safe — family outing.

"Hexed" opens in theaters on November 25, 2026.

GTA 6 Has A Secret Mission That Feels Like Hard Target Meets Saw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the mood for a little bloodsport?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again. Breaking: What Happened To Harrison Ford’s Deckard After Blade Runner 2049? I Asked 2099’s EP For Her Take

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2049, in my humble opinion, is a science-fiction masterpiece. The Denis Villeneuve-directed sequel not only expertly builds upon Ridley Scott’s 1982 film, but it also adds to the mythology in interesting ways. Additionally, the film includes a stellar performance from Harrison Ford, who reprises his role as Rick Deckard. In the near decade since the film’s release, I’ve been wondering about Deckard’s ultimate fate. So, when CinemaBlend spoke to the creator of Blade Runner 2099, I asked for her take.

In a recent development, deckard serves as more of a supporting character in Villeneuve’s heavily praised film, which reveals the former Blade Runner to be in hiding in the ruins of Las Vegas 30 years after the events of the OG film. Found by Replicant Runner K (Ryan Gosling), Deckard is eventually revealed to have fathered a child with his late replicant partner, Rachel. That child is eventually revealed to be replicant-memory-maker Dr. Ana Stelline (Carla Juri), with whom Deckard reunites at the end of the film, thanks to K.

Recent findings suggest that since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants. Blade Runner 2099 creator/showrunner Silka Luisa is also a major fan of the franchise and, when she was asked for her take on what happened to Ana and Deckard, she shared some surprising comments with CB:.

According to recent reports, I never asked Michael Green, because I'm sure — he was the screenwriter for 2049, and there's just no world [where] he didn't know what happens. But I almost didn't want to know. What I love about Blade Runner is that so much of it can exist in your own mind, and the world feels so rich that it inspires you to create your own stories within it. And something about that period not being totally defined is exciting, because we can all suggest different things. Yeah, so I don't have a definitive answer.

Considering how big a Blade Runner fan Luisa is, I’m honestly shocked over her not asking Michael Green (who shares 2049 writing credits with Hampton Fancher) for a definitive answer on Deckard and Ana. I can, however, also see Luisa’s point, though, as this franchise does leave certain plot threads open-ended, leading to fan speculation. This answer also tracks with the EP’s approach to 2099, which is a standalone piece that doesn’t have direct references to its big-screen predecessors.

While Blade Runner’s ending remains controversial in some circles, the discussions surrounding 2049’s conclusion arguably aren’t as tense. Villeneuve’s film went through different alterations during development, and even the ending changed. Fancher previously disclosed that the original plan was for Deckard to die. While that could’ve been powerful (if crafted effectively), I’m fine with Deckard not biting the significant one, considering it leaves the door open for a direct sequel. And Silka Luisa is down for that as well:.

It has been revealed that I really hope they make another. I really hope they make a sequel, just as a fan, to be honest.

In a recent development, for right now, though, fans can return to this dark, futuristic universe by way of 2099. The limited series centers on dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human posing as a Replicant. While fans won’t be getting answers on Deckard, the show covers plenty of ground in other respects. And, who knows, maybe we’ll actually get that 2049 sequel one day.

It has been revealed that all episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will begin streaming for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25 amid the 2026 TV schedule. Blade Runner 2049 can also currently be streamed on Prime, and it’s available to watch for free on Tubi.

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

#97230. GTA 6's Staggering Sales Still Might Never Catch GTA 5

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (790 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Polygon ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6's Staggering Sales Still Might Never Catch GTA 5

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Friday, Rockstar Games' parent firm Take-Two Interactive declared sales figures for Grand Theft Auto 6 that are so dizzying, I'm still processing them.
  • Take-Two mentioned that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies during its pre-release period, and that through the end of launch day on Nov.
  • Comparisons are fun to make, but apt ones don't really exist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Friday, Rockstar Games' parent firm Take-Two Interactive declared sales figures for Grand Theft Auto 6 that are so dizzying, I'm still processing them. They have clearly shattered preorder records for video games and launch sales — in fact, total sales – for just about any form of entertainment.

Take-Two mentioned that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies during its pre-release period, and that through the end of launch day on Nov. 19, it had racked up $3.79 billion in revenue.

Comparisons are fun to make, but apt ones don't really exist. On its day of launch, GTA 6 had made twice as much money as Taylor Swift's entire Eras tour, and more than any film has ever made across a full theatrical run. Alinea Analytics reckons that by the end of the weekend the numbers were up to 44.9 million copies sold and a round $4 billion in revenue. It took GTA 6 one day to eclipse the lifetime sales figures of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.

It has been revealed that here's a more meaningful comparison: Grand Theft Auto 5 took three days to hit $1 billion in sales. GTA 6's launch is four times bigger than its predecessor's. It will definitely crush GTA 5's lifetime record, right? Well… not necessarily.

According to recent reports, as amazing as GTA 6's sales are, it has a long, long way to go to catch up with its major brother. GTA 5 is the second-best selling game of all time behind Minecraft (or third-best, depending on how you account for sales of Tetris). It has sold a staggering 235 million copies to date, more than two and a half times as many as the next game in the all-time ranking, Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2.

When it comes to long-tail, long-term sales, GTA 5 is in a different class entirely — a class of two, alongside Minecraft. It's not a given that GTA 6 will necessarily be able to join this class. A few things have to fall into place.

Rockstar has yet to confirm a PC version of the game, for starters, though one is expected in 2027. That will unlock a whole newly introduced audience for GTA 6, especially globally, and supercharge its sales again.

Industry observers note that rockstar has also yet to confirm that it will create a GTA 6 version of GTA Online. GTA 5's scrappy multiplayer mode became a live-service behemoth that has driven a huge proportion of those 235 million sales, and that financially sustained Rockstar through the extremely long and expensive developments of Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 6. Analysts also seem confident in predicting GTA 6's online mode will arrive in 2027, although I think a degree of skepticism is warranted on that part.

Rockstar hasn't mentioned one word publicly about GTA 6 Online for good reason. Migrating online gaming audiences, who’ve invested massive amounts of time and money in their accounts, from one game to a sequel is notoriously difficult. It's why there was never a World of Warcraft 2, for example, and there are vanishingly few examples of it being done successfully (Destiny 2 being, perhaps, the exception that proves the rule).

According to recent reports, this is not to say that Rockstar won't do it, but the studio will need to be extremely careful and consider its strategy. Will it lock the latest online mode behind a full purchase of GTA 6, as it initially did with its predecessor? Sell it separately and/or bundle it in a GTA Plus subscription, as it now does for GTA Online? Or maybe even go free-to-play? These approaches all have their advantages and drawbacks when it comes to tempting GTA Online players to upgrade and maximizing the new online game's revenue, but only one of them is going to help GTA 6 sell as many copies as GTA 5.

There's a final but key asterisk to consider with respect to GTA 5's astonishing sales. It has been released across three console generations, and a lot of those purchases will be duplicates or even triplicates (which is especially true for GTA Online players).

In other words, the sales figures are likely flattering to the maximum size of the GTA audience; I don't think there are 235 million GTA players out there. It's going to be challenging for GTA 6 to meet that number unless it, too, spans three generations. I hope we won't be waiting until late in the PlayStation 7's life for GTA 7, but you never know with Rockstar.

One thing's for sure: Rockstar's only real competition is itself. GTA 6 has had the biggest launch imaginable. Can it also go the distance?

If You're Tired Of Colleen Hoover Movies, Watch This Overlooked 2026 Rom-Com
