With "You, Me & Tuscany" he embraced his more tender side with a story of a young cook who finds love in the titular Italian region.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that colleen Hoover is the reigning queen of BookTok-phenomenon-turned-movie entertainment. The woman just has a knack for writing the kinds of books that might not get a lot of critical love but which social media crowds cannot resist. Thus far, that has resulted in four Colleen Hoover movie adaptations. Unfortunately, none of them are very good. At least, the critics didn't like them. Audiences, on the other hand, keep showing up. Following the less than enthusiastic response to the latest Hoover movie, "Verity," however, even fans might be in need of a break. In which case, might I suggest "You, Me & Tuscany," directed by Kat Coiro.

According to recent reports, corio previously helmed the 2022 glossy rom-com relic "Marry Me" starring Jennifer Lopez and Owen Wilson. Like your standard Hoover affair, it movie earned an okay 61% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes, but managed to push the "popcornmeter" to 92%, meaning audiences absolutely loved Coiro's movie — which was based on a webcomic.

In 2026, Coiro — who also directed several episodes of "She-Hulk: Attorney at Law" — returned with another romantic comedy: "You, Me & Tuscany," an original story written by Ryan Engle, who, oddly enough, has mostly written actioners such as the Idris-Elba-vs.-a-lion survival horror "Beast" and the Liam Neeson outing that was 2014's "Non-Stop." With "You, Me & Tuscany" he embraced his more tender side with a story of a young cook who finds love in the titular Italian region.

Industry observers note that "You, Me & Tuscany" stars Halle Bailey ("The Little Mermaid") as Anna, a young woman who after losing her house-sitting job, meets a strapping Italian named Matteo Costa (Lorenzo de Moor). Following their brief encounter, Anna decides to fly to Italy and manages to find a spare key to Matteo's empty Tuscan villa. There, Matteo's mother, Gabriella (Isabella Ferrari) arrives and Anna decides to lie and tell her that she's Matteo's fiancé.

It might seem as though "You, Me & Tuscany" is yet another fake dating rom-com, whereby a feigned romance becomes real. But the movie diverges from that well-worn path when Matteo's cousin, Michael (Regé-Jean Page) arrives and there's an instant attraction between he and Anna.

Page is, of course, best known for playing Simon Basset, the Duke of Hastings, in Season 1 of Netflix's hugely-popular series "Bridgerton." But he's since enjoyed a successful film career and is swiftly making a name for himself in Hollywood. Page's Simon Basset left "Bridgerton" after the first season, after which the actor appeared in "Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves," and in Steven Soderbergh's sleek spy thriller "Black Bag." With "You, Me & Tuscany" he further proved he has leading man chops. Otherwise, however, the movie doesn't do much to separate it from the glut of sort-of-okay romance movies with which we've been inundated in recent years. But it has at least outdone every Colleen Hoover movie on Rotten Tomatoes.

It has been revealed that the latest Colleen Hoover movie was the dead-on-arrival "Verity," which no doubt left many viewers disappointed in the lack of straightforward romance. Much of the movie features Anne Hathaway glaring silently at Dakota Johnson from a medical bed or wheelchair. "You, Me and Tuscany" on the other hand should delight those hoping for more schmaltzy romance in the vein of Lili Reinhart's Prime Video smash hit "The Love Hypothesis" or Sofia Carson's similarly popular Netflix romance "My Oxford Year.".

Over on Rotten Tomatoes, it's a familiar state of affairs. "You, Me & Tuscany" earned a somewhat respectable 65% critic score while managing to push the "popcornmeter" all the way to 91%. This is the rom-com pattern of late. Audiences clearly got what they came for here, even if Nikki Gemmell of The Australian called the movie "the filmic equivalent of paint by numbers, lift muzak, Fruit Loops, Contiki Tours and The Voice," essentially "anything that feels bland, inauthentic and deeply commercial." Sadly, this is just where we are in 2026. We used to make rom-coms like "Sleepless in Seattle" and "When Harry Met Sally." Not anymore.

"You, Me & Tuscany," however, isn't the worst example of the modern day rom-com (Netflix's "The Wrong Paris" might have claimed that title in 2025). If you happen to be looking for a Hoover palette cleanser that also isn't too far removed from the author's BookTok-friendly brand of romance, then this one's worth a go. "You, Me & Tuscany" is right now available to rent from the usual platforms, and can be streamed via Peacock with a premium subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, not even porn is immune to the GTA 6 effect, as it's just one of several forms of entertainment that has seen a decline in viewership since the massive open-world game introduced. It's not surprising, given the game's record-breaking start, with 32.5 million sales from preorders alone. On PS5, GTA 6 is the "biggest launch" in PlayStation history, and players spent an average of 17.4 hours playing in its first few days--which probably didn't leave much time for a quick browse of after-hours material. According to Mashable, US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically, Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely indicating that people were bored and randy. Pornhub traffic started to fluctuate after the GTA 6 launch and reached an average peak a few days later. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c Thanks to the game's massive success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries were made on November 18 alone, with people searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low. Thursday Night Football also saw a big dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's upcoming open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. For more GTA 6 news, you can read up on how modders are attempting to make an unofficial PC port, how to fix GTA 6's broken HDR, and you can check out our list of walkthroughs in the GTA 6 guides hub.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Inside the NBA’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his plans to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Industry observers note that barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside. The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube) and, when asked about the job, he said this:.

It has been revealed that I love Charles and yes, that would be something that I would be interested in. The one thing I learned about this business is everything isn't transactional. If Charles Barkley is going to say into a microphone that you're the person that he feels like should replace him, you can't write a check for that. Even if it never happens. And so, for him to say that, it's priceless. I'm so very gracious.

The notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside, and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal. With that said, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

It has been revealed that inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley). Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

Sources indicate that again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

Sources indicate that to be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely, he hasn’t noted much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

Check out Inside the NBA when it returns to NBA on Wednesday, November 25 amid the 2026 TV schedule.

WoW: Forever’s Best Buffs Now Work As Intended

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1256 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.
  • World Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended. World Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the Horde and the upcoming Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest. Now that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP. Unfortunately, players haven't been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be removed. That has finally been fixed in the latest revision, so players can now enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable. Blizzard clarified in the patch notes that World Buffs will still be removed when entering raids, so players won't be able to stack as many World Buffs as possible before raid night, as was the case in previous versions of classic WoW. Other changes found in the patch notes include a fix for an Uldaman boss that players were exploiting to make fast gold. Another is a fix for "a few spells and abilities" that were causing more weapon-proc effects than intended, likely nerfing the DPS of whatever classes were taking advantage of the bug. You can read the full patch notes below. Blizzard recently outlined in the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast how it wants to get rid of the idea of "best-in-slot gear," as well as how the game's has overhauled old-school WoW's player-vs.-player systems. In other Forever news, the game's launch has seen more than 15 million characters created so far, with the highest weekly player numbers for WoW in 15 years. WoW: Forever November 23 Hotfix Patch Notes Classes Druid The 4-piece Feralheart set for Druids now correctly grants 4 Energy regeneration every 1 second for 5 seconds. Priest Mind Vision should no longer proc effects. Shadow Fixed an issue where Dark Inspiration was not granting the correct amount of %Spirit increase if Mind Flay was used to activate it. Fixed an issue where Chastise was not usable in Shadowform. Warlock Destruction Fixed an issue where Intensity was not working on Incinerate. Warrior Fixed an issue where players could have and use Mortal Strike from their spellbook, even without the Mortal Strike talent. This does not remove it from their spellbook but prevents it from being used without the talent point spent. Dungeons Uldaman The Obsidian Sentinel drops loot as intended. Items The Filcher’s Cowl no longer has a level requirement. Professions Cooking Boiled Clams, Clam Chowder, Goblin Deviled Clams, Giant Clam Scorcho, Undermine Clam Chowder, and Clam Linguine each now offer the correct Well Fed bonuses and have been recategorized in the recipe list under “Stamina Food”. Murloc Fin Soup has had its recovery and Well-Fed amounts increased to the next tier of food, bringing it closer to other food of that level. Engineering Fixed a bug that caused Goblin Engineer’s Renewal Gift and Gnome Engineer’s Renewal Gift to appear as broken, unusable question marks in the inventory. Fixed a bug that prevented “The Mortar: Reloaded” recipe from being learned upon learning the “Goblin Mortar” recipe. Leatherworking Fixed a bug that prevented Pattern: Centaur Hoofwarmers from being learnable. Quests Riverglades - Dunston Willis once again runs near the end of the escort “Dunston Checks Out.” Wetlands - After further study, the quest “For Further Study” now has rewards. Wetlands - The quest “Uncovering the Past” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Wetlands - The quest “Gleaning Our Future” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Races Fixed an issue where Wisp Form could be applied to players while they were alive. Spells Fixed an issue where a few spells and abilities were causing more weapon procs than intended. Fixed an issue where World Buffs would fall off when changing areas. They will still fall off when entering raid instances. Fixed an issue where Fengus’ Ferocity was granting twice as much Spell Power as intended. Fixed an issue where Darkmoon Faire buffs were granting twice as much power as intended.

Now that he's free of "Stranger Things," we're going to find out if Noah Schnapp can fulfill the promise he flashed over five seasons of the Netflix sci-fi/horror series. His character, Will Byers, had arguably the most emotional arc of the show, with viewers watching him go from missing boy to psychically tortured returnee from the Upside Down to out and proud young adult. Byers' journey mirrored Schnapp's personal voyage to coming out of the closet in 2025. It was a lovely moment for Schnapp, both as an individual and also for his character, who presented a positive gay role model for kids who too often struggle with prejudice and outright hatred in their everyday lives.

According to recent reports, I've no idea if Schnapp will return to the "Stranger Things" universe (he's only just portrayed a disaffected rich kid and, when the plot jumps forward 20 years, the kid's son in Andy Sandberg's controversial stage play "Affluenza"), but he had a shot at joining the "Hunger Games" franchise as a young Haymitch Abernathy in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." The "Hunger Games" prequel is right now tearing up the box office, so it would've been a sweet gig for the 22-year-old actor. But he congratulated Joseph Zada like a gentleman for landing the role, and, as an egoless bonus, the brunette Schnapp posted a still picture of himself in blonde hair from his screen test to Instagram. (See below.).

Recent findings suggest that after a couple of ... emojis, Schnapp tagged Zada and added, "Think they picked right for this one.".

I have no true measure of Noah Schnapp as an actor. He's handsome, he's got some mystery to him and, in the right role (e.g. Will Byers), he connects. Do I think he would've been an effective Haymitch Abernathy, given all the horrible things that happen to the character on his way to growing up and becoming Woody Harrelson? Maybe not.

"Affluenza" ended its London run on November 21, and, boy, did the critics lay into this sucker. In a one-star review for The Guardian, Arifa Akbar called it an "epic wreckage," adding, "You want to look away, for shame, but simply can't stop gawping." Most critics concurred, but that actually worked out for Schnapp, as they were too busy lambasting Sandberg to pay much attention to his performance. Writing for The Times, Clive Davis simply noted that Schnapp "doesn't disgrace himself." If you get cast in a disaster, you can live with that.

It has been revealed that it's unclear where Schnapp will go from here, but thanks to "Stranger Things" he has a pretty sizable fan base. I can't see him being a part of the forthcoming series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure," which is a prequel set in the 1950s, but we'll certainly see more of him in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a strategy for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”.

It has been revealed that the proposal was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is noted to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”.

Recent findings suggest that by implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Recent findings suggest that under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

It has been revealed that they may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could problem letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”.

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”.

Shane Gillis’ ex-girlfriend Grace Brassel is pulling back the curtain on what she claims was their rocky relationship, revealing the alleged “red flags” she wishes she didn’t overlook.

“Until last August, I was in a year-long relationship with Shane, and his comments didn’t faze me,” Brassel wrote in an essay for The Cut, published on Tuesday, November 24, admitting she wasn’t surprised by Gillis’ controversialSaturday Night Live monologue last month in which he called women “whores” for wearing shorts to the gym.

Brassel revealed in her essay, “After our time together, how do I think he feels about women? He doesn’t like them much.”.

In a recent development, she explained in the story that she slid into Gillis’ DMs in 2024 after seeing him on Netflix’s Tires. She was in her early 20s, had a TikTok following and was working as a social-media manager when Gillis, now 38, responded to her message, requesting her phone number.

“We started texting, which turned into daily phone calls, which turned into an invitation to meet in person in Austin,” Brassel recalled, noting she was “too afraid” to tell her mom she was flying to Texas to meet a man who was 12 years her senior.

She remembered the “dream” weekend with fondness, saying that they became “official” before she left Austin and flew back to Latest York City.

“Shane was rich, he had a cool car, and his house was lined floor to ceiling with awards. He thought I was beautiful and treated me with care,” Brassel noted of the start of their romance. “He said all the right things. … His world was so fast and extravagant. I was just happy to be part of it.”.

The pair’s second date was allegedly just as exciting, with Gillis inviting Brassel to be his date to Christian McCaffrey and Olivia Culpo’s wedding. The comedian even reportedly bought his latest girlfriend an $800 dress for the occasion.

The whirlwind romance took off from there, and after two months together Brassel agreed to move to Philadelphia with Gillis when he wrote the next season of Tires.

“Once we started living together, it was a nonstop party — Eagles’ games, long nights of drinking, hanging out with celebrities. Wash, rinse, repeat,” she wrote.

It has been revealed that during that time, Brassel had trouble keeping up with her day job, so she stated, “Shane told me I should just quit. He would take care of me, and I would take care of him. He made it seem like the most plausible option.”.

She confessed, “Little did I know I had actually just accepted a different full-time position, one that had a high rate of burnout and no chance for upward mobility: Shane Gillis’s stay-at-home girlfriend.”.

Becoming Gillis’ live-in girlfriend was one of the many “red flags” Brassel claimed she would later identify, but at the moment she was still in awe of her boyfriend’s high-profile life.

It has been revealed that “I felt plucked out of my ordinary existence like some kind of chosen one, dropped straight into the orbit of the coolest guy with the flashiest life,” she shared. “It felt like a dream. I was so excited for my and Shane’s life together that I didn’t even notice my agency was slipping through my fingers.”.

Recent findings suggest that the couple moved to West Chester, Pennsylvania, during filming for Tires, allegedly alienating Brassel even more. As Gillis filmed his show, Brassel found herself stuck at home and “turning into a 25-year-old housewife, someone who cooked, cleaned, did the laundry, and waited for her man to come home from a long day at work.”.

Brassel claimed that being a modern-day housewife “felt like an expectation” and that when things “weren’t exactly to his liking, he would tell me that I wasn’t ‘being good.’ You know, the way you would talk to a dog.”.

That was another red flag, but Brassel remarked she “ignored” it because “I really did love him.”.

Then came the rude remarks, allegedly laughed off as jokes. “Shane would often say something remarkably cruel and then play it off like a joke. He did it with me, he does it with his friends, and I saw him do it with his colleagues,” Brassel claimed. “I felt like being able to handle it made me the Wild Shane Tamer.”.

Brassel claimed that if they got into an argument or Gillis was “mad” at her, he would “withhold touch and call me greedy or put pillows in between us in the bed to show how much he didn’t want to be near me.”.

She confessed, “I was walking on eggshells so often that they began to feel like regular hardwood.”.

Five months into their relationship, Brassel noted she started to gain weight from all the drinking and continued to isolate.

Sources indicate that “During our time in West Chester, Shane started getting really mean. I heard him calling other women whores around me, so I started dressing more conservatively,” she claimed, alleging that while she was planning a Halloween party “tasked” her with, they “got into a fight about whether or not I could wear a costume that was revealing [and] I gave up and agreed to be some kind of vampire whose whole body was covered.”.

Brassel recalled crying “every day” and calling her mom in “tears,” which prompted her mom to tell Gillis that she was worried their next move to Austin in January 2025 would not be “good” for her.

“My six-month free trial of Sweet Shane Gillis had run out, and it was time for me to start paying,” Brassel wrote, claiming that Gillis told her mom she’d be “fine” when they relocated to Texas, but that was not what happened.

Shortly after they moved, Gillis jetted off to the Super Bowl in February 2025 and left Brassel at home alone in a city where she knew no one.

Industry observers note that “I had no friends, really nothing to my life there, and I felt like he had just ditched me to go party with celebrities,” she remembered. “I played it cool and then privately sobbed in the guest bedroom.”.

The following month, Gillis hosted SNL on Brassel’s birthday, so she “lightheartedly asked what we’d be doing next week to celebrate,” to which he allegedly responded, “You’re lucky I’m even f***ing inviting you to this,” in what she described as his “‘I’m just joking but maybe not’ tone.”.

Brassel revealed that July 2025 was when everything came to a head days after Gillis allegedly told her that she was “so f***ing depressed” and had “no motivation,” which looking back she now considers to be accurate.

In a recent development, “In a way, he was right. I had spent May and June constantly sleeping. My body was so inflamed that I began to think I had a chronic illness,” she shared. “I began to ask myself, ‘Who am I, and what do I do if this life is slowly killing me?’”.

On the 4th of July that year, the pair had some of Gillis’ friends over after a day on a boat and when Brassel went to change the music on his phone, she decided to check his text history as well.

It has been revealed that “I scrolled, looking for a woman’s name. It didn’t take long to find one,” Brassel claimed, saying she found a woman’s “sexts” with Gillis and an exchange in which the comedian allegedly texted the woman, “I should have had sex with you, I was being gay” during Super Bowl weekend when he left Brassel behind.

Brassel confessed that she lost it and yelled at Gillis in front of his friends and he “pretended he didn’t know who I was talking about.”.

“I threw my phone. I threw a chair. I was not myself, but then I hadn’t been myself in months. I didn’t even hear my own voice in my head anymore. It was always Shane’s,” she recalled. “Every action was filtered through thoughts of him: ‘What would Shane think? Will Shane get mad at me for this?’ Finally, I snapped. It was the first time I ever felt like I had any sense of control in the relationship.”.

Sources indicate that brassel stated Gillis brought her “an apology matcha” the next day, but she just “chucked” it at the wall. The pair “started the process of breaking up” in August 2025, but even after their split, Brassel said Gillis’ fans continued to pull her down. (The pair texted on and off for some time before cutting ties completely that fall.).

Industry observers note that “Throughout our relationship, they loved to comment on every one of my posts, calling me a gold-digging whore,” she claimed of Gillis’ followers. “After we broke up, it felt like every white man age[d] 18 to 40 in America had daggers on me. They would recognize me out in public and shout degrading things at me.”.

Brassel noted that she’s been in therapy the past year to “deprogram myself from the relationship” and she now sees Gillis as one of many men who “are insecure and instead of choosing to be better men, they take their shortcomings out on everyone else around them.”.

She explained that Gillis’ “once-looming presence has shrunk down to that of a buzzing gnat,” and one she doesn’t let affect her anymore.

Industry observers note that “When I happen to see him onscreen or his fans send me hate comments in my DMs, I repeat a sentiment I learned in therapy: ‘They know the entertainer. I knew the man,’” she concluded.

In a recent development, doctor Victor von Doom's ego and conviction in his own superiority are as enormous as the universe, but in his cold heart, he does respect some of the "foolish" heroes who oppose him. Doom unconditionally loves his goddaughter, Valeria Richards of the Fantastic Four. He is frenemies with Namor the Sub-Mariner, and also maintains a friendly rivalry with his fellow sorcerer Doctor Stephen Strange; their dynamic lacks the bitterness that defines Doom's feud with Reed Richards. Doom also acknowledges Captain America as a paragon of his chosen ideals, and sees even Spider-Man's puerility as if he's a court jester, the one willing to tell a king what no one else will.

Industry observers note that but there's one hero that Doom most consistently views and addresses as an equal, and that's Ororo Monroe, Storm, of the X-Men. Storm is easily one of the strongest X-Men; she can control the weather itself and is a self-styled "goddess." Even Doom concedes her that description. Unusually for Doom, he rarely tries to downplay Storm's power next to his own. Ororo's strength intrigues him — as does her beauty.

Now, Doom isn't the kind of man to act on romantic whimsy. "Doom needs no one" is one of his self-affirming catchphrases, and he once drove away his childhood sweetheart Valeria to prioritize his quest for knowledge and power. Part of Doom's self-inflicted misery is choosing to believe that no woman could ever love a man with a scarred face like his, yet another reason Doom hides behind a mask: "How could she... when even I am driven to madness by the sight!" But even so, one feels Doom would revel in the fantasy of Storm sitting by his side. It all goes back to their first meeting in "Uncanny X-Men" #145 by Chris Claremont and Dave Cockrum.

"Uncanny X-Men" problems #145-147 comprise a short arc where the twisted gamesman Arcade teams up with Doom to destroy the X-Men. In #145, Storm indicates up at Doom's castle... and he welcomes her as an honored guest, treating her to a feast while the other X-Men are attacked by mecha-armored guards. Storm herself is charmed by Doom, thinking he is "a fascinating man," and he reciprocates.

"Storm seems drawn to me, as I am to her. Lioness to lion. Queen to king. She does not fear me. She should. She will.".

Sources indicate that indeed, Doom soon defeats the X-Men, Storm included, as he dismisses them all as simple "children" next to him. While the others are thrown into deathtraps, Doom — charmed as he was by Storm — transmutes the still conscious Ororo into a chrome statue, while creating a robot in Storm's image to serve him. For Ororo, who is claustrophobic, being trapped inside her own body is a living hell. Once freed, she lives up to her name and unfurls a terrifying storm. Echoing Doom's own words, Storm declares: "Am I not beautiful, Lord Doom? And terrible? Do you not fear me? You should. You shall.".

Recent findings suggest that normally, this would be a bungled first impression. But after surrendering Arcade, Doom apologizes to Storm for his behavior, suggesting his infatuation with her was real: "I would hope that we might begin anew. You are a fascinating woman. I should like to know you better." Ororo grants him the grace of a clean slate.

It has been revealed that the events of this arc are referenced almost any time Doom and Storm meet, such as in concern #4 of Storm's 2024 solo series, where Doom hosts her in Latveria. He's not alone among villains in his view of Storm, either.

In a recent development, read any of Chris Claremont's writing, including the hundreds of "X-Men" stories to his name, and it's easy to tell that he's got a thing for powerful women. No "X-Men" character more consistently indicates that than Storm, the strongest of the team and their frequent leader. It often feels like Claremont wrote his own infatuation with the character into the text; "powerful villain tries to take Storm as theirs" is a stock Claremont "X-Men" plot, and not just with Doom.

According to recent reports, claremont and Bill Sienkiewicz's "Uncanny X-Men" #159 sees Dracula himself try to turn Storm into his bride. (Latest comic series "Midnight X-Men" takes place in a timeline where he succeeded, and Storm reigns as a vampire queen.).

Recent findings suggest that an attraction to Storm binds Doom and Dracula... or does it? Shortly after Doom's guest appearance in "X-Men," writer-artist John Byrne took over "Fantastic Four." Byrne had made his name drawing "X-Men," but ultimately left due to creative differences with Claremont. A lingering mark of those differences highlights up in "Fantastic Four" #258. Byrne, apparently dissatisfied with how Claremont wrote Doom, suggests the Doom who teamed up with Arcade was one of Doom's robotic duplicates, or Doombots.

Industry observers note that now, in the "X-Men" issues themselves, there's no hint this isn't the real Doom. Years later, in Al Ewing and Stefano Caselli's "S.W.O.R.D." #7, Storm hosts Doom for dinner, and their conversation is loaded with references to "X-Men" #145. Doom blames his unbecoming behavior of attacking Storm, his guest, as a Doombot's faulty programming (but he would, wouldn't he?). Across the conversation, Doom demonstrates his interest in Storm is all too real, to the point Ororo tells him: "Don't flirt, Victor. It's unbecoming." Except, Doom would likely argue, with an exceptional woman like her.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles.
  • The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

“I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”.

“I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” notes showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”.

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.).

According to recent reports, hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter claims, “and eventually seduced.”.

Industry observers note that cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she claims, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”.

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

According to recent reports, “The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter states, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”.

The twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a Newly introduced York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”.

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

Cutter says she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain blueprint of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”.

The second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

“Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter indicates, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one of the enduring American monster myths is the Wendigo or the forest spirit that possesses and compels men to become cannibals. Originally a myth of the Algonquian peoples, the Wendigo has become a monster of comic books, horror films, and more, like Stephen King's chilling novel "Pet Sematary.".

Sources indicate that possibly the strangest Wendigo movie is the 1999 horror western comedy "Ravenous," inspired by real tales of 19th century cannibalism on the frontier like the Donner Party. During the Mexican–American War, Lieutenant John Boyd (Guy Pearce) plays dead during battle. Hidden among a cart of deceased soldiers, Boyd takes an enemy fort. A hero but also a coward, Boyd is then reassigned to a remote outpost in the Sierra Nevada mountains.

In a recent development, curiously, during Boyd's seizure of the fort, he seemed to gain strength when the blood of the dead dripped down onto his tongue. In that moment, Boyd became an unknowing Wendigo, acquiring the strength of the men whose blood he drank — and he's not the only one on the mountain. A traveler named F.W. Colqhoun (Robert Carlyle) shows up at the fort, claiming to be the survivor of a band of wagon travelers killed and cannibalized by their guide, one Colonel Ives. But "Colqhoun" is Ives and, seizing control of the camp, plots to turn it into a cannibal colony. He recognizes Boyd as a seeming kindred spirit, and the movie becomes a test of whether Boyd will succumb to Ives' pressure and his own Wendigo hunger.

Industry observers note that "Ravenous" was a box office bomb in its day, grossing $2 million against a $12 million budget, and it received largely underwhelmed or confounded reviews. But don't take that as a mark against the movie, which has a following to this day. (Any "Yellowjackets" fan should make watching "Ravenous" a priority.).

For "Ravenous" to work, Boyd's temptation needs to feel real. When you've got someone as charismatic as Robert Carlyle playing Ives, it sure does. That performance isn't the only way that Carlyle saved the movie.

Sources indicate that "Ravenous" had a tumultuous production, and Guy Pearce has called "Ravenous" his worst experience shooting a movie. The film's original director Milcho Manchevski was fired mid-filming with 20th Century Fox moving to replace him with "Home Alone 3" director Raja Gosnell. The cast rejected that, and so Carlyle brought in director Antonia Bird, who he'd worked with on the 1997 crime film "Face." Bird is the credited director of "Ravenous," but was she able to wrangle the mess she'd inherited?

Even a "Ravenous" fan will admit the movie is, tonally, all over the place. After a scene of Ives revealing his true murderous self, the movie breaks out into a chase scene with comical banjo music. If you'll pardon the pun, "Ravenous" bites off a lot and tests how much it's capable of chewing. But that strangeness is a strength, as there's no other movie quite like "Ravenous.".

According to recent reports, in a 2015 retrospective review for Rolling Stone, critic David Ehrlich showed the kind of praise that has earned "Ravenous" a fanbase. Ehrlich complimented its unique tonal recipe and how, through its setting, it equates manifest destiny colonialism with literal cannibalism... while conceding those qualities are likely what turned off audiences in 1999.

Considering the 1990s saw Anthony Hopkins make Hannibal Lecter into a cinematic icon on the heels "The Silence of the Lambs," I can see why studio execs would invest in cannibal horror. But "Ravenous" was just too weird a movie to ever be a massive hit, even though it's found its supporters with time.

The sweeping World War I romance comes from the young Belgian filmmaker whose last film, Cannes winner “Close,” received a Best International Feature Oscar nomination. Related Stories 26 Years After He Wrote ‘Meet the Parents,’ John Hamburg Brings Comedy Back to Theaters with ‘Focker In-Law’ Billy Ray Joins Oscar Short Contender ‘Magan’s Fare,’ Starring Barkhad Abdi, as Executive Producer.

Per MUBI, “Surrounded by brutality but bound by tenderness, two World War I soldiers find a fragile sanctuary of love and art amid the shadows of the Belgian trenches. ‘Coward’ asks a profound question for a generation sent to war: when the world demands violence, is walking away the truest act of bravery?”.

More from IndieWire’s review: “Belgian filmmaker wrestles the tenderness and softness between soldiers from the brutality of the battlefield in his visually arresting if thematically by-the-book third feature, ‘Coward.’ Starring newcomers Valentin Campagne and Emmanuel Macchia as achingly beautiful soldiers of the Belgian front in World War I who fall in love and learn to discover that, in one of the most fascinatingly contradictory ideas of Dhont’s highly contradictory career, the violence of war is what both enables and protects their attraction, and allows them to be together at all.”.

In a recent development, there’s more, as “in 1916, on the western front of World War I, the flamboyant Francis (Valentin Campagne) leads a not-so-merry band of rejects among his infantry, of soldiers whose job it is to entertain and raise the morale of their comrades. In this case, it’s forming a theater troupe of the soldiers in drag as they move from battle to battle, a role that’s become almost as instrumental in keeping spirits high as actual combat is to wearing them down. The withdrawn, ethereally beautiful Pierre (Emmanuel Macchia) becomes drawn into the world of the troupe, and he’s intrigued by the outré Francis’ ostentatious theatricality, and how comfortable he is in dresses and makeup. … Through an attraction that’s only allowed to flower because of and in context of their closeness to each other on Francis’ performances, he and Pierre become secret lovers.”.

Watch the new trailer, an IndieWire exclusive, below. MUBI opens the film in theaters throughout the United States and Canada on December 25 (that’s Christmas Day).

How to get your car out of the impound in GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It doesn't take long for one of your cars to end up at the police impound in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • If you are not ready to abandon your favorite car and want it back, we've got you covered.
  • There are two methods to retrieve a car from the police impound: you can either steal it back or pay for it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It doesn't take long for one of your cars to end up at the police impound in Grand Theft Auto 6. You might have abandoned it near a crime scene, or they arrested you while you were driving it. While the circumstances may vary, you have only two ways to proceed if a car is impounded: you forget about it or you retrieve it.

If you are not ready to abandon your favorite car and want it back, we've got you covered. Here's how to get your car out of the impound in GTA 6.

There are two methods to retrieve a car from the police impound: you can either steal it back or pay for it. Both are valid, but the second one becomes available only in Chapter 2.

Recent findings suggest that stealing the car is the most plausible and cheapest option to execute. You just need to head to the impound lot, enter, and drive your car away from there. Some impounds, like the one in Port Gellhorn, have openings that you can use to enter unnoticed. Regardless of how you get inside, the challenge is escaping from the police once you leave. You must be prepared to run away, so try to come up with an escape route by setting a destination far from the city.

Sources indicate that now, the second option requires the Scooter Bros app, which you unlock in Chapter 2 after completing Moses' mission. If you have it already, open the app and select the impounded car (the one with a police badge icon). You will see that the first option in the menu is to pay a fee to retrieve the car.

In a recent development, the price varies depending on how far you are from the police impound. For example, I would have to pay $699 to get my car back from the Port Gellhorn impound while in Vice City. However, if you have upgraded your Scooter Bros account to Premium, you can use your remaining daily credits to request an impounded vehicle. Since this will essentially consume all your credits for the day, you should wait until you have only one left before using this option.

Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first, recommendations for the best ways to make money fast, and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.

Sources indicate that our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy, too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission, and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes. You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

#97203. Sell Thy Neighbor: Trump Official Howard Lutnick and the Clandestine Deal to Sell NYC’s Glamorous Pierre Hotel
