💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mystery Science Theater 3000 fans have always had a special relationship with American Thanksgiving.
  • Industry observers note that the Turkey Day tradition got dropped when MST3K moved from Comedy Central to the Sci-Fi Channel in 1997.
  • 2026's Turkey Day celebration, Back in Orbit, features six episodes from the Sci-Fi Channel run, as introduced by Mike Nelson, Kevin Murphy, and Bill Corbett.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mystery Science Theater 3000 fans have always had a special relationship with American Thanksgiving. The show originally premiered on Thanksgiving Day in 1988, back in its public access era on KTMA TV in Minneapolis. Three years later, Comedy Central ran the first "Turkey Day" MST3K marathon, as both an anniversary celebration for the show and a 30-hour Thanksgiving special.

Industry observers note that the Turkey Day tradition got dropped when MST3K moved from Comedy Central to the Sci-Fi Channel in 1997. (While Sci-Fi did run a MST3K marathon on Thanksgiving 1997, it wasn't labeled "Turkey Day.") That was the end of the tradition until 2013, when MST3K’s DVD distributor Shout! Factory revived Turkey Day via livestream.

2026's Turkey Day celebration, Back in Orbit, features six episodes from the Sci-Fi Channel run, as introduced by Mike Nelson, Kevin Murphy, and Bill Corbett. This is both a nod to their time as the hosts of the show during its Sci-Fi Channel run and a tie-in to the recently concluded MST3K/Rifftrax crossover spinoff, The Rifftrax Experiments.

According to recent reports, this year's Turkey Day starts on Nov. 26 at noon EST on the official MST3K YouTube and Twitch channels, and is currently scheduled to feature:.

That's a solid lineup of late-season MST3K. However, if you're interested in alternative programming (or you simply want a marathon on a day other than American Thanksgiving this year), just about all of the first 10 seasons of MST3K can be found for free on YouTube, either from old fan uploads or via the official MST3K channel. Due to MST3K's famous "keep circulating the tapes" mantra, the old uploads are the next best thing to officially endorsed, so you can binge guilt-free. Here are some more MST3K episodes to consider for your own Thanksgiving entertainment, sorted by their original broadcast order.

According to recent reports, “I’m the luckiest boy in the world! I have slipped the surly bonds of Earth and touched the hand of God!”.

It has been revealed that MST3K really hit its stride in season 3. There are a few good episodes in the first two seasons, such as Catalina Caper and Robot Monster, but season 3 features a stacked roster of series-defining classics, and it starts with this hastily-made Italian fantasy film.

It has been revealed that cave Dwellers is a rebrand of the second movie in a four-part franchise starring the fantasy hero Ator (Miles O'Keefe). There's this whole rich vein of cheap B-movie sword-and-sorcery films from the mid-to-late 1980s that were all trying to cash in on the success of Arnold Schwarzenegger's Conan the Barbarian, and most of them are Italian knock-offs that were made in a week. The best of them are dumb fun; the worst are cocaine-infused unwatchable dreck.

Recent findings suggest that what sets Cave Dwellers apart from the pack is that it takes some really big swings. It feels like one big continuity error even before the climactic moment where Ator instantly and inexplicably invents both hand grenades and the hang glider. It's a nearly perfect bad movie, both in its own right and as fodder for an MST3K episode.

“Hey, what gives? I’m on the milk carton.”.

It has been revealed that this was the episode that made MST3K click for me. Any B-movie fan knows there's a world of difference between "fun bad" and simply bad, and Pod People is about as fun-bad as it gets.

Sources indicate that the backstory is reportedly that Spanish director Juan Piquer Simón (Pieces) set out to make a straightforward horror movie about a vacationing pop band that stumbles across a murderous alien. Then E.T. got popular, so Simón's producers demanded a reshoot to include an additional subplot about a boy who befriends an alien child.

It has been revealed that the result was released in France and Spain as 1983's Extra Terrestrial Visitors, before being retitled to The Unearthling and Pod People for overseas release. It's a baffling mixture of at least three major plotlines, stitched together with little care for the final product. One moment is a heartwarming story of a child and his plush marketable alien pal; the next is some dude in a fursuit killing his way through a set of backup singers. That tonal mismatch makes Pod People a nearly perfect target for MST3K, which led to several of the show's most famous jokes.

“Every frame of this movie looks like someone’s last known photograph.”.

To no one's real surprise, Manos is still generally considered the best episode of MST3K's run on Comedy Central, if not the single best episode. There are other good episodes in the fourth season, like City Limits and Hercules Unchained, but Manos overshadows them all. Like Pod People, this episode dug a notorious dud out of the back alleys of cinematic history and turned it most of the way into comedy gold.

Recent findings suggest that I only say "most of the way" because Manos is a rough watch, even with Joel and the bots running interference. It's a truly baffling independent horror film from 1966, made with faulty equipment on a shoestring budget by a fertilizer salesman who allegedly did it all to win a bet. Manos is just so damn weird that it’s difficult to sit through. It was only ever screened at a handful of theaters in Texas before it appeared on MST3K, at which point it instantly became a legend.

Every frame of Manos is simply uncomfortable. The cast and crew of MST3K were always quite clear in behind-the-scenes featurettes that by the time they sat down to film an episode of the show, they'd watched the entirety of that episode’s featured movie at least five times. Despite that, Joel and the bots still manage to come off as realistically flabbergasted by each bizarre twist in Manos. There's a distinct point at which it stops being a classic MST3K episode and becomes pure trainwreck syndrome, whether you’ve seen the movie before or not.

Sources indicate that much like how Cave Dwellers is a reaction to the success of Conan the Barbarian, Escape 2000 (originally released as Escape From the Bronx, and not to be confused with the 1982 Australian humans-hunting-humans film) is an Italian clone of the first two Mad Max movies. It's set in a dystopian near-future New York City, as the gangs of the Bronx team up to defend their borough from a mega-corporation that wants to destroy and rebuild it. Come to think of it, Escape 2000 predicted gentrification.

Escape 2000 isn't actually that bad of a film. It's just cheaply made, overwrought, and has the same low-quality English dub as a lot of other '80s Italian B-movies, so if you’ve got a taste for that sort of thing you can have a good time with it. That makes it a solid target for the MST3K crew, which instantly lock in on a half-dozen running jokes in the first 10 minutes. It's hard to hear the word "Bronx" after this episode and not immediately think, "None of this would have happened if they'd just left the Bronx.".

“I wonder if there’s beer on the sun.”.

In a recent development, the first 10 seasons of MST3K were filmed in Minnesota, which neatly explains why the show was always so comfortable poking fun at Canadians. With that in mind, The Final Sacrifice is one long joke at Canada's expense, even before Mike and the bots sit down.

It has been revealed that in another example of MST3K pulling a movie out of obscurity, 1990's The Final Sacrifice was made by a film student in Alberta on a budget of CA$1,500. Apparently it aired a few times on Canadian television in the early '90s, but was virtually unknown outside the country until its MST3K appearance.

In a recent development, the saving grace of The Final Sacrifice, both as a film and as an MST3K episode, is Zap Rowsdower (Bruce J. Mitchell). He might have the dumbest name of any character in film history, he's the sidekick until he's suddenly the hero in the last act, and he's a big buttery beer-fed ball of Canadian stereotypes. In other words, he's perfect. No notes. In a more perfect universe than this, Rowsdower would be on his tenth major motion picture, as he fights and drinks his way through unexplored Canadian action history. It's easily the highlight of this year's Turkey Day celebration, as it was hard to find online until recently, and it's worth incorporating into your own custom marathon.

In a recent development, ”Why is he so impossible to hit? How can they keep missing this slow, giant white thing?”.

Industry observers note that space Mutiny is still perhaps the most quotable episode of MST3K, even 29 years after it aired. It's given the internet decades of running jokes and forum handles, all at the expense of famous chunkhead Blast Hardcheese Punch Rockgroin Dave Ryder (Reb Brown, Yor, the Hunter From the Future) and his battle to save a colony ship from mutineers.

The co-stars of Space Mutiny have insisted since its release that it was meant to be a campy spoof of science fiction, but that's obviously damage control. Instead, it's obviously a million-dollar script paired with a buck-fifty budget. At its best, Space Mutiny is funny for all the wrong reasons, from Reb Brown’s random screaming to every woman on the colony ship wearing exercise gear as a “uniform” to the space battles that consist of visibly recycled footage from the original Battlestar Galactica. Its MST3K episode is one of the best in the series' run, often held up as the best in the Sci-Fi Channel seasons, and a genuine classic.

According to recent reports, “You asked for an avalanche of flavor, and now you got it, huh? Not enjoying it, are you?”.

It has been revealed that while MST3K has always been known for its high volume of jokes, the Netflix seasons have a particular rushed delivery that can work against them. There are still a few great episodes in the two-season run, however, and Avalanche is a dark horse contender for the best of the lot.

Avalanche is a 1978 disaster movie produced by schlock auteur Roger Corman, starring Rock Hudson and Mia Farrow, who have less than zero chemistry with one another. They play a divorced couple, and it's obvious within seconds of seeing them together that there were multiple good reasons for that divorce.

Industry observers note that that isn't Avalanche's biggest problem, however. In the best low-budget tradition, it saves all its special effects for the finale, which makes it a disaster movie where the titular disaster doesn't show up until the last 20 minutes. That leaves the viewer to sit through an hour of awkward foreshadowing, personal dramas, and horrible '70s dinner parties (there's a baked Alaska in Avalanche that's so unappetizing that it deserves its own unique content warning) until half the cast gets murdered by snow. The MST3K crew makes the best of it with some of the best jokes in season 11. It's an unsung hero of Jonah Ray's time as MST3K's host.

Latest Update: 10 Action Video Games That Are Bangers From Start to Finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to video games, some of the most popular have always been the likes of action/adventure titles.
  • Like any genre of any medium, though, there are some games that most certainly stand out among the others.
  • It has been revealed that this wonderful series by Rocksteady Studios is known as one of the best superhero video game franchises of all time, and for very good reason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to video games, some of the most popular have always been the likes of action/adventure titles. Video games provide a great escape for the player. Giving them the chance to be an action hero, swinging around New York City, stealing cars, shooting up bad guys, or becoming the samurai of their dreams makes them as popular as they've become.

Like any genre of any medium, though, there are some games that most certainly stand out among the others. This isn't to say that they're better than all the rest—there are too many games to make such an objective statement—but there are some certified bangers that come to mind when the discussion of action video games begins.

It has been revealed that this wonderful series by Rocksteady Studios is known as one of the best superhero video game franchises of all time, and for very good reason. A lot of those reasons were either expanded upon from the first game, or established in the second title, Batman: Arkham City. This is known as one of the best superhero games out there, and has gone down in history for it.

According to recent reports, batman: Arkham City is well-known for the common notion that it makes you truly feel like Batman (Kevin Conroy). The gameplay mechanics are very well-executed, and the story is thrilling from start to finish. Not to mention, the return of Kevin Conroy as Batman and Mark Hamill as Joker is a huge win and makes this truly feel like some of the many definitive versions of the characters.

If there's one thing PlayStation is excellent at, it's having some amazing console-exclusive titles. One of the best of recent years is none other than Horizon Zero Dawn. Following the hunter known as Aloy (Ashly Burch), Horizon Zero Dawn takes players on a journey of trying to discover the truth about the hunter's origins, and, in turn, the world around her itself.

This project takes place in a post-apocalyptic setting, but not in the manner of another PlayStation exclusive, The Last of Us. The landscape of Horizon Zero Dawn is wide, vast, and filled with high-technology—machine creatures that are now the apex predators, to be exact. The combat—using Aloy's hunting skills and weapons—is wonderful, and such a blast to play. Not to mention, this upcoming world is such a joy to explore and keeps the players actively wanting to discover more about it via the story and the open-world nature of the title.

Industry observers note that when it comes to action, there are few that bring the amount that Hades does. That's because the entire point of the game is, well, action. While there is a story to Hades, the game, at its heart, is a rougelike dungeon crawler title that puts the player against hoards and rooms upon rooms of foes to face as the son of Hades (Logan Cunningham), Zagreus (Darren Korb), attempts to escape the Underworld.

Players will die but, every time they begin anew, they can spend their hard-earned resources to level up and go at it again with upcoming powers. The method to the madness of Hades is failing, trying again, failing, and going until the player finally makes it through. It is an absolute thrill ride the entire way through.

It has been revealed that while Sega is most known for the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, they have another video game series that is widely beloved, Yakuza. The best game in stated series is none other than Yazuka 0. The Yakuza series is a great time, and the way it brings together gritty crime drama with some hilarious comedy that keeps the players on their toes.

It has been revealed that as stated, the best of the best, Yakuza 0, brings all of these things to the table and enhances them. It follows two stories simultaneously, and that really helps in keeping the players invested. The combat mechanics are phenomenal and the true, main highlight of the game. Yakuza 0 is truly the perfect example of how to make an incredible Yazkua game.

Sources indicate that while the recent God of War games are easily some of the best PlayStation titles in recent years, if fans of action want something in the series to seriously deliver on that, they need to look no further than God of War II. This sequel truly delivers on action, spectacle, and fun gameplay. It has a blockbuster-level story that is engaging for the entire runtime.

According to recent reports, not to forget, the players get to take on the gods of Olympus. Kratos (Terrence "T.C." Carson) is out for blood, and he is going to stop at nothing to get it. This allows players to experience some serious spectacle as they fight their way through Olympus and take down the gods. It's a ride filled with intensity till the very end and worth playing every second.

Much like Batman: Arkham City, Insomniac Games' hit title, Marvel's Spider-Man, is well-regarded because of how much it makes the player truly feel like Spider-Man (Yuri Lowenthal). The swinging physics/mechanics are stellar, and easily some of the best in any Spider-Man game ever. Swinging mechanics are so much more crucial to a Spider-Man game than one would realize on paper. For quite some time, Spider-Man 2's video game was known to have the best.

In a recent development, many consider it one of the best modern superhero video games of all time. The execution of Marvel's Spider-Man was done with grace and prowess. This reimagining of the Spider-Man world—where Peter Parker is older, experienced, and facing off with enemies he's never faced before—is so well-done, and it's a fan-favorite Spider-Man universe. Playing Marvel's Spider-Man truly does make the player feel like Spider-Man, and, alongside that, has an astounding story.

It has been revealed that there are a few things in this life that will always be cool: cowboys, superheroes, spacemen, and . . . samurais. A modern game that might genuinely capture the samurai vibe the best is none other than 2020's Ghost of Tsushima. If there's one thing that can describe this game, it's that it is vastly cinematic. It feels like players are playing through a classic samurai film.

According to recent reports, playing the ever-gorgeous Ghost of Tsushima feels like playing through a movie in all the best ways. The camera, shot framing, battles, and more all make this story amazing to experience. The melee combat is borderline perfect. Sword duels and other action feel so natural and exhilarating to play—it's genuinely difficult to put this amazing game down.

According to recent reports, 2016's Doom is about as action-packed as it gets. It is a literal non-stop space adventure that has players firing bullets of all kinds into horrifying monsters. Doom rewards players for being aggressive and jumping straight into action, rather than strategy. There is always a battle or chase going down, and it never stops being abundantly exciting.

Sources indicate that but players aren't just firing the same kind of gun the entire time—no, there is a gigantic arsenal of weapons players will have the choice to utilize throughout the entire game. Just as importantly, the score behind the action is one of the best action game scores of all time. Composed by the legendary Mick Gordon, everything that is great about Doom is enhanced by Gordon's excellent work.

Another sword-wielding adventure—reminiscent of Ghost of Tsushima—from recent years that is phenomenal is the ever-thrilling Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. Taking place in the late-1500s, this 2019 adventure follows a shinobi named Sekiro (Daisuke Namikawa and Noshir Dalal), players get to step into the shoes of an incredible swordsman as he goes on a journey to rescue his captured lord, Kuro (Miyuki Sato and Amber Hood).

Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice is everything a typical FromSoftware game—Dark Souls, Bloodborne, and Elden Ring—is, in all the best ways. It truly challenges the player in ways other FromSoftware titles don't. It also has a setting unlike the others, too, being set in 1500s Japan. It is so distinct, vast, and exciting that it feels like a must-play for those who love some good sword combat . . . even if it has the classic tough FromSoftware difficuly.

Sources indicate that there is absolutely no question that Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest game of the decade—maybe even the last two decades. People have been waiting for this game for so long that the cultural impact has been increasing little by little every year, exploding in one great release this year. Ask anyone who's played it, and they'll most likely say, "It was worth the wait.".

In a recent development, this game is truly something special. It has attention to detail unlike any other, gorgeous visuals, skilled performances, groundbreaking mechanics across the board, and a wonderful story at the core of it all. There are dozens of reasons to love this game, but one of the main highlights are the action sequences—of which there are plenty. Robberies, assassinations, gunfights, etc. bring Grand Theft Auto VI to the top of the "best of all time" list.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].

Recent findings suggest that with a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen. The gay 29-year-old songwriter finished touring his sensational, sensually charged second album “Spanish Leather” earlier this fall, and only just a few short months after his screen debut, “La Bola Negra,” won a Cannes top prize, got scooped up by Netflix, and entered the awards season fray.

Sources indicate that oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017. Born Álvaro Lafuente Calvo, he’s now a meme thanks to his stage and screen sobriquet, which means “little guitar of the fountain.” Related Stories ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente, and Peter Gamble to Receive SFFILM Honors.

Recent findings suggest that guitarricadelafuente’s performance balances both hushed repression and eventually unleashed emotions throughout “La Bola Negra,” as Sebastián nurses wounded (and handsome) Republican soldier Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau, a more established actor in Spain). They fall for each other in the process, in a furtive romance mostly framed in stolen glances and tacit looks — in other words, the sort of good old-fashioned gay yearning that’s made movies like “Brokeback Mountain,” “Call Me by Your Name,” and “God’s Own Country” so popular. “La Bola Negra” is, by now, one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies ever to play in Spain, and it’s a major Oscar contender in select theaters as it gears up for its early December Netflix streaming premiere.

In a recent development, indieWire spoke to Guitarricadelafuente over Zoom where, behind him, an oversized window frame flanked the waves gently rushing up to Miami Beach. Below, we discuss his songwriting process for “La Nieve,” witnessing the breakup of directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo (which happened during filming), and how he overcame his fears to make his auspicious screen debut. That’s all while balancing a proudly out music career where his sexuality is front and center. Plus, watch an exclusive video about his role in the film at the bottom of this story.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

It has been revealed that indieWire: You’ve been all over the world with “La Bola Negra,” from Cannes in May to Toronto and, now, Miami Beach for this virtual junket interview. You’re used to being all over the place. You also toured your album this year. Did that help you prepare for promoting the film?

Guitarricadelafuente: I would say that kind of, in a way, because there’s something that I see as very similar to going and talking about the movie and talking about your character, which is something very similar to when you’re going around touring with your album. I think it’s more difficult because you need to talk about yourself and not just about playing a character because the music you make comes from a very profound place, and you need to talk about many things that go inside of you.

This is your acting debut, and there’s Oscar chatter for both your performance and the song you wrote for the film, “La Nieve.” Do you watch the Academy Awards in Spain?

Not that much recently, but I remember when I was studying architecture in college, I used to stay up late at night doing projects. I remember staying up until 3:00 a.m. and with my friends, we were doing our little houses, and we would put the television on, and see the awards. But that was one of the only times that I stayed up late, or that I used to stay up late to see the awards, because you always receive that in Spain in the morning after.

It has been revealed that you signed up for the movie without a script. What was the pitch that the Javis gave you? You knew you’d have to learn the trumpet.

They didn’t tell me that I had to learn an instrument because it was going to be originally something that I already knew how to play, but they wanted to make it more difficult. So they noted, “OK, why don’t you try a trumpet?” But yeah, the first pitch, there was not much about it. They told me about “La piedra oscura” by Alberto Conejero, which was the original play where the characters of Rafael and Sebastián appear.

I just knew that it was going to be set against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, with Lorca being so present. … They didn’t convince me, but I was so moved by how they were so confident that I could do it because I was so frightened and I wasn’t sure at all, but it was their vision. I admired them so much from before. I knew that they’ve worked with many nonprofessional actors, and people acting for the first time. So it was something that I just threw myself into.

You were frightened about whether or not you could deliver as an actor, or was it the material?

I was spending all of my time making music and touring, and it was very time-consuming and exhausting. … I didn’t know if I could put myself into that experience because I thought the proper way to dig into that role was to put your soul into it.

In a recent development, they were looking for someone who was openly gay for this role, right? There’s a spectrum of sexualities among the cast. Miguel Bernardeau, your scene partner, is straight.

Recent findings suggest that well, I don’t even know if we talked about that at any point because it was just assumed that I was. [Laughs] I don’t know if that was a condition. I think it was something that, to be more faithful to the story, had to happen. At the time that they approached me with the role, I was finishing my last album, “Spanish Leather.” It represented an imaginary — but not that imaginary — journey of a young gay man who comes out from his village and puts himself out to the world, discovering who he is and where he belongs.

Many people would know my music, but I would realize that not many people knew that I was gay even. There’s a substantial, not sexual, but I would say sensual component to [“Spanish Letter”] and this process of growing up and sexual [awakening]. So it was very special in a way to play this role … it’s something that you don’t get that much, maybe in Spain, just to see things where you can get referenced with or reflected with.

According to recent reports, los Javis broke up during production. Did they communicate that to the cast? How did you find out?

It was so weird because I don’t know if I’m stupid or what, I didn’t even notice. I would hear obviously so many rumors, but … you couldn’t tell that they were apart because they were acting as one. And I couldn’t believe that they were breaking up with the intensity of that shoot. It was like, “How on earth are they going to split up in the middle of this craziness and this madness?”.

Industry observers note that but I don’t even remember when they told us. I think it was at the end of the shoot. We would eventually know that something was going on. I couldn’t believe it. How have you managed to carry this shoot? But that also represented how moving this story was to them.

People were gossiping at that point.

Of course. Even when they reached out to me with the role, I would hear rumors, and I was like, “How is this going to be possible if they’re so tight together?” It was inevitable because they are so well known in Spain, that rumors would arrive.

Miguel has probably 10 years of acting experience that you don’t have. Was he helpful as a mentor, as well as an onscreen romance?

Recent findings suggest that the first time that we met, it was actually when he was doing his audition because the only character that was clear in the movie was Sebastián. We had to test how this approach was going to be with the real Rafael, because this very tight and intimate connection had to happen. He didn’t know that I was going to play Sebastián, and he just appeared in the rehearsal room. And I thought there was a very special instant connection there, that I think we’re obviously very different, or we come from very different backgrounds or different ways of seeing the world.

Sources indicate that but there was a beauty in that because obviously I saw him as this wonderful, beautiful, talented, and professional actor that I could anchor myself in. He’s all the time lying on a bed [on screen]. And so he has to say so many things without being able to move. We were both left a lot of freedom on set and to try and to make errors. The room would get empty, and it was just Los Javis, Miguel, and I.

Were you writing the movie’s theme song, “La Nieve,” during production?

It was a very long process from the beginning, when I was told to write the song. I don’t think of me doing a song as in I get into a room and say, “OK, what I’m going to talk about right now?” And then I get a lyric, and I go back home. This Film has so many stories in it, and to try to be faithful to all of them and try to unify them in a thread, in a song, was very difficult. I was listening at the time, before they reached out to me, to Spanish Civil War songs.

It was actually a queer singer of the time who was called Rolando Alarcón. There were songs played with parlor guitars that were [made] to be sung on the waterfront. We started preparing the role with Los Javis. Lorca had to be very present also in this because he’s all over the place. He’s pretty omnipresent all of the time, surveilling what’s going on. And you had to pay a homage to him because, in the end, “La bola negra” was this unfinished script that he was writing.

I had to live my character in my own skin and properly carry that emotional baggage that he was holding. And it wasn’t until the end of the shoot, when we were in Cantabria living for two months … I obviously had this melody in my head, but when this scene with the firing squad happens, and [SPOILER ALERT] Rafael dies, it was a combination of all of that emotional journey that the character was living.

I would arrive home that day and start playing a melody on a piano and mumbling some lyrics, and I would send this to Los Javis, and I didn’t know that they were going to use this to unify the three stories that go on in the movie. And it was a way for me to let all of that emotion go.

Industry observers note that this song will now have to be part of every setlist you perform. It’s your “My Heart Will Go On.”.

I hope it turns into that. I wish to be 50 years old and be in Madrid and be singing that. That would be so beautiful. Because I feel that I was just playing in Madrid my last concert one month ago, it was kind of the closing chapter of this “Spanish Leather” tour, and the film was just released one week before that. And so I got the chance to play “La Nieve” there for the first time. After that, it was very emotional because you would hear 18,000 people singing to that. It was like goosebumps. After that, people would be commenting on TikTok, “So Sebastián had the chance to finally be a musician and get to Madrid and perform.” That’s kind of like a closing of the thread, a very beautiful thing.

Industry observers note that “La Bola Negra” is also one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies to play in Spain ever. Have you been able to go home and experience that?

It has been revealed that we were in Spain those first two weeks until we had the last concert in Madrid, and then we went to Toronto and all over the place. And that was a very special week because I was at my sister’s wedding. You could feel something in the air. There was a communal excitement, and people of all ages, all different ages, going to the cinema, or even people, like aunts of mine, who haven’t been to the cinema in 10 years, to see how that’s happening is something that makes us very proud.

For me, the Spanish premiere was more important because that’s all Spanish people’s lives. Everybody has been linked to that moment of time, it’s like their ancestors. So the Spanish were going to be the most critical of it. But to see how young people, old people, people from different backgrounds go and you suddenly have this sense of communion was something spectacular that you could see in the streets. Like older ladies and young queer guys coming up to you, it’s just incredible.

What are you doing next? Do you want to keep acting?

Recent findings suggest that yeah. It’s been a crazy time. I’m having the time to even make new music and to, I don’t know, to see what I’m able to, because even three years ago… I would oblige myself to be quiet and rest to be able to feel inspired. But now it’s all these hectic times that are making me feel so inspired, and to share that time and put it into making art.

“La Bola Negra” is now in select theaters will start streaming on Netflix on Wednesday, December 2.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Add to that a return to the medieval fantasy roots that had made the series so popular in the first place, and Square Enix were never going to be on to anything other than a substantial winner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Final Fantasy series has enjoyed a lot more ups than downs over the years, but most fans agree that the ninth mainline game in the series is one of the very best. The game's greatest strength is undoubtedly its narrative, and the cast of characters who bring it life, many of whom still serve as the most memorable protagonists we have seen to date.

Add to that a return to the medieval fantasy roots that had made the series so popular in the first place, and Square Enix were never going to be on to anything other than a substantial winner. Though the developer doesn't traditionally do direct sequels in their mainline games in the series, it sure would have been nice to pick up the story of this one elsewhere, even in a spin-off.

Happily, that's all about to change, but it isn't in a medium that you might expect.

As first reported by GameDaily, Final Fantasy IX: The Black Mages' Legacy is an upcoming animated series that's back in development, after spending plenty of time in limbo. The project was first declared back in 2021 by Cyber Group Studios, a Paris-based animation tech giant, after they secured the rights to partner with Square Enix.

It has been revealed that they then spent the best part of three years trying to sell the product to licensees, seemingly without much in the way of success, before they entered financial difficulties in October 2024. After that, four potential buyers expressed their interest in securing the rights to the assets and IPs of the comapny, before EuroVisual came out with approximately 80% of them, including Final Fantasy, in March 2025.

Now, the 2D animated series has appeared on the organization's official website as officially in development, with a first season of ten 22-minute episodes and a tentative targeted release date of 2028. The series is being aimed at children between the ages of 8 and 13, with supervision from Square Enix designed to ensure the story remains consistent with the game.

In a recent development, so what narrative will the story follow? The series is set to pick up around ten years after the original game, with the children of Vivi Ornitier, six young black mages named Mel, Koln, Luciola, Théa, Fala, and Doc, who are living in the city of Alexandria.

Anybody who has played the game will know the emotional weight that Vivi's character arc has, and the series is likely to touch on similar themes, only through the prism of his offspring. We don't have specific details beyond that just yet, but it could absolutely be one to watch for old fans, despite its usual target audience.

Outside of that, Final Fantasy fans also have the concluding part of the Remake trilogy of the seventh game to look forward to. Titled Revelation, it's set to drop on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, finally bringing to a close the retelling of one of the best games of all time in the process.

Sources indicate that how will Robert Pattinson‘s casting as James Bond affect his Oscar chances? The hard-working star, who was established by the “Twilight” franchise, has ricocheted from Christopher Nolan projects (“Tenet” and “The Odyssey”) and the DC franchise’s “The Batman” (“Part Two” is shooting in London) to riskier indies like the Safdies’ “Good Time” and Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse.”.

This award season, Pattinson was juggling three long-shot potential Oscar nods: Best Actor for A24’s marital deconstruction “The Drama,” and Supporting Actor for two Snidely Whiplash villains, lead suitor Antinous in Universal’s blockbuster “The Odyssey” and shape-shifter Scytale in Warner Bros.’ “Dune: Part Three,” respectively. His best chance at an Oscar nomination, though, was always for his creepy lead turn as TV journalist Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” another A24 release. When Daniel Craig was cast as James Bond during the awards tour for Steven Spielberg’s “Munich” (2005), the immediate result was a marked increase in attendance at all screenings, recalls one veteran publicist. “There was a different before-and-after energy,” he stated. That did not land Craig a nomination, however. The only Bond to score an Oscar nod and win after a long and storied career was Sean Connery (“The Untouchables”). Playing Bond does not lend an actor cred with the Academy. But it does extend a career.

The impact for Pattinson, who is ubiquitous in online media, is the same. At this point, most awards voters will have seen “The Odyssey,” but those seeing the Christopher Nolan blockbuster for the first time will view the actor differently. “He will have heightened scrutiny,” stated one studio Oscar expert. “Clearly he is being tapped to anchor a franchise. For the actors [branch], he will be someone to reckon with.”.

Clearly, fewer people have screened “Primetime.” Pattinson’s Bond ascension will push the movie up in the must-see rankings. “Bond probably gets more people to watch the movie,” said one Oscar strategist. “That’s half the battle. The goal is to get people to watch the movie. But the movie has to do the work.”.

Sources indicate that at the box office, “Primetime” has fared better domestically ($47 million) than abroad ($12 million), which is significant given an Oscar voting pool of more than 10,000 voters, one-quarter of whom are international. How will “Primetime” do with the upcoming critic votes? Or BAFTAs, which will reveal the international tale? And SAG’s Actor Awards, where, at this stage, Gold Derby has “Digger” star Tom Cruise edging out Pattinson? The race between those two actors is “squishy,” remarked Debra Birnbaum, Gold Derby editor-in-chief, who distinguishes between early season “hopedictions” and “real predictions.”.

Sources indicate that it helps to remember that the Academy is just starting to catch up with the contenders. The experts on Gold Derby (I’m one), at this stage, have seen way more movies than the site’s consumers or the Academy. Later in the season, Gold Derby users and experts are more in sync. That’s why we should take with a grain of salt the recent ascension among the Gold Derby users to number five for Best Actor contender Pattinson. They’re responding to publicity. The experts have him at seven. The same is true for the betting site Kalshi’s odds. Their accuracy improves the closer you get to the Oscars. At this stage, their bettors haven’t seen everything. And the key Oscar season markers, from critics’ groups to Guild awards, haven’t played out.

Industry observers note that the American Cinematheque came out way ahead by honoring Pattinson with its annual award fete, set to take place on February 9, 2027. Tables are selling out and Bond studio Amazon/MGM — and Hollywood — will be there in force.

Industry observers note that while Pattinson has never been an actors’ actor, he’s a hugely bankable global movie star. He’s going to keep us interested for a long time.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that what makes for a truly exceptional video game experience is going to vary and differ from each individual person, as there is no truly 100% correct list of the greatest video games of all time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that especially compared to the likes of literature, theater, and film, whose histories go back over 100 years of history, video games are a much newer artform of creative expression that is still taking shape and evolving year by year. Still, the medium has had an undeniable growth since the early days of arcade shooters and 8-bit graphics, as games are able to tell rich and powerful stories all while being more immersive than any other artform. Especially with Grand Theft Auto VI's recent record-breaking release further cementing video games as the dominant entertainment medium of the modern age, it places an even greater legacy on the games designated as the greatest of all time.

Recent findings suggest that what makes for a truly exceptional video game experience is going to vary and differ from each individual person, as there is no truly 100% correct list of the greatest video games of all time. For the sake of this list, the entries are a collection of games that consistently stand out and come up in conversation not just because of their high quality, but because of the standards they set when they released and their influence on the entire medium. Still, this only scratches the surface of exceptional video games that have been released since the inception of the industry.

While many people may think of the long-running television franchise or even the original comic when it comes to The Walking Dead, gamers will immediately sing the praises of Telltale's legendary point-and-click adventure game. An original story set in the comic book universe, the episodic game set a new standard for emotional storytelling and writing in video games, with a rich narrative influenced by player choice that amplifies the greatest strengths of Robert Kirkman's original series.

With stylish cell-shaded graphics and approachable gameplay simple enough for even casual gamers to enjoy and get wrapped up in the story, Telltale's The Walking Dead does a great job of making its central story as engaging and impactful as possible. While Telltale has continued the story with an array of subsequent sequels and continuing story, it's the original run of 5 episodes that made such a massive impact on audiences as one of the most poignant and beautiful gaming experiences of all time.

Industry observers note that in the early days of 8-bit video games, the platformer genre reigned supreme as the most widely popular style of gaming, with no platformer franchise being as popular or immediately recognizable as Super Mario Bros. While the original NES classic is exceptional enough as it is, the brilliance and timeless appeal of the Mario franchise wouldn't be fully realized until Super Mario Bros. 3, which almost 40 years later is still one of the best 2d platformers ever made.

In a recent development, the game absolutely perfects the feeling and smooth controls required of a platformer of the era, being leaps and bounds ahead of its contemporaries in terms of precision and game feel. This is all on top of the overwhelming creativity in terms of the game's level designs and power-ups that truly bring the wild chaos of the Mario world to life. This classic platformer still stands as the absolute best game released on the Nintendo Entertainment System.

It has been revealed that A striking monolith of the action-adventure genre from Team Ico, PlayStation 2 classic Shadow of the Colossus has stood as one of the quintessential examples of games as serious art ever since its release. The game features staggering visuals and a gargantuan sense of scale, seeing the player have to face off against various massive creatures across the land with the goal of resurrecting a young woman. Through traversing the world on horse and by foot, its exceptional visuals and minimalist design come together to create a defining gaming experience.

Especially in an era where action adventure gaming was continuously getting louder and more abrasive with its gameplay and visuals, the slow and methodical approach that Shadow of the Colossus took made the game that much more striking and memorable to 2000s gamers. It truly felt ahead of its time in terms of being an interactive work of art, with something meaningful and sorrowful to say in its storytelling instead of pure entertainment.

Recent findings suggest that one of the premiere masterpieces of the PlayStation brand and one of the first games that come to mind for many when considering games that actively go for a cinematic feel, The Last of Us is one of the defining gaming masterpieces of the 2010s. It tells a dark post-apocalyptic story that primarily focuses on the loss of humanity at large, paralleling the unlikely connection that fosters between a smuggler who lost his daughter and a young girl who has only known this apocalyptic world.

While the emotional and groundbreaking storytelling is the primary element that people praise about The Last of Us, the core stealth-centric action gameplay is also worthy of praise, as it gets the player engaged and immersed in this heightened world where anything can go wrong. The game was also for many a massive leap forward in terms of technical craft in visuals, pushing the PlayStation 3 to its limits and ushering in a upcoming age of realism in video games.

One of the great advents of gaming as an artform becoming more accessible in the digital era is that many more independent game developers are able to bring their visions to life, with a wide array of indie game masterpieces being released in the 21st century. One of the most defining and culturally dominant indie games has been Undertale, Toby Fox's quaint and quirky mixture of RPGs like Earthbound and bullet hell games like Touhou Project.

More than anything else, Undertale thrives thanks to its overwhelming charm and ingenuity, utilizing simplistic visuals and dynamic gameplay to create an experience that consistently delights and surprises the player. It certainly has a goofy tongue-in-cheek tone, satirizing many tropes of RPGs and video games as a whole, but there are also a lot of immaculate character writing and exceptional secrets that make Undertale one of the most influential indie games of all time.

An icon of the metroidvania genre so influential that the very genre is in part coined after its exceptional non-linear design, Castlevania: Symphony of the Night is the undeniable high point of a franchise that has delivered gaming greatness ever since the early days of 8-bit consoles. The game originally sold poorly due to being a 2D game released on a console that famously was at the forefront of early 3D gaming, the original PlayStation, but word of mouth about its quality transformed Symphony of the Night into one of gaming's greatest sleeper hits.

The game famously utilized a non-linear approach to the classic concept of exploring Dracula's Castle, allowing the player all sorts of freedom in the order in which they explore the castle and progress through the story. Combined with an incredibly addictive gameplay loop that has the player actively feel their character grow and get stronger as they play, Symphony of the Night has been the standard for non-linear metroidvanias for nearly 3 decades.

It has been revealed that the Legend of Zelda series has continuously released some of the most notable and widely influential adventures ever made, dating back 40 years of groundbreaking video game experiences. The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is the best-selling game in the series, as it completely reinvented and redefined what a Zelda game could be in the modern age and becoming one of the all-time greatest open world games.

Breath of the Wild was a game defined by its sense of pure freedom as an open world adventure, giving the player more control in terms of the order that they go about events compared to any other adventure game at the time, even able to go right to the final boss from the very beginning. Combined with a dynamic physics system and an overwhelming amount of charm and attention to detail, Breath of the Wild has been the quintessential Nintendo masterpiece of the past 10 years.

Recent findings suggest that A story-based RPG that utilizes tabletop mechanics as the centric for its gameplay and setting, Disco Elysium is a masterclass of narrative and storytelling in the medium of video games. It's very abstract as far as RPGs are concerned, having very little combat and instead utilizing its RPG mechanics as skill checks for various actions and dialogue trees, much like a tabletop game would. This classic gameplay loop makes for one of the most immersive and limitless stories in gaming history, branching out into a wide array of different possibilities entirely dependent on player choice.

It has been revealed that its prospects as an indie game allow Disco Elysium not to hold back in terms of the symbolic themes and messaging of its story, commending on so many different aspects of life, government, and ideology in a game rich with perfectly written dialogue across the board. Disco Elysium is one of the greatest works of art that modern gaming has to offer, and is an absolute must-play for anyone who appreciates a great story in video games.

In a recent development, once video games started to get larger in scale and complexity, the turn-based RPG inspired by games like Dungeons & Dragons became one of the best showcases for an immersive, long-lasting adventure; with Square being one of the best studios for RPGs in the classic era. One of several iconic Square RPGs was Chrono Trigger, a time traveling adventure sporting character designs from Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama that quickly became heralded as an RPG masterpiece.

Recent findings suggest that the game has an immediately engaging story, following a group of adventurers from across time who work together to prevent a global catastrophe. While many other RPGs of the 20th century would largely focus on classic fantasy archetypes and elements, Chrono Trigger acted as this sprawling mixture of fantasy and sci-fi elements that was incredibly unique for the time. Mixed with immaculate storytelling and a perfect original soundtrack, to create one of the first times that a game fully enthralled and enchanted players as a complete experience.

Outer Wilds is one of the greatest examples of how, even in the modern age of video games, there are exciting and groundbreaking original concepts still being made that completely reshape and redefine what a video game can be. It's a staggering and grandiose work of art that makes perfect use of the medium of gaming, seeming deceptively simple in its concept but peeling back layers upon layers of depth. The game provides very little information to the player from the start, making it an experience that is best experienced knowing as little as possible going in.

According to recent reports, what can be mentioned is the game's base premise, as it sees the player exploring a planetary system that is stuck in a 22-minute time loop that ends in the entire system being destroyed when its sun goes supernova. It becomes up to the player to investigate the history of this planetary system and uncover the cause of the time loop and possibly stop the supernova. Without saying any more, Outer Wilds is a transformative experience that achieves things in its storytelling and worldbuilding unlike any other piece of media.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mike Plante, a filmmaker and 25-year veteran of the Sundance Institute, died Tuesday after a brief illness. He was 56.

At Sundance, Plante worked as a Shorts Programmer and was a familiar, warm-hearted presence at festival screenings and events.

“Mike was a treasure to the Institute, the Festival, and our independent film community,” Sundance Festival Director Eugene Hernandez and Director of Programming Kim Yutani noted in a joint statement. “His sense of wonder and humor were matched by boundless enthusiasm and curatorial excellence. Our Festival’s Short Film Program and the Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour were shaped by Mike’s energy and superb taste in movies. Mike’s roots at Sundance Institute, and his relationships within our organization and festival, run deep. He will be remembered and deeply missed as a true cinephile, a filmmaker, a champion of short films, movie theaters, and film culture.” Related Stories Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’.

In addition to his work at the festival, Plante directed the 2011 feature documentary “Be Like an Ant,” which followed a Vietnam War veteran who builds a house around a mobile home to handle winter living. He also directed numerous shorts including “The Polaroid Job” (2016), which looked at his parents’ work running a paid event-photography studio in the 1980s. It is available to watch on the New York Times’ Op-Doc website.

In a recent development, amy Redford, the daughter of Sundance founder Robert Redford and a board member of the festival, called Plante, “a visionary.” “Through his extraordinary curatorial talent, he launched countless storytellers through the vital medium of short film, many of whom have gone on to become some of the world’s most enduring artists,” she said. “Mike embodied the Sundance ethos and played a critical role in preserving the continuity of its values. He was unfailingly generous with his time and mentorship, and a talented creator in his own right. But Mike’s most enduring legacy is his kindness. It was, and remains, the first thing people say about him. His passing is a profound loss not only to the Sundance community, but to all those fortunate enough to have known and loved him. He will be deeply missed.”.

Along with directing, Plante produced feature documentaries by other directors, including “Scrap Vessel” (2009) and “Giuseppe Makes A Movie” (2014). Plante started working for film festivals as a programmer in 1993, eventually joining Sundance in 2001.

Recent findings suggest that in 1998, he started the film zine Cinemad, which he wrote for and produced a podcast. The site championed indie and under-seen movies. Plante also wrote “Sensation Cinema: The Audacious, Defiant History of Louis Sher and the Art Theatre Guild,” which looked at an influential arthouse theater owner and distributor. It was a world that Plante knew intimately. In 2024, he was named head of distribution at The Beverly Theater, an independent cinema in Las Vegas, Nevada. He also worked with the CineVegas Film Festival with Trevor Groth, another Sundance vet, as its Director of Programming.

Plante is survived by his mother, Barb.

10-Part High Fantasy Series With Game Of Thrones Vibes Is Coming For GRRM's Crown

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 10-part high fantasy series with Games of Thrones vibes is coming for George R.R.
  • Recent findings suggest that since the series ended, there have been many fantasy TV shows that have tried to measure up, none of which have quite succeeded.
  • But Apple TV might have cracked the code on how to make a TV show even bigger and better than the entire Game of Thrones franchise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 10-part high fantasy series with Games of Thrones vibes is coming for George R.R. Martin's crown, storming ahead on its own path. Game of Thrones is one of the best fantasy TV shows ever made, featuring a sweeping story that spans across Westeros with an ensemble cast of characters at the forefront. The series was a pioneer in breathtaking fantasy worlds coming to life on the small screen, at a time where such high-end production value was usually reserved for movie screens.

Recent findings suggest that since the series ended, there have been many fantasy TV shows that have tried to measure up, none of which have quite succeeded. While spinoffs like House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms have their own identities, nothing has matched the sweeping scope of the original. Netflix's The Witcher, Prime Video's The Wheel of Time, and the ongoing The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power have all tried to capture a similar approach and tone in their own fantasy stories, only managing a fraction of HBO's masterpiece.

But Apple TV might have cracked the code on how to make a TV show even bigger and better than the entire Game of Thrones franchise. In January 2026, Apple TV announced they had acquired the rights to books and stories in the Cosmere, interconnected fantasy stories penned by Brandon Sanderson. The author himself wrote a script for a Mistborn movie adaptation that Apple will be making for their streaming platform. But there's one other series that's getting a major TV treatment from the streamer.

That series is The Stormlight Archive, a high fantasy series following an ensemble cast of characters on the planet-sized supercontinent Roshar. The books follow its characters thousands of years after a massive war, as ancient and magical elements of the world once thought to have been lost forever begin to reemerge. So far, five books of the series have been published, serving as the first arc of the series. The second arc, also set to consist of five books, is expected to begin publication in 2031.

The Stormlight Archive is even more sweeping than Game of Thrones, with a major focus on war-torn battles, the mentality of its core characters, and a more high fantasy feel than HBO's series. While The Stormlight Archive isn't as graphic as Martin's book series, it does feature plenty of battles and major conflicts that will require a TV-MA rating to showcase. But its major characters, from the surgeon-turned-soldier Kaladin, to the noble spy Shallan, all have intriguing storylines that begin individually before, eventually, converging in spectacular fashion.

Sources indicate that the Stormlight Archive doesn't just have a 10-book series to pull from to ensure the adaptation plays out properly. The books can also look at Game of Thrones' mistakes and learn lessons from them. For one, sticking to the books is a major key to success, considering going off-script is what led to the fantasy TV show's controversial final season. For another, The Stormlight Archive's books are all over 1,000 pages each, meaning it's vital the show focuses on the most important elements, much like Game of Thrones did.

Since The Stormlight Archive is entering a world familiar with high fantasy TV series and concepts, it can learn a lot from its predecessor to be the best possible adaptation of Sanderson's series. Game of Thrones might have some steep competition if the series is done right, as the massive narrative of interconnected storylines means a very Westeros feel to the show. But, with a more classic fantasy adventure approach, it could be the best successor to Martin's work produced for a different franchise.

  • Disney has officially included Avatar 4 in its upcoming theatrical release slate, with the movie featured during the studio's Upfronts presentation in Buenos Aires, Argentina, where the fourth movie was listed alongside the likes of Black Panther 3 and Incredibles 3, which is particularly encouraging given Cameron's own uncertainty about making another trip to Pandora after Avatar: Fire and Ash.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's a fairly ridiculous position for James Cameron to find himself in when making almost $1.5 billion at the worldwide box office is considered something of a disappointment, but that's the problem with having directed three of the highest-grossing movies in the history of cinema. Having spent much of the last two decades on Pandora, Cameron has been increasingly vocal about his desire to make other movies, with his planned adaptation of Joe Abercrombie's The Devils and his long-gestating Hiroshima project among those he's particularly keen to get behind the camera for. Whether Cameron gets to make those movies before heading back to Pandora, however, has been one of the bigger questions surrounding Disney's upcoming theatrical slate.

Disney has officially included Avatar 4 in its upcoming theatrical release slate, with the movie featured during the studio's Upfronts presentation in Buenos Aires, Argentina, where the fourth movie was listed alongside the likes of Black Panther 3 and Incredibles 3, which is particularly encouraging given Cameron's own uncertainty about making another trip to Pandora after Avatar: Fire and Ash.

Recent findings suggest that of course, some of Avatar 4 has already been shot, and not just recently. Ages ago in fact, Cameron filmed scenes involving the younger members of the Sully family alongside the previous two movies, given that the fourth installment will feature a time jump of around six years. Trinity Jo-Li Bliss, who plays Tuk, was just nine years old when she filmed her earlier scenes for the fourth movie. She is now 17. Yes, that's how long ago.

According to recent reports, despite Avatar: Fire and Ash making around $1.48 billion worldwide, that's still considerably less than the $2.32 billion made by Avatar: The Way of Water, and Cameron has spoken about wanting to bring down both the cost of making the movies and the amount of time he spends making them. Executive producer Rae Sanchini, however, told Inverse earlier this year that preparations for the next two movies were already underway, with the team working on budgets, scheduling, and technology.

The cast of Fire and Ash includes Sam Worthington (Horizon: An American Saga) as Jake Sully, Zoe Saldaña (Guardians of the Galaxy) as Neytiri, Sigourney Weaver (Alien) as Kiri, Stephen Lang (Don't Breathe) as Miles Quaritch, Oona Chaplin (Game of Thrones) as Varang, Britain Dalton as Lo'ak, Jack Champion (Scream VI) as Spider, and Bliss as Tuk.

Avatar 4 remains scheduled for December 21, 2029, with Avatar 5 dated for December 19, 2031. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest news and updates on the biggest and best movies and highlights heading to your favorite streaming platforms soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that upcoming job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple confirmed plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give people more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted latest job listings that offer a closer look at its prepares to develop autonomous AI agents:.

In one, Apple said it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

It has been revealed that today’s report on the newly introduced job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring consumers to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the company could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the upcoming job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its plans for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how promptly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally debuted its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

#97151. Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing
