Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves.
  • According to recent reports, 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition.
  • “COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse, told IndieWire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves. The 1948 Paramount Decrees (named after the studio that pioneered the vertical integration) required studios to give up one of the three options. They decided to give up exhibition. The choice was easy: With low margins on ticket sales and the need to constantly bring audiences in, who wanted to run a movie theater?

According to recent reports, 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition. The rise of streaming was stated to bring about the end of theaters as we know them. But the COVID-19 pandemic brought exhibition to its closest brink of extinction yet. Related Stories Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56 Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination?

“COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse, told IndieWire.

According to recent reports, after the global pandemic, lockdown protocols forced movie theaters to close for months. The luxury theater chain Arclight shuttered all its locations within weeks. Locations closed at a variety of companies, including Alamo Drafthouse. Some theaters survived off of private rentals. Even as theaters slowly reopened, COVID protocols required leaving some seats empty, meaning not all tickets could be sold.

Recent findings suggest that “I think there was no right move,” League added. “We laid most of our people off. We spent a lot of energy trying to build up a TVOD streaming platform which didn’t entirely work for a lot of reasons… And so we went through bankruptcy, and it was rough. We just ran out of money.”.

“There really was no strategy,” noted Greg Laemmle, owner of the California-based independent theater chain Laemmle Theatres. Since Los Angeles did not allow private rentals, the company stayed afloat via concessions, pop-up events, and some virtual cinema opportunities. “It was all just trying to understand how we can maintain contact.”.

Exhibition became such an unappetizing business that many of those who jumped on board the irony-fueled GameStop stock inflation of 2021 also bought shares of AMC Theatres, bringing the company to an all-time high in valuation.

It has been revealed that but years later, the theater market is experiencing a rebirth. Driven by new theater operators and new kinds of theatrical experiences, the contemporary exhibition landscape looks very different from 10 years ago.

Theater operators paint a picture of an industry that is no longer weathering a storm. Instead, they reveal the trends driving theaters to thrive and the issues with the model that won’t seem to die.

The first high-profile artist-led theater acquisition was Quentin Tarantino’s purchase of the New Beverly Cinema in Los Angeles. The director had previously helped fund his childhood theater to keep it afloat before buying the cinema outright and taking over as programmer in 2014. The purchase of the 300-seat New Beverly was partly fueled by Tarantino’s desire to preserve what the digital era sought to make extinct: celluloid projection. Since the director’s acquisition, the theater proudly boasts that it screens only on film, usually 35mm.

Tarantino declined to comment on this story.

A few years later, COVID-19 brought a new threat to movie theaters. A similar mission-driven attitude took hold in a new crop of directors and artists: to protect not just how movies are screened, but to ensure audiences can still see them in communal spaces.

In a recent development, independent film director Kevin Smith bought his hometown theater in Atlantic Highlands, Fresh Jersey, in 2024. The Atlantic Twin Cinema was a five-screen multiplex Smith grew up going to, housed in a building over 100 years old. But over time, nearby multiplexes threatened to drive the theater out of business. When Smith’s friend Ernie O’Donnell told him the theater would be torn down to build condos, he resolved to help save it.

Sources indicate that “Anything I ever learned about myself I never learned in a classroom, and I certainly didn’t learn it sitting in a church,” Smith told IndieWire. “But mostly everything I know about myself I learned sitting in the darkness of that theater, looking up at the great white mirror and seeing life reflected back at me.”.

Smith invested $450,000 and partnered with several friends to buy the theater, rebranding it as Smodcastle Cinemas. While he mostly lives in Los Angeles, Smith travels to Jersey every month to work on the theater.

Smith described how the finances of owning a theater in a small town may not always reflect larger box office trends. “Avatar: The Way of Water” opened in 2024 and eventually grossed over $2 billion, making it one of the most successful films in history. But at Smodcastle Cinemas, they only sold 12 tickets opening weekend.

Industry observers note that at Smodcastle, the theater has leaned into what Smith calls “The business of Kevin Smith.” This includes Q&As of his films featuring Smith and his collaborators like Justin Long for a “Tusk” screening, and Tracy Morgan for the 15th anniversary of “Cop Out.” The theater started a film festival to help showcase local Newly introduced Jersey cinema. Smith was working on selling a reality show about the theater’s day-to-day operations, similar to the seven-season run of “Comic Book Men” filmed inside the comic shop he owns, but said progress has stalled.

“I love calling up Ernie and being like, ‘How many seats [have we sold] so far?’ And he’ll be like ‘120 out of 230,’ and I’m like, ‘All right man, I gotta put 90 more asses in seats. Let me see if I can jump on a radio show… go over to Manhattan and jump on “Good Day New York” and try to get the word out,’” Smith explained. “It’s fun, but it is definitely fucking work. I have a feeling Quentin don’t work nearly as fucking hard at his theater.”.

Smith elaborated on the work it takes to keep the theater running, “We all got together and saved the theater, man. But it was the worst financial fucking decision I ever made,” Smith remarked. “Owning a movie theater in the 21st-century post-COVID [world], it’s a dicey proposition at best… We became a nonprofit theater because the movie theater’s never going into fucking profit.”.

It has been revealed that the nonprofit model has become an increasingly popular option for keeping theaters alive. In 2012, Los Angeles video rental store Vidiots transitioned to a nonprofit to stay afloat, recasting its mission around film preservation, protection, and education. The organization later received heavy support from Megan Ellison’s Annapurna Pictures, which kept the tech giant running for two years after it shuttered its store in 2017.

“If you go across the country, you’re seeing a real boom in nonprofit or community-supported movie theaters,” remarked Laemmle. He highlighted the Tasveer Film Center in Seattle, which reopened the former Ark Lodge Cinemas in 2025 due to support from a local nonprofit that had run a South Asian film festival.

“Why not form a community organization that augments ticket sales with other sources of revenue, or that can take advantage of their not-for-profit status and do the enhanced kind of programming that you can’t do at a for-profit business?” noted Laemmle.

The high costs of running a movie theater are also evident in one of the latest major theater purchases by an artist. Director Jason Reitman led a group of 30 filmmakers — including Christopher Nolan, Guillermo del Toro, Steven Spielberg, and Chloé Zhao — to purchase the historic Village Theater in Westwood, Los Angeles, in 2024. Since rebranding as Directors Village, the theater has partnered with the film nonprofit American Cinematheque, which will handle its programming.

The $12 million acquisition in 2024 rescued the historic theater after its lease with its former owner expired. The filmmakers will pour an additional $25 million into renovating the theater, which was open for programming in summer 2026 but closed in October and will reopen in 2027. The project required an alleged six-figure minimum buy-in from the artists involved.

According to recent reports, jason Reitman declined to comment through a representative, citing that it is too early to discuss plans for the theater’s renovation. American Cinematheque did not respond to requests for comment.

It has been revealed that jason Reitman and Co. also looked into purchasing the adjacent Bruin Theater but were ultimately deterred by the extensive cost of renovations, as previously reported by IndieWire.

It has been revealed that the list of artists owning theaters is only growing. Kristen Stewart purchased the historic Highland Theatre in Los Angeles in February 2026 and plans to restore the space into a hub for the L.A. film community. Tarantino bought a second LA theater, the Vista, in 2021. Martin Scorsese, Ethan Hawke, and Frances McDormand joined the advisory board of the Upper West Side Cinema Center to turn the former Metro Theater on Broadway in New York City into a five-screen arthouse theater, funded by New York City grants and donors like the Kate Capshaw and Steven Spielberg Hearthland Foundation.

The trend highlights a newly introduced form of altruism by creatives seeking to keep theaters alive. But even if the business isn’t financially valuable, there is an argument for artists to be seen as patrons of their craft. “As more and more movie theaters start closing down, every filmmaker is from somewhere, and every filmmaker has their hometown theater,” stated Smith. “And if you have a degree of success where you’ve got some side hustle loot and whatnot, what a great way to spend your money.”.

It has been revealed that in 2019, the Department of Justice marked the Paramount Decrees for termination, citing changes in the studio system structure and film market that rendered the law obsolete. In August 2020, while most theaters in the United States were shuttered, the Department of Justice ended the decree.

In November 2019, Netflix revealed it would lease Latest York City’s historic Paris Theater, three months after a notice of closure was posted. In May 2020, the streamer bought the closed Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood to be co-programmed between the studio and its previous operator, American Cinematheque. In October 2021, Netflix also announced it would take over the lease of the Bay Theater in the Pacific Palisades.

It has been revealed that these acquisitions had a touch of irony considering Netflix made a name for itself by rejecting theatrical exhibition. The streamer did not abide by the then-standard 90-day exhibition window before making its films available on the service. The Academy Awards require week-long theatrical runs to make films eligible for awards. Major chains like AMC Theatres and Regal Cinemas refused to show Netflix films (and still do on occasion; Regal and Cinemark recently unveiled they will not screen “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” due to the shortened theatrical window). But just as it became legal for Netflix to enter the theater market, it did. By becoming an exhibitor, it no longer needed major theaters to show its films.

According to recent reports, “Netflix needs screens in the L.A. and Fresh York market,” stated James Huntsman, the co-founder of distribution organization Blue Fox Entertainment Group, which purchased two former iPic theaters in June 2026. “I don’t care if you are Netflix, it’s really hard to get a screen in both of those two markets… So if you’re Netflix and you have six movies that are coming out between October and December and they all need qualifying runs of seven days, full runs in both markets, now you start seeing why they’re interested in screens.”.

Amazon Studios opened The Culver Theater — the former Culver City Arclight location, which shuttered in March 2020 after the company went bankrupt due to closures from the COVID-19 pandemic — in December 2022. The theater screens a mix of latest releases, repertory screenings, and hosts premieres for Amazon MGM Studios’ television shows and movies.

It has been revealed that in October 2026, Paramount Pictures announced it took over the lease for the Bay Theater, which has been closed since the 2025 Palisades fires. The fresh theater, opened in November 2026 and operated by The Lot, similarly offers first-run theatrical releases from all studios, along with dine-in food.

Industry observers note that “We’ll see if it really develops into anything more than just a novelty for them,” mentioned Laemmle about studios purchasing individual theaters. “[They’re] one-offs and just being able to want to say that they’ve got something. But I don’t sense there’s going to be a more prolonged investment, but if it happens, it’d be great.”.

The most high-profile studio entrance into the movie theater market was Sony Pictures Entertainment’s acquisition of theater chain Alamo Drafthouse in 2024. Founded by Karrie and Tim League in 1997, the manufacturer made its name as an offbeat theater option with dine-in service and strict rules against talking and phone use in its theaters.

Industry observers note that “I think we came to it from people who loved movies but didn’t really love our options with chain theaters that we had around,” remarked Tim League. “We were always looking at how we can build this and build a community around sharing movies we love.”.

Alamo Drafthouse began talks with Sony Pictures Entertainment in late 2023 before completing the sale in 2024.

“It was kind of essential to find a upcoming partner as soon as we ran out of money,” said League, who has since stepped back from daily operations at the tech giant and remains involved as Strategic Advisor.

“Why it was appealing for us as a tech giant with our board prior to deciding that Sony was the right acquirer for us is partly because of what that also meant in terms of resources that Sony could offer… Not only in terms of Sony [being] a very significant, well-capitalized company but reputationally, very financially stable, [and] very well respected in the space,” noted Michael Kustermann, CEO of Alamo Drafthouse and head of Sony Pictures Experiences.

According to recent reports, sony is not involved with day-to-day operations of Alamo Drafthouse. But the parent organization’s ownership is evident in occasional special programming, such as airing the Season 4 finale of “Breaking Bad,” which Sony’s TV division produced, in Alamo theaters in September 2026 to celebrate protagonist Walter White’s birthday.

But the largest initiative made possible by Sony’s ownership was the July 2026 announcement that Alamo Drafthouse would purchase the historic Cinerama Dome theater in Hollywood and the attached 14-screen multiplex.

According to recent reports, “This has been the white whale for Alamo for a long time,” remarked Kustermann. He explained Alamo was interested in the location before the Sony deal but didn’t have the financial means to acquire a latest flagship location. But after a couple of years of interest and conversations that did not progress, Alamo reached back out after the Sony deal and began serious talks in 2025.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant looks to operate the Cinerama Dome screen unlike traditional Alamo theaters. Dine-in service will not be offered. Kustermann remarked that the renovations will be minimal, aiming to keep a similar seat count. The iconic curved screen that defined Cinerama projection will remain, and reprints of films screened in Cinerama such as “It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World” will be part of the programming slate.

Renovations to the multiplex will include adding one or two 70mm projectors, karaoke rooms, an updated bar, and an aesthetic redesign inspired by the theater’s 1960s decor.

Industry observers note that blue Fox Entertainment was founded in 2015. The North American distribution and film sales organization distributes over a dozen films a year across a variety of genres.“Exhibition is where all the glamour is, right?” said Huntsman. “Distribution is very labor-intensive; you’re supplying content to a theater, to a platform, to DVD. It’s very back office, administrative.”.

According to recent reports, “I only got into distribution as a way to get into exhibition,” Huntsman explained, adding that Blue Fox Entertainment bought its two theaters to combine the manufacturer’s passion for film and enter a new market. “I make no qualms. I’m in the money business, but I’m using movie theaters and film distribution and film sales to do that.”.

Industry observers note that when the dine-in theater chain iPic went bankrupt in 2026, Blue Fox bid on six of the 12 available locations and ultimately purchased the Westwood, Los Angeles, and New York City theaters. The dine-in service was removed, but each location has a full-service restaurant attached that does not require a cinema ticket.

By rebranding as The Cinemas, Huntsman aims to turn the theaters into viable assets that can make money beyond box office revenue. “I have private events, I have two restaurants at these locations, I do advertisements around the exterior. So if you put all that together, it’s not a bad business. If it was just a standalone straight movie theater, it’s a tough market.”.

The economics of why so many upcoming independent theaters are popping up can be traced to a basic reality of the business, according to Laemmle: the simplicity in bringing a theater back to life. “You don’t need to pay anything to acquire inventory. It’s not like opening a bodega where you’ve got to fill it with stuff. You get a film, you promise to pay a percentage of the box office to the studio, and suddenly you’re in business.”.

Ticket split rates can vary per title. The rate can be anywhere from 30% for repertory screenings to over 60% for a blockbuster Disney release. Some studios send a range of split rates that can be negotiated; others (like Disney) set a non-negotiable rate.

It has been revealed that A film’s success can also affect how much a theater owner makes per ticket sale. Speaking to this summer’s releases, Huntsman said that the underperformance of films like “Supergirl” and “Moana” meant he received a larger portion of the box office. But for big hits like “Toy Story 5,” theaters get a smaller piece of the action.

Studios can also control exhibition through clean policies: the practice that if a theater licenses a certain film, it must be on screen when the theater is open. These policies can be especially detrimental to single-screen theaters in rural areas, effectively limiting the variety of films a community can show.

At Smodcastle, Smith planned special programming with Vulgathon, a marathon of all the films in his View Askew universe from “Clerks” to “Clerks III” in order. But while ticket sales were tracking to sell out all 900 seats across five screens, Disney stated that if the theater did not leave a screen open for the second weekend of “Deadpool and Wolverine,” the studio would not send them the film to screen for its opening weekend.

“So we had to leave one screen open, for fucking ‘Deadpool’ and shit, that did not sell out,” Smith said.

Advertising revenue also dropped dramatically post-COVID, according to Laemmle. He estimates that the company at the moment makes 25% of its pre-pandemic revenue through theater advertising. “Ad agencies had a budget that they allocated for in-theater advertising in the pre-pandemic world. All of a sudden, movie theaters were closed so they just took those same ad dollars and moved them somewhere else…That was a significant source of contribution to the bottom line that’s really gone.”.

Loss of advertising revenue forces theaters to find new revenue streams. For some major chains like AMC and Regal, that includes pay-for-play trailer programming: where studios can pay to put trailers for their upcoming releases in front of new titles. This also incentivizes longer trailer blocks that can run up to 30 minutes.

Other major sources of revenue for theaters are concessions, which can offer high margins for cheap snacks like popcorn and pre-packaged candy. Beer and wine sales have also been a major boost of revenue for Laemmle Theatres.

The other option: Lean into alternative programming that may not incur as high ticket splits. The Cinemas has been experimenting with testing various repertory titles across different genres to figure out what titles will draw people back into theaters. Their upcoming lineup for November and December 2026 includes “Boyz in the Hood,” “When Harry Met Sally,” and “The Lord of the Rings” trilogy.

Industry observers note that for Huntsman, the need for theaters to diversify revenue reflects the current model for how studios release films. “When I grew up seeing movies in theaters primarily in the ‘80s, there were like three studio releases every week…There was always the rom-com, the horror film, the action film, the indie film…Now it’s ‘Fast and the Furious’ comes out, and nobody releases anything for three weeks.” Huntsman added, “So in terms of profitability, [that’s] part of why we’re making the theater a destination.”.

In a recent development, rising labor, rent, and electric bills over the last few years have made it harder for theaters to improve their margins. In a search for more profits, theater operators have taken on new initiatives to upgrade the technologies and amenities associated with theater-going to bring in crowds looking for a more premium experience, with varying degrees of success.

For Alamo Drafthouse, the Sony-owned manufacturer received complaints from longtime fans in 2026 after introducing mobile ordering to its theaters, replacing the original pen-and-paper method that involved more engagement with servers. Instead, guests scan QR codes to place orders that are sent directly to the kitchen.

Industry observers note that this move drew ire from the Alamo community, who saw it as hypocritical to the organization’s prominent No Phones policy. The company’s subreddit became flooded with users saying they wouldn’t be returning to the theater amid the changes. Actor Elijah Wood, an Austin local who frequently appeared at events put on by the chain, criticized the upcoming system, calling it “truly awful” in a post on X.

The organization described the QR code ordering system as part of a larger strategy to ensure long-term stability and keep innovating the experience, citing past changes like introducing reserved seating and ending its adults-only policy.

According to recent reports, an Alamo spokesperson said that the tech giant has not laid off any staff due to introducing QR codes and that it allows servers to handle more tabs. They added the core of the decision was to protect wages and jobs for the company’s staff working 12 months a year, but that QR codes will allow them to hire fewer seasonal staffers.

Tim League declined to comment on the QR code system.

It has been revealed that while Alamo Drafthouse pioneered the dine-in model for theaters, League’s newest business venture is to bring exhibition into the luxury space. He released Metro Private Cinema in 2025, a 20-screen theater in New York City’s Chelsea neighborhood that specializes in small, private theater experiences with fine-dining menus to accompany the films.

Recent findings suggest that theaters range from four to 20 seats. Bookings start at four hours, and food packages are added to the price. Guests can choose between new releases, special holiday-themed programming, or a specific movie, plus a la carte food.

Recent findings suggest that “Since the dawn of cinema, it has been being tightly packed into a large room with a bunch of strangers,” remarked League. “So what if we kind of flip that around, and it’s you’re surrounded by friends. And how does that change the experience?”.

Pricing for the experience can vary. Example packages on the website list costs starting around $200 per person. When asked about introducing a luxury price point into the theater market, League explains that costs align with the high prices commonplace in the city. “Our meals are $115 for a 13-course meal, which is very much in line with Fresh York pricing.” League added, “We have built a more higher-end, expensive model, but I think what we’re offering is not ridiculous.”.

If companies are not expanding the price-point of concessions, the other option is to expand the theatrical viewing experience itself. Sony Pictures Entertainment released Cosm, a 364-seat immersive theater with an 87-foot curved screen, in 2024. Tickets are roughly $50, with some including themed food options. And massive Las Vegas entertainment complex The Sphere received over $400 million in revenue from sales of its multisensory AI-edited run of “The Wizard of Oz.”.

In recent years, audiences have shown growing interest in premium theater presentations. Major studio blockbusters are expected to have exclusive IMAX runs. Films like “Sinners” and “The Odyssey” have driven a rise in interest in IMAX 70mm screenings, letting audiences see movies in the format directors intended.

Industry observers note that CJ 4DPlex, the developer of premium screening formats ScreenX and 4DX theaters, reported a 26% increase in revenue in the first half of 2026 compared to 2025. Their technology includes 270-degree panoramic presentations or immersive 4DX theaters with moving seats and water effects. Ticket surcharges can range from $3 to $7 for ScreenX showings and up to $10 for 4DX tickets, compared to a traditional 2D ticket.

Industry observers note that but the desire to jump into premium formats is not universal. Laemmle remarked his theaters have no plans to offer advanced presentations. “We’re not necessarily engaged in the large format with the higher ticket price because we believe that movie-going should be something that’s done regularly…Moviegoing historically was the cheapest form of out-of-home entertainment, and we believe it should stay that way.”.

The movie theater industry has always existed on a wire’s edge. Owners and monopolies have come and gone. Projection trends like Cinerama and Vistavision had their moments before becoming obsolete. Television, VHS, DVDs, and streaming have all carried the threat of being the final innovation that would put theatergoing in the past forever.

Sources indicate that “The death of our industry has been predicted since the ‘50s with every new turn,” said League. “I just think there’s [now] pressure not to lose sight of the fragility of being an awesome third space.”.

2026 is right now on track to have the best box office performance globally since 2019, with the year expected to end with $35.7 billion in global ticket sales.

According to recent reports, for Huntsman, the increase is corollary to the output the studios offer: that the box office success of “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is more tied to quality than any other metric. “Anyone that says, ‘Oh, movie theaters are back,” they didn’t go anywhere. There just weren’t any good movies playing.”.

At Laemmle Theatres, the biggest draws of the year have been indie success stories, with films like “You Can See Everything,” “NAZA,” and “Filipiñana” bringing the theater some of its largest ticket sales.

Speaking with a variety of theater operators, the common thread in running a successful theater wasn’t what was on the screen. The key was understanding each theater’s audience. For Laemmle Theatres, it’s typically older people who go to the movies often and have a wide variety of tastes. At Metro Cinema, it’s Latest Yorkers with the funds to splurge on an elevated experience for special occasions. And at Smodcastle, it’s Kevin Smith fans looking for programming only Kevin Smith can provide.

According to recent reports, the full scale of how COVID-19 changed culture has yet to be fully realized. But the renewed investment in owning and innovating movie theaters speaks to a broader desire to safeguard community spaces where people can exist between work and home. The theater industry’s revenue streams are more diversified than they’ve been in years. The allure of owning a movie theater isn’t just about making money; public goodwill has added intangible rewards for exhibitors for keeping theaters alive.

Or as Smith said, “It’s good for the heart, good for the soul, good for the optics, good for the brand.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there's no doubt that 2026 has been a really exciting year for Pokémon fans all over the world, as the franchise we have all grown up adoring finally celebrates its 30th birthday. That meant all kinds of exciting announcements from those continue to chart its course, and we got plenty of fascinating release designed to mark the occasion too.

Arguably the biggest of those was confirmation of the first games of the tenth generation, Winds and Waves, which are set to release in the latter half of 2027. The newly introduced region featured in those is based on the archipelagos of South-East Asia, and it looks like a major departure from anything else we've seen to date, something which the series has arguably needed after treading water for a while.

With that in mind, the fact that we haven't reached the tenth generation yet should mean that any info about Gen 11 is far out of the question. That might not be the case though, as recent information seems to touch on exactly what players can expect next.

In a recent development, over on Reddit, one user shared a post featuring information gained during the infamous Teraleak, which contained thousands of internal files from developer Game Freak. Within that, there were timelines explaining exactly what they were planning to do next (at the time, at the very least), and it could be the most monumental shift we have seen in years.

Specifically, the developer is seemingly planning a fresh kind of RPG set across all the regions that are based on Japan, namely Kanto, Johto, Hoenn, and Sinnoh. That would be a huge project, and something which fans have been putting together for themselves for a while now, via recompilation projects based on older games.

In a recent development, an official release in that ilk would be huge though, and there is supposedly also a proposal to introduce the 11th generation at around the same time, which would make it one of the most fundamentally changing moments in the franchise's history. That could mean a four year cycle for generations is going to become the norm, though Winds and Waves is coming later than expected to make room for the 30th anniversary.

Industry observers note that fans in the responses speculated on what a project that substantial could look like, with one saying, "It would be interesting to see what sort of story they went with. The criminal organizations include thieves who report to their mafia boss, two extremist groups attempting to terraform the planet, and a nihilistic man who wants to delete the planet entirely. I can’t see any of them working together well.".

"Remake of the first 4 regions, in a similar graphics style to black and white, with things like Mega Evolution and modern quality of life features, with a proper battle frontier. I'd love this kind of game," another added.

Whatever does end up happening, we are likely still more than a few years away from seeing it for ourselves, but with Pokémon in a great place right now, it's probably best to just sit back and enjoy it anyway.

Pokémon is a Japanese multimedia franchise created by Satoshi Tajiri and Ken Sugimori, debuted by Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures in 1996. Centered on fictional creatures called Pokémon, the series spans video games, trading cards, animation, films, merchandise, and competitive events. Players assume the role of Trainers who capture, battle, and trade Pokémon. It is one of the highest-grossing entertainment franchises in history.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with latest privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful update, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and people on the public beta can now try out these newly introduced features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you wanted to be a completionist for the movies of documentary legend Frederick Wiseman, or if you have a blind spot for Wiseman’s formalist portraits of American institutions dating back decades, today is your lucky day.

Janus Films has acquired the North American distribution rights to the complete collection of 45 feature films from Wiseman’s career dating back to his seminal “Titicut Follies” in 1967, and Janus plans to distribute all of them beginning January 1, 2027. Janus already has a library that includes the works of Agnès Varda, Ingmar Bergman, Akira Kurosawa, Chantal Akerman, and Edward Yang, so Wiseman finds himself in good company. Related Stories Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56.

Specific distribution aims haven’t been confirmed yet, be it whether these films are going to be seen theatrically, via streaming, or on physical release. But Wiseman’s early films, everything from “Titicut Follies” in 1967 through “State Legislature” in 2007 have been restored in 4K by Wiseman’s Zipporah Films. “La Danse” (2009) through his final feature “Menus-Plaisirs – Les Troisgros” (2023) will be available in their original digital formats.

This is the first time any distributor other than Zipporah Films is licensing Wiseman’s work in North America, so the hope is that the late documentarian can now reach an even greater audience. It wasn’t until as recently as 2024, that Wiseman’s movies were even all available in digital formats.

“We couldn’t imagine a better home in North America for Frederick Wiseman’s films than with Janus Films,” stated Karen Konicek of Zipporah Films. “It has been an honor to work alongside Fred for so many decades, producing and distributing his films. As Zipporah Films continues as the rights holder and distributor of the Wiseman Collection, we very much look forward to this latest partnership with Janus Films and are excited to collaborate with them.”.

“We are honored and thrilled to be the first distributor, in the US, outside of Zipporah Films, to be entrusted with licensing one of the greatest bodies of work in American cinema” said Peter Becker, President of Janus Films and Criterion. “We’re looking forward to presenting these monumental works, theatrically, to newly introduced audiences across the country.”.

It has been revealed that wiseman passed away earlier this year in February 2026 at 96 years old. Not only was he one of the most influential documentarians in American cinema, he was one of the most prolific considering the 45 features he independently produced, directed, and edited over his 50-year career.

In 2016, Wiseman received an Honorary Oscar for lifetime achievement from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Board of Governors for his “masterful and distinctive documentaries [that] examine the familiar and reveal the unexpected.”.

In a recent development, indieWire spoke with Wiseman in 2025 as Lincoln Center prepared a retrospective of all his early films as part of the 4K restoration effort. He spoke about the attention to detail in his editing and his examination of each institution and its layers, despite the enormous length of many of his films.

“The subjects I choose to make films about are complicated, and I think I have an obligation when I’ve been given permission to make a movie about a place to have the final film reflect the complexity of the institution and not just be some superficial, banal representation of the institution,” he said.

The full list of titles acquired by Janus for North American distribution is below:.

“Titicut Follies” (1967), “High School” (1968,) “Law and Order” (1969), “Hospital” (1970), “Basic Training” (1971), “Essene” (1972), “Juvenile Court” (1973), “Primate” (1974), “Welfare” (1975), “Meat” (1976), “Canal Zone” (1977), “Sinai Field Mission” (1978), “Manoeuvre” (1979), “Model” (1980), “The Store” (1983), “Deaf” (1986), “Blind” (1986), “Racetrack” (1985), “Adjustment & Work” (1986), “Multi-handicapped” (1986), “Missile” (1987), “Near Death” (1989), “Central Park” (1990), “Aspen” (1991), “Zoo” (1993), “High School II” (1994), “Ballet” (1995), “La Comédie-Française ou L’amour joué” (1996), “Public Housing” (1997), “Belfast, Maine” (1999), “Domestic Violence” (2001), “Domestic Violence 2” (2002), “The Last Letter” (2002), “State Legislature” (2007), “La Danse: The Paris Opera Ballet” (2009), “Boxing Gym” (2010), “Crazy Horse” (2011), “At Berkeley” (2013), “National Gallery” (2014), “In Jackson Heights” (2015), “Ex Libris: The Newly introduced York Public Library” (2017), “Monrovia, Indiana” (2018), “City Hall” (2020), “A Couple” (2022), and “Menus-Plaisirs, les Troisgros” (2023).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • One Netflix show’s deliberate pacing, smart avoidance of genre clichés, and intelligent, measured writing resulted in the streaming service canceling the series at the height of its popularity.
  • For every enjoyably silly, brainless hit, there is a smart, successful series like Netflix’s three-season time travel epic Dark, a sci-fi drama that was as intellectually challenging and cerebral as it was enjoyable and engaging.
  • Sadly, this often results in streaming services pulling the plug on these titles for fear that they don’t appeal to a big enough audience, regardless of how popular they may have been proven to be so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One Netflix show’s deliberate pacing, smart avoidance of genre clichés, and intelligent, measured writing resulted in the streaming service canceling the series at the height of its popularity. Plenty of very silly TV shows have become incredibly popular with viewers, thus reaffirming the common conception that the medium caters to the lowest common denominator. However, a lot of very smart TV shows have also disproved this idea.

For every enjoyably silly, brainless hit, there is a smart, successful series like Netflix’s three-season time travel epic Dark, a sci-fi drama that was as intellectually challenging and cerebral as it was enjoyable and engaging. Admittedly, the fact that the Yellowstone franchise and its sequels dominate streaming charts proves that escapist silliness is still as popular as ever, but there are plenty of other examples of smart indicates becoming mainstream hits.

Sadly, this often results in streaming services pulling the plug on these titles for fear that they don’t appeal to a big enough audience, regardless of how popular they may have been proven to be so far. This was the fate of the two-season psychological thriller Mindhunter, based on the non-fiction book Mindhunter: Inside the FBI's Elite Serial Crime Unit. Set during the inception of the FBI’s Behavioral Science Unit, Mindhunter follows Jonathan Groff’s rookie Holden Ford and Holt McCallany’s veteran Bill Tench as they interview serial killers.

At least, their serial killer interviews are the shocking promise that the show dangles in front of viewers to get them invested. With the reluctant assistance of Anna Torv’s psychologist Wendy Carr, Ford and Tench attempt to use interviews with notorious real-life serial killers like Edmund Kemper, Richard Speck, and Dennis Reader to establish a psychological profile of potential murderers.

There is a strange sense of inevitability to proceedings, since viewers knew from shows like Criminal Minds and movies like Silence of the Lambs that these efforts eventually pay off. However, like HBO’s similarly critically acclaimed Mare of Easttown, Mindhunter learns from the approach of True Detective and proves that the true appeal of a murder mystery isn’t always in the final reveal, but rather learning more about the detectives along the way.

It has been revealed that whether Ford, Tench, and Carr will foil a specific killer on time is less notable than Mindhunter’s broader concern about the science behind their work as a whole. Mindhunter calls into question the legitimacy of the FBI’s Behavioral Science Unit time and again, and the show is deliberately ambiguous about how much the group’s work is helping to make the world safer.

In a recent development, the result is a chilling masterpiece that can go toe to toe with True Detective season 1 or HBO’s recent DC hit Lanterns as a classic moody, morally ambiguous small-screen detective thriller. As such, it is almost inevitable that Netflix famously told executive producer David Fincher that Mindhunter was too slow and even wanted it to be "more like CSI.”.

When the streaming service suggested adding sequences where characters are running and using their guns, Fincher decided that pulling the plug on Mindhunter earlier was a smarter move than subjecting viewers to a dumbed-down take on the material. It was a choice that proved wise in the years since, as plenty of shows have attempted to replicate Mindhunter’s appeal, but few have succeeded.

The disastrous critical reception of shows like 2026’s soapy Patricia Cornwell adaptation Scarpetta proves that upping the drama and action quotient of a dark, somber psychological thriller can sometimes be a terrible idea, and this retroactively justifies Fincher’s choice. Mindhunter may only have released 19 episodes, but these outings are at least true to the creator’s plan for the Netflix thriller series.

It has been revealed that whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp customers: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

In a recent development, whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the enhancement becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

Recent findings suggest that this rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the tech giant announced four upcoming features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

Sadly, the Timo Tjahjanto-directed dark action comedy couldn’t replicate the box office success of Nobody, putting an end to speculations about further installments, for now.

According to recent reports, last year, Odenkirk continued his action streak with Normal, which he co-wrote with Kolstad. We follow Odenkirk as a world-weary lawman Ulysses, who accepts a temporary posting as interim sheriff in the snowbound, seemingly idyllic town of Normal, hoping for a quiet respite. However, those aims come to a rest when two bungling drifters attempt to rob the local bank, accidentally exposing a massive underground vault filled with illicit gold bullion. Ulysses soon discovers that the entire community, from the friendly mayor (Henry Winkler), local deputies, to ordinary neighbors — all are secretly on the payroll of the Japanese Yakuza. Cornered and exposed, the heavily armed townsfolk turn on their fresh sheriff, forcing Ulysses into a relentless, snow-soaked fight for survival.

The feature was a modest box office success, grossing roughly $6.1 million worldwide against an estimated $17 million. But since then, it has become a streaming favorite, appearing on various streaming charts. The 78% Rotten Tomatoes-rated feature has critics consenting that the feature thrives on “Bob Odenkirk's gruff yet playful presence and director Ben Wheatley's over-the-top carnage, delivering simple, ridiculous, and consistently entertaining thrills despite its familiar premise.” Now that love for the film has catapulted it to newly introduced heights, Normal has landed on HBO Max’s global top 10 list. Other titles on the list include The Batman, The End of Oak Street, The Hunger Games, and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Trek's 60th anniversary has been an incredible celebration of one of the most influential science fiction franchises of all time. From exciting new collectibles and original stories to the return of iconic characters from across six decades of Trek history, fans have been spoiled for choice throughout 2026.

Industry observers note that arguably one of the biggest highlights of the anniversary celebrations has been Star Trek's crossover with Magic: The Gathering, which brings together two massive fandoms and gives Trekkies an entirely new way to experience their favorite sci-fi universe. However, the celebrations are far from over, and Star Trek fans looking to expand their collections even further have another exciting release to look forward to before the end of November.

It has been revealed that star Trek's 60th anniversary celebrations are continuing this November with an officially licensed collection of Magic: The Gathering accessories from Sirius Dice. According to the official press release, the collection is scheduled to launch this month to coincide with the franchise's milestone anniversary and the release of its highly anticipated Universes Beyond crossover.

In a recent development, among the most exciting additions to the collection are the Star Trek Mini Dice Cups, which retail for $19.99 each and feature a range of iconic factions from across Star Trek history. Each individually packaged cup comes with two Magic: The Gathering counter dice, with randomized designs that incorporate various color schemes and metallic finishes.

There are ten different designs available in the Mini Dice Cup collection:.

Industry observers note that the Q design is particularly noteworthy, as it's the collection's rare chase variant. Much like opening a Collector Booster pack in Magic: The Gathering, fans won't know exactly which design they've purchased until they open the packaging, adding another layer of collectibility to the release.

In a recent development, the Mini Dice Cups are just one part of Sirius Dice's larger Star Trek collection, however. The firm is also releasing $7.99 Treasure Packs, which contain one of 25 collectible 25mm Spindown Life Counters alongside a Magic: The Gathering token accessory. The dice themselves come in three different rarity categories: common, rare, and legendary.

Recent findings suggest that for fans looking for something a little more extravagant, Sirius Dice is also releasing two oversized 55mm Spindown Life Counters featuring miniature replicas of the U.S.S. Enterprise and a Klingon Bird-of-Prey encased in transparent resin. Both designs retail for $54.99 apiece and could easily double as standalone display pieces.

While the collection is clearly geared toward Magic: The Gathering players, there's plenty here for longtime Trekkies who simply enjoy collecting memorabilia. With the holiday season right around the corner and Star Trek's 60th anniversary year drawing to a close, the latest Sirius Dice collection is another great opportunity for fans to commemorate six decades of the iconic science fiction franchise.

In a recent development, the DeWalt 20-volt MAX 4.5” paddle switch angle grinder is on sale for $209, 47% off its typical price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a 4-amp-hour battery. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's easy for shows on Netflix to get lost in the shuffle sometimes, with the streamer releasing so many on a regular basis that it can be tough to keep track of the good ones. Fortunately, the cream rises to the top, and the best shows will find a way to either break through or leave a legacy. One of those shows gets brought up a lot around the fall and holiday times, and folks continue to revisit it on a regular basis — even though it's a completely heartbreaking watch.

Lost Ollie, released back in 2022, is a four-episode limited series that follows a stuffed toy on a journey to find the little boy who lost him. It's a live-action/animation hybrid that has a lot in common with Disney's Toy Story franchise, except that it gets a lot more intense with the emotions and will likely make you cry even more than you did at Buzz and Woody holding hands in a garbage furnace. If you need a good cry, or just want to watch some of the most beautiful storytelling you've ever seen on Netflix, Lost Ollie is a quick little watch that will certainly check off both boxes.

Recent findings suggest that while it plays with some substantial ideas, Lost Ollie is able to pack a ton into a very short amount of time. The series is just four episodes long, with each of them running between 41 and 51 minutes. When it's all remarked and done, Lost Ollie takes about three hours to watch, which is about the same as a pretty long movie. But the series makes great use of its episodic format, leaving plenty of opportunity to take a break or have some conversations about the deeper aspects of the story (if you're watching with younger family members).

Sources indicate that from top to bottom, everything about Lost Ollie feels like a home run. It's a funny and adventurous story that also brings in significant swells of emotion throughout, giving viewers a plethora of emotional experiences. It's also got some of the most fantastic CG animation we've ever seen on any form of television. Ollie and the other toys in the show are put into a live-action format, and they don't come off as wonky or even all that computer generated. They look about as close to real walking and talking toys as you'll see on the screen. Combined with some masterful cinematography and a lot of great production design, it's hard to look away from everything Lost Ollie has going on.

When you look at the credits for Lost Ollie, it's easy to see how it turned into something so magnificent. The series is based on a children's book by William Joyce, who was a concept artist on the original Toy Story and creator of the series Rolie Polie Olie. Some of his other books were adapted into animated features like Meet the Robinsons and Robots. Shannon Trindle, who previously worked on Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends, created the series for television, while Oscar-winning Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse director Peter Ramsey helmed all four episodes.

As if the creative team wasn't interesting enough, they put together a stellar cast that really takes Lost Ollie to the next level. Latest Girl's Jake Johnson and Jane the Virgin star Gina Rodriguez star as the parents of Billy, the main character played by Kesler Talbot. The titular Ollie is voiced by Tony winner and Frozen star Jonathan Groff, with Tim Blake Nelson and Mary J. Blige also lending their voices to the other main toys in the movie.

Industry observers note that lost Ollie is what happens when a lot of immensely talented people get the opportunity to pour everything they can into a collaborative project, and it's a series that a lot of families have revisited on more than one occasion. Sure, it's going to make you cry, but it's also going to make you smile an awful lot.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • In a recent development, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first announced. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

In a recent development, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

According to recent reports, the simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you said) to your “Notes to self” note.

Recent findings suggest that to take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

All the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

In a recent development, it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

There’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can plan them better next time.

Industry observers note that you’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

According to recent reports, but this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I noted it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

In a recent development, the Legend of Vox Machina will end on its own terms, with the high fantasy series coming to an end with its upcoming fifth season, and all four seasons and 48 episodes released thus far have been impeccable. On Rotten Tomatoes, the Prime Video fantasy series stands at a rare perfect 100% critics' score for all of its four seasons released thus far, proving just how consistent the show is on a high level. Additionally, viewers also share that opinion, as the hit show boasts a near-perfect 93% overall audience score. These positive reviews can be explained by a few key factors.

Given how another hit TV-MA Prime Video animated series, the superhero show Invincible, is frequently criticized for its cheap-looking animation, the fact that The Legend of Vox Machina has managed to be as consistent as it has with the way it looks is impressive. Those are enhanced by different classes of characters, including a cleric, a bard, a druid, a gunslinger, and more. The fact that The Legend of Vox Machina brings all these characters of completely different backgrounds and skill sets together is not only perfect for creating elaborate, visually appealing, and impactful battles, but also in making sure that the show feels fresh, with a plurality of voices that both creates tension and unique moments of connection between completely different people. Additionally, the adult animated series has a healthy dose of humor, but it is never used out of place.

As major movies and TV reveals, such as Marvel's Thor: Love and Thunder, have shown, striking a seamless balance between serious and comedic is not that easy a task, yet The Legend of Vox Machina always seems to know when to go more somber and when to let Scanlan run his mouth. Finally, this Dungeons & Dragons series comes with extensive source material, as Critical Role's first campaign spanned a mighty 115 episodes, so the show has many nuanced, exciting, and popular stories to pick from, adapting major arcs with dragons, vampires, and more. The Legend of Vox Machina belongs in the S-Tier of fantasy series.

The update includes multiple latest features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 ….

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone customers sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

It has been revealed that the redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final patch.

In a recent development, the redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-newly introduced design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 people, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with newly introduced clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The upgrade also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many fresh capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these latest capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so owners can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

In a recent development, with iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test latest ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to latest languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ proposal, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a latest vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 also adds a fresh Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

Sources indicate that for Apple Music customers, iOS 27.3 adds a fresh “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The patch also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a newly introduced “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Latest Update: 8 Sci-Fi Miniseries That Are Bangers From Start to Finish

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1417 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Feel free to connect with him or check out his work.
  • According to recent reports, sci-fi shows have a habit of getting carried away with their own ideas.
  • Recent findings suggest that fortunately, some miniseries understand that distinction better than others.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork, YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Collider, LinkedIn, Instagram.

According to recent reports, sci-fi shows have a habit of getting carried away with their own ideas. Give a series time travel, alien civilizations, or a machine that can predict the future, and suddenly every conversation becomes an excuse to explain how the technology works. The characters get buried under complicated theories, and by the time the story becomes interesting, it’s hard to care who survives. That’s a shame, because the best science fiction has always been about people, not the impossible things happening around them.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, some miniseries understand that distinction better than others. They use their wildest concepts to tell surprisingly personal stories about grief, love, family, and the choices people make when their world stops making sense. And because these stories have a beginning and an actual ending, every episode has a reason to exist. Here are 8 sci-fi miniseries that are bangers from start to finish.

Recent findings suggest that childhood’s End opens with ships appearing above the world’s major cities. Karellen (Charles Dance) promises an end to war through Ricky Stormgren (Mike Vogel), the farmer chosen to meet him. He keeps his face hidden, so Ricky’s private conversations with the Overlord leave him with questions humanity cannot put directly to its newly introduced ruler.

In a recent development, then the story jumps forward. Jake (Ashley Zukerman) and Amy Morrel (Hayley Magnus) watch their children develop abilities they cannot explain. Their world has peace and abundance, but they cannot raise their children into adulthood or share what the children are becoming. That shift, from a farmer asking one alien for answers to parents who have no one to ask, is why this show hurts. And that ending? Man, it really knows how to make a perfect world feel like the worst possible nightmare.

In a recent development, A key opens any door into the same motel room. A comb can stop time, and a bus ticket sends its holder elsewhere. That's the kind of bizarre mystery The Lost Room throws you into, and somehow, it only gets stranger. Detective Joe Miller (Peter Krause) finds these objects after a murder investigation leads him to Room 10 at the abandoned Sunshine Motel. Then his daughter Anna (Elle Fanning) disappears inside the room.

In a recent development, other people want the key because it gives them control over every door. But, Joe wants it because Anna is gone. His search takes him through the private rules and rival groups that have formed around the objects, but the strange powers never matter as much as a father checking another empty room. And that's what makes this whole thing so gripping. Joe has no time to fall apart while he tries the next key, the next clue, the next door. For all its mysteries, the series comes down to one painfully simple thing. A father just wants his daughter back.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners follows Gloria (Gloria Garayua), who takes extra emergency shifts to keep David (Zach Aguilar) at Arasaka Academy. After an ambulance crash kills her, he finds the military Sandevistan among the cyberware she stole from bodies at work. He installs it in his spine and uses it against the classmates who torment him.

Industry observers note that lucy (Emi Lo) indicates him a braindance of the moon. She wants to go there for real, and David makes getting her there his goal. Maine (William C. Stephens) loses control, David adds more implants, and Lucy begs him to stop. Each dose of immunosuppressants helps him keep using the Sandevistan, but it cannot protect him forever. And here's what makes Cyberpunk: Edgerunners so damn heartbreaking. Lucy actually makes it to the moon, just like she always wanted. But David isn't there, and suddenly, getting everything she dreamed of doesn't feel like much of a victory.

Can a three-day pill trial help with heartbreak? Maniac takes that ridiculous question surprisingly seriously, which is pretty impressive for a show where two strangers keep waking up in increasingly bizarre versions of reality. Annie (Emma Stone) joins hoping to revisit the last car ride with her sister Ellie (Julia Garner), while Owen (Jonah Hill), recently fired, is pressured by his family to deny his schizophrenia diagnosis. At Neberdine, the pills send them into staged roles as thieves, spies, and strangers who keep meeting.

Their waking selves barely speak, while the drug scenarios repeatedly place them together. Annie relives her argument with Ellie before the crash, while Owen tries to work out whether his brother’s legal trouble is real or part of his illness. Annie and Owen make each fantasy funny enough to enjoy, then seem visibly drained when the pills wear off. When Annie decides Owen should not be left alone, it feels earned because she knows what it is to be dismissed while trying to explain that she is in pain.

Russell Keys (Steve Burton) returns from a World War II mission with missing time and nightmares nobody believes. Meanwhile, Owen Crawford (Joel Gretsch) sees the Roswell crash as a career opportunity and helps bury what happened. Sally Clarke (Catherine Dent) meets an alien while trapped in an unhappy marriage, then raises a daughter whose origins she cannot explain.

Recent findings suggest that back home, Russell’s wife and son live with his fear, while Owen’s choices cost him his family’s trust. Sally protects Allie (Dakota Fanning) from adults who see her as evidence. Taken follows their families for five decades, with children and grandchildren growing up around secrets their parents will not explain. And that's the crazy thing about this show. You've got aliens, government cover-ups, and decades of mystery, yet the people doing the most damage to these families are often the ones sitting right across the dinner table.

In a recent development, in 11.22.63 a diner’s back room gives Jake Epping (James Franco) one rule. Walk through the door and arrive in 1960, then return to the present and the past resets. He is there to stop Kennedy’s assassination. In Jodie, Texas, he meets Sadie (Sarah Gadon), a school librarian who notices how often his phrases sound wrong for the year.

While Jake is tracking Oswald (Daniel Webber), he and Sadie have built a life together. He keeps November 22 in mind and withholds what he is risking, and every decision protects the mission at her expense. After the timeline resets, Jake finds the elderly Sadie at a dance. She does not recognize him. He asks for one dance without telling her that he was the man she loved.

Station Eleven opens with Arthur Leander (Gael García Bernal) collapsing onstage while playing King Lear. In the audience, Jeevan (Himesh Patel) tries to help. Kirsten (Matilda Lawler), an eight-year-old actor, watches. Later that night she asks Jeevan to take her home. Then the flu spreads, and the two are stuck trying to make a safe life in an apartment with Jeevan’s brother Frank (Nabhaan Rizwan).

Twenty years later, Kirsten (Mackenzie Davis) is with the Traveling Symphony, performing Shakespeare for communities that have survived. She still carries the Station Eleven comic Arthur gave her, with drawings and lines she knows by heart. The airport story gives Clark (David Wilmot) a different emergency of keeping strangers fed, calm, and willing to live together. The series shifts focus among survivors’ losses. When Kirsten and Jeevan find each other again, the relief hits before either of them speaks.

Industry observers note that in Devs, Sergei (Karl Glusman) gets one day inside a secretive development division. Lily (Sonoya Mizuno) knows he wouldn’t simply leave, but Forest (Nick Offerman) and security chief Kenton (Zach Grenier) have already settled on the explanation she is supposed to accept. She looks for answers inside Amaya’s sealed development building, where a quantum computer reconstructs events in unnerving detail.

Sources indicate that forest lost his daughter Amaya and built a system that lets him watch versions of her again. He insists the universe has only one possible course, but Lily refuses his account of Sergei’s death. One man wants proof that the daughter he lost still exists somewhere, while one woman wants the truth about the person she loved. And the really unsettling part is that Forest has a machine capable of looking into the past, yet Lily still has to fight just to get a straight answer about what happened to Sergei.
