📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The best all-in-one printer should make everyday jobs simpler, whether you're printing shipping labels, scanning vital paperwork, copying forms or producing color photos at home.
  • Industry observers note that our tested picks cover each of those needs, from the Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II being a capable all-rounder for most households to low-cost options like the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW.
  • At Tom's Guide, we test each printer for printing speeds, print quality, ink costs and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The best all-in-one printer should make everyday jobs simpler, whether you're printing shipping labels, scanning vital paperwork, copying forms or producing color photos at home. The right choice depends on what you print and how often: some models prioritise rapid document handling, while others keep ink costs down or deliver stronger photo output.

Industry observers note that our tested picks cover each of those needs, from the Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II being a capable all-rounder for most households to low-cost options like the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW. There's even the Inkwon Tag, a compact creative printer for stickers and creating custom T-shirts.

At Tom's Guide, we test each printer for printing speeds, print quality, ink costs and more. Read on to find the model that best matches your workload, budget and must-have features, including scanning, copying and faxing.

In a recent development, printers might not be the most impressive (or interesting) things in the world, but they are supremely useful. To make sure you get the best printer possible, our dedicated reviews team put printers through their paces. That's going to be Nikita Achanta, on the Tom's Guide side, who's been testing consumer electronics for years. Then there are our freelancers, such as Eric Butterfield, who's tested a range of brands.

These are the tests that we put the printers through so that we can properly evaluate their performance.

Industry observers note that with the amount of shipping labels I need printed and documents that need copying for my household, a printer has become a quiet essential for my home. That's why I wanted a simple, do-it-all machine, and I refer to our experts, Nikita Achanta and Eric Butterfield, for all the in-depth recommendations they have to offer.

According to recent reports, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

In a recent development, when it comes down to it, the Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is quite simply the only printer you'll ever need. Yes, it can print, scan, copy and fax, but it does it all with a hassle-free setup experience and rapid speeds across the board. When a printer actually gives easy step-by-step instructions on how to fix a paper jam, you know it's a good one.

In our tests, it delivered a five-page text print job in just 11.31 seconds (26.5 pages per minute) and scanned in color in 6.22 seconds, and that's faster than its inkjet competitors.

And this 250-capacity printer (plus an extra 150 prints in the middle section) has quick start-up, too, as our reviewer, Nikita, found it effortless to get up and running, with warm-up times as quick as 14 seconds from off.

Sources indicate that it isn't just speed, as print quality is consistently sharp and detailed, both in color and black and white, and everyday jobs came out looking just as sharp as they did on our screens. Where the MF753Cdw II pulls ahead of inkjet competitors like the more budget-friendly Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is in raw speed and features.

Sources indicate that you get much faster printing and a true all-in-one experience (there's no faxing on the G3290), but running costs are higher if you print in volume. Against the business-class Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850, the MF753Cdw II still keeps up on print speed and quality but can’t match those rock-bottom ink costs.

Sources indicate that that’s the main compromise here: the per-page price is higher than what you’ll find with most ink tank printers (around 5.1 cents per color page and 2.7 cents per mono print). But not by that much, and that shouldn't put you off grabbing this workhorse.

If you want a dependable, fuss-free machine for everyday tasks — letters, homework, invoices, you name it — the MF753Cdw II is the best fit for most households.

Recent findings suggest that unless you need faxing in your life, this is the all-in-one printer to grab if you're after a reliable machine for excellent prints. The Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW stands out largely thanks to its exceptionally low ink costs: just 0.3 cents per black page and 0.94 cents per color page based on our lab testing. That's value you can't ignore.

In daily use, the T780DW keeps pace with demanding routines. It prints standard text documents at 12.4 pages per minute (ppm) and handles double-sided text at 6.7 ppm. These speeds put it among the fastest inkjets we've tested for both single and duplex jobs, making it reliable for everything from schoolwork to business invoices.

Print and scan quality are equally reassuring. In our hands-on tests, text and graphics came out crisp and accurate, while color scans preserved detail and clarity.

The main compromise is its 20-sheet automatic document feeder. While fine for light multi-page copying and scanning, if you've got a large batch of documents, it will take some time to do. That, and there's no USB thumb drive port, and don't expect to make double-sided copies or scans via the automatic document feeder (ADF).

In any case, for those who want low running costs and easy printing, the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW will fit in nicely with your home or office.

Whether you're a photographer or just need highly detailed, colorful prints, the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is the all-in-one printer for you. Sure, it may come with fewer additional features, but it excels where it matters: print quality and affordability.

In a recent development, it's a modest printer; it has just one paper tray and no document feeder, and it's not the speediest option. But for home use, it's an excellent choice. Expect this to deliver reliable, high-quality prints with the versatility to do documents, photos and double-sided print jobs. Speaking of which, those graphic prints and glossy photos will come out with plenty of detail and natural, accurate colors.

Sources indicate that while the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 prints at pretty average speeds, it actually excels at double-sided documents. In our testing, it printed single-sided pages at an average of 9.2 pages per minute, but double-sided text documents cranked up to 7.2 pages per minute, the fastest duplex print speed we've recorded of any recent ink tank printers.

And thanks to its easy setup process, robust wireless support (this thing can print via Wi-Fi or a smartphone app) and low ink costs (we estimate color prints cost roughly 0.9 cents per page, significantly lower than the 1.9 cents per page category average), I recommend the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 for anyone seeking an affordable, reliable ink all-in-one printer, especially for photo printing.

If your at-home office needs fast, reliable color printing day in and day out, the Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850 is just the printer you'll want. In our tests, it handled a six-page mixed color document in just 1 minute and 8 seconds (5.3 pages per minute), nearly doubling the category average, so you won’t be waiting on big print jobs during busy stretches.Where the ET-5850 really stands out for speedy work prints is its speed with graphics-heavy jobs. Letter-size glossy photos print in 2 minutes and 21 seconds, far outpacing typical inkjets. The three separate paper input trays mean you can keep letter, legal, and specialty papers ready to go, which helps minimize interruptions if multiple people are printing different document types.

It has been revealed that moreover, you're getting an impressively low ink costs with a device capable of handling more than 3,000 pages per month. During our testing, we found an extremely low per-page cost of 0.4 cents for text pages, and 1.6 cents per color page. The printer can scan, copy and fax, uses dual 250-page paper cassettes and has a 50-sheet automatic document feeder.

Industry observers note that setup was mostly straightforward, but we did run into some hiccups. Connecting to our network required manually entering a router password (WPS isn’t supported), and the touchscreen flagged network challenges before resolving. Once added, using the printer with a Mac was simple, but it’s worth noting you might spend extra time on initial setup and troubleshooting.If you’re after an all-in-one that keeps pace with high-volume, graphics-rich business tasks and want flexible paper handling, the ET-5850 is a great fit.

It has been revealed that alright, this one's a little different from any other all-in-one printer, as the Inkwon Tag is a one-of-a-kind portable color inkjet printer. Instead of printing, scanning or copying documents, this pocketable printer delivers all the fun stuff — instant photo prints for scrapbooks, heat transfers for creating custom T-shirts, temporary tattoos and even stickers.

This 4-in-1 portable printer is as tiny as it is light, coming in at 4.1 x 3.8 x 1.7 inches and weighing just 8.2 ounces. Our reviewer, Nikita, has no problems carrying this around in a pocket, as it's actually smaller than the best big phones around today.

According to recent reports, despite its size, you'll find it boasts surprisingly good print quality, no matter the image. It uses a CMY three-dye-based ink system (no dedicated black ink, though) with a resolution of 600 dpi, making it excellent for small prints of friends and loved ones, designs of your choosing or even screenshots from games. And it's all extremely easy to use, right from setting it up to the very user-friendly app for editing and printing photos.

It isn't perfect, as it can only handle one sheet of paper at a time, and don't expect it to create any borderless prints. It's also quite a pricey portable printer, coming in at $299, but its ink costs and paper refills are much more value-friendly when compared to its competition, especially from Canon or Instax (plus, those brands don't offer 4-in-1 portable printer options with sticker or heat transfer capabilities).

Industry observers note that to have a mini, portable printer by your side to instantly create stickers to personalize whatever you want, temporary tattoos for parties, heat transfers for customized T-shirts and Polaroid-like photos, all at low running ink costs? As far as portable all-in-one printers go, the Inkwon Tag is a winner.

Sources indicate that if you're looking for a compact, capable printer purely for stickers and photo prints, then the StickerPix Print + Cut is exactly what you're after. It comes in an adorable design, is fast at printing stickers and offers loads of templates to customize what you want to print. There are only 18 sheets of sticker/photo paper out of the box, so you'll need to invest in more, and the Inkwon Tag offers a bit more "all-in-one" versatility, but the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut is well worth grabbing for all things stickers! Read our full Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut review.

(★★★★☆)The Brother INKvestment MFC-J995DW bucked the trend of printers gouging you on ink costs by coming with roughly a year's worth of ink (depending on how much you print) pre-loaded in the extra-large ink cartridges, so you get a great price-per-page right out of the gate. On top of that, the Brother INKvestment MFC-J995DW offers solid printing, scanning and copying. But this model is trickier to find these days, and more of the current Brother printers of its kind do just the job for less these days. Read our full Brother INKvestment MFC-J995DW review.

Industry observers note that (★★★★☆½)The Brother MFC-L2750DW XL is the best multifunction laser printer we've reviewed in years for everything but color prints. Every print is sharp and clean, and it's packed with features including a quick ADF, fast duplex printing and copying, fax capability, and a second paper tray. But this is one pricey machine!Read our full Brother MFC-L2750DW XL review.

According to recent reports, (★★★★☆)Looking for another photo printer option? The Canon Pixma TR8620 is a fantastic shout that offers plenty of office features, from scanning and faxing to a 20-page ADF, a duplexer for two-sided printing, and two paper trays for keeping two types of paper at the ready. But that extra ink cartridge does bump up the cost of ink. Read our full Canon Pixma TR8620 review.

Sources indicate that to help you find the best all-in-one printer, we put each model through an extensive range of printer tests, including timed prints of text, mixed text and graphics and color photos. The resulting prints are carefully examined for errors and challenges, and compared with samples from other printers to determine the print quality.

We time every test print to see how swiftly the machine handles document printing, and closely examine the finished product to determine how well different printing tasks are handled.

We also test the scanning and copying functions of the printer, timing how quickly it captures a page and comparing the results to the original images to determine how well it captures color and detail.

To measure the cost of owning and operating a printer, we look at the current street price of ink refills and the estimated number of pages that each cartridge can produce, and calculate the cost of printing a single page.

Not sure which all-in-one printer to buy? Obviously, you want a printer that performs well, so all of our reviews and rankings discuss a printer's output quality and speed, but there's more to an all-in-one printer than just how quickly it can crank out documents.

Industry observers note that some companies even offer subscription services that save you money while sending you ink just in time to replace that empty cartridge. Learn more in our article HP Instant Ink vs. Canon vs. Epson: Are ink subscriptions worth it?

Ink-tank printers, a type of Inkjet, usually offer the lowest running costs because their refill bottles deliver far more pages than conventional cartridges.

In our guide, the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW is the best-value option for home or light-office use, while the Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850 pairs very low per-page costs with the capacity and features needed for heavier business printing.

You should compare current cost-per-page figures with your expected print volume, not just the printer’s upfront price.

Choose an inkjet if you print color graphics or photos, want a lower upfront price or value the low ongoing costs of an ink-tank model. Choose a laser all-in-one if your priority is fast, sharp text documents and a responsive office workflow.

The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is our top pick, as it's a fast laser workhorse, whereas the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is the stronger fit for photo printing.

An automatic document feeder (ADF) is worthwhile if you regularly scan, copy or fax multi-page documents, as it feeds the sheets for you instead of requiring one page at a time on the scanner glass.

It has been revealed that it matters less for occasional household printing or photo-focused use. Also check its capacity and whether it supports double-sided scanning: an ADF does not automatically mean both sides can be scanned in one pass.

Some can, but not every all-in-one printer with an ADF supports automatic double-sided scanning or copying. Do not confuse duplex printing with duplex scanning: a printer may print on both sides of a sheet while still requiring you to turn over originals when scanning or copying.

Check the model’s specifications before buying; the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW has an ADF but does not support duplex scanning or copying through it.

It has been revealed that many current all-in-one printers support wireless mobile printing through a manufacturer app, Apple AirPrint or another built-in service. The Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290, for example, supports Wi-Fi and printing through a smartphone app.

Before buying, confirm that the printer works with your phone or tablet, operating system, preferred app and network setup. Some features may require the device and printer to be on the same Wi-Fi network.

Industry observers note that amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

Industry observers note that if Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Signal’s latest app revision on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.
  • As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t presently provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a latest upgrade that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats. Here are the details.

Signal’s latest app revision on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t presently provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.

By default, consumers who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that notes: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

In a recent development, fortunately, there’s an easy workaround. Users who want to re-enable screenshots can do so by visiting Signal’s privacy settings and turning off the new toggle that’s labeled ‘Block Siri AI.’.

Here’s 9to5Mac’s own Arin Waichulis:.

Signal now blocks in-app screenshots on iPhone to keep Siri AI from reading chatsIt’s a newly introduced toggle in settings that’s on by default, but can be turned offNo equivalent for its Mac app pic.twitter.com/ImsinqMNPq.

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:.

Prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

Recent findings suggest that it’s good to see that users can manually disable the newly introduced privacy setting if they want. But Signal’s decision to block screenshots does raise key questions about the potential gap in privacy tools for iOS developers.

In a recent development, apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing customers to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this patch.

What do you think of Signal’s latest move? Let us know in the comments.

This 65-Inch Samsung Mini-LED TV Is $200 Off Ahead of Black Friday

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that early Black Friday deals are popping up everywhere from Amazon to Costco.
  • While it’s considered an entry-level 4K smart TV, the M80H is packed with Samsung Vision AI features, and like the rest of the brand’s TVs, it runs on the Tizen interface.
  • Recent findings suggest that it has AirPlay support and built-in Alexa, but lacks local dimming and may struggle in very bright, sunlit rooms, so keep that in mind if you do a lot of daytime viewing.

Sources indicate that early Black Friday deals are popping up everywhere from Amazon to Costco. For those looking to upgrade an old but smaller TV to a newer model without splurging on an OLED, the 65-inch Samsung M80H Mini-LED TV is 29% off and down to a record-low $497.99 (originally $697.99). If you want to downsize (or go massive), the 55-inch, 75-inch, and 85-inch models are also discounted ahead of the holiday.

While it’s considered an entry-level 4K smart TV, the M80H is packed with Samsung Vision AI features, and like the rest of the brand’s TVs, it runs on the Tizen interface. A high 144Hz refresh rate, as well as VRR and  AMD FreeSync Premium, makes it a decent choice for gamers compared to the standard 60Hz of cheaper models.

Recent findings suggest that it has AirPlay support and built-in Alexa, but lacks local dimming and may struggle in very bright, sunlit rooms, so keep that in mind if you do a lot of daytime viewing. That said, Filmmaker Mode delivers reliable color accuracy for standard dynamic range (SDR) content out of the box. At under $500, the 65-inch Samsung M80H Mini-LED TV is a solid option if you want a significant screen and a high refresh rate on a budget.
